definition_zh: 望远镜；可套叠的筒状物；使套叠收缩；压缩（时间或过程）
definition_en: an instrument that gathers light or other waves and makes a distant object look larger and nearer
core_image: 山顶一支黄铜长筒对准海面，雾散之后，远处的帆船被拉到眼前
scene: 山顶观测台上，一支长筒对准海湾尽头的帆船，雾散时船影忽然被拉到眼前。A brass telescope on the ridge brought the distant sailboat close enough to read its flag.
sceneCN: 这里 telescope 指「借透镜或反射镜把远处物像放大拉近的光学仪器」（第 1 个义项：用来观察远处物体的光学装置）；句意为山脊上的黄铜望远镜把远处的帆船拉到能看清船旗的距离。可辨识物件：三脚架、长镜筒、目镜、海面帆船。

senses.title: An instrument for distant objects
senses.titleCN: 把远处物像放大的光学仪器
senses.definition: an instrument that collects light from a distant object and makes it appear larger and nearer
senses.definitionCN: 收集远处物体发出的光，使其看起来更大、更近的装置
senses.example: A brass telescope on the ridge brought the distant sailboat close enough to read its flag.
senses.exampleCN: 山脊上的黄铜望远镜把远处的帆船拉到能看清船旗的距离。
senses.why: Greek tele meant far and skopein meant to look, so the name says plainly a far-looker.
senses.whyCN: 希腊 tele 意为「远方」，skopein 意为「看」，名称字面就是「看远处之物」。

senses.title: A dish that gathers radio waves
senses.titleCN: 射电望远镜：收集无线电波的巨盘或阵列
senses.definition: a telescope that collects radio waves rather than visible light, usually with a large dish or a group of dishes
senses.definitionCN: 收集无线电波而非可见光的望远镜，通常由大口径天线或天线阵列构成
senses.example: The radio telescope mapped clouds of hydrogen across the galaxy.
senses.exampleCN: 射电望远镜绘出了银河系中的氢云分布。
senses.why: the name stayed because the task stayed: something far away is still being resolved by gathered waves.
senses.whyCN: 名称保留下来，因为任务没有变：仍旧靠收集波来分辨远处之物。

senses.title: An instrument placed above the air
senses.titleCN: 空间望远镜：架在轨道上以避开大气
senses.definition: a telescope put into orbit so that the atmosphere no longer blurs or absorbs what it collects
senses.definitionCN: 送入轨道、使大气不再模糊或吸收观测信号的望远镜
senses.example: The space telescope resolved stars that ground instruments could not separate.
senses.exampleCN: 空间望远镜分辨出了地面仪器无法分开的恒星。
senses.why: placing the tube outside the air removes the medium that made the older instrument imperfect.
senses.whyCN: 把镜筒放到大气之外，就去掉了让旧式仪器失真的那层介质。

senses.title: A tube that slides into itself
senses.titleCN: 可套叠的镜筒或筒状物
senses.definition: a tube, or a set of tubes, that slide inside one another so that the whole can be shortened
senses.definitionCN: 由若干节套接而成、可逐节缩回以缩短整体的筒状物
senses.example: The brass telescope collapsed into three nested sections for the journey.
senses.exampleCN: 这支黄铜望远镜收成三节套筒，以便携带上路。
senses.why: early telescopes were drawn out and pushed back like a spyglass, so the object and its folding action took one name.
senses.whyCN: 早期望远镜像单筒镜那样拉出推进，于是器物与「叠缩」这个动作共用一个名字。

senses.title: To nest one part inside another
senses.titleCN: 使一节套进另一节而变短
senses.definition: to shorten an object by sliding its sections inside one another
senses.definitionCN: 让各节逐段滑入彼此内部，从而缩短某物
senses.example: They telescope the mast down before the boat passes under the bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 船过桥之前，他们把桅杆逐节缩下。
senses.why: the verb simply names the action that the sliding tube performs.
senses.whyCN: 动词义只是给套筒所做的那个动作起名。

senses.title: To press events into a short span
senses.titleCN: 压缩时间、过程或事件，使前后挤在一起
senses.definition: to make stages or events follow so closely that they seem to occupy a much shorter time
senses.definitionCN: 使各个阶段或事件紧密相接，仿佛只占很短一段时间
senses.example: The film telescopes ten years of work into a single montage.
senses.exampleCN: 这部影片把十年的工作压缩进一段蒙太奇。
senses.why: the picture of sections sliding into each other becomes a way of saying that separate periods are pushed together.
senses.whyCN: 「各节滑入彼此」的画面，被用来表示原本分开的时段被推到一处。

senses.title: A sight mounted on a weapon
senses.titleCN: 枪械上的瞄准镜
senses.definition: a short telescope fitted to a rifle or other weapon so that a distant target can be aimed at
senses.definitionCN: 装在步枪等武器上，用来瞄准远处目标的短筒光学装置
senses.example: He adjusted the telescope before taking the long shot.
senses.exampleCN: 在打这一记远射之前，他先调好了瞄准镜。
senses.why: a sight does exactly what the instrument does: it brings a far target close to the eye.
senses.whyCN: 瞄准镜做的事与望远镜完全相同：把远处目标拉到眼前。

senses.title: To bring distant things near in thought
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：把遥远之事拉到可理解的距离
senses.definition: to make something distant in time or in understanding feel close and graspable
senses.definitionCN: 使在时间上遥远或在理解上隔膜的事物显得贴近、可以把握
senses.example: The diary telescopes a vanished village into a few vivid rooms.
senses.exampleCN: 这本日记把一个消失的村庄压缩进几间鲜活的屋子。
senses.why: the abstract sense drops the glass entirely: what is shortened is the distance between reader and thing.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义完全去掉了镜片：被缩短的是读者与所述之物之间的距离。

intro.en: Telescope is a modern scientific coinage: Greek tele far plus skopein to look, Latinized as telescopium in 1611. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: telescope 是近代科学新造词：希腊 tele「远方」加 skopein「看」，1611 年拉丁化为 telescopium。年代均为约数。

items.en: Tele was an adverb of place meaning far off; English uses it only as the prefix tele-, as in telephone and television.
items.cn: tele 是表示「在远处」的地点副词；英语只把它用作前缀 tele-，如 telephone 与 television。

items.en: Skopein meant to look at or examine. The related noun skopos meant watcher or target, and English scope comes from it.
items.cn: skopein 意为「看、察看」。相关名词 skopos 指「观看者、目标」，英语 scope 即由此而来。

items.en: Members of the Accademia dei Lincei Latinized the new instrument as telescopium, and the English form telescope followed in the same century.
items.cn: 猞猁学社的成员把这种新仪器拉丁化为 telescopium，英语形式 telescope 在同一世纪随之出现。

items.en: Galileo himself wrote perspicillum, literally looking-glass, so the Greek-Latin name competed with a plainer Latin one before it won.
items.cn: 伽利略本人写作 perspicillum，字面是「看之镜」，因此这个希腊-拉丁新名曾与一个更朴素的拉丁名并存，后来才胜出。

items.en: Microscope, periscope, spectroscope and endoscope are all built from skopein with a different first element naming what is looked at or through.
items.cn: microscope、periscope、spectroscope 与 endoscope 都由 skopein 构成，只是第一个成分各自指明看什么或透过什么看。

items.en: Source uncertain (attribution and deeper origin): the 1611 naming is generally credited to the Lincean circle around Cesi, but which member first said it is disputed, and the pre-Greek origin of skopein is unsettled, so any Indo-European form offered for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（命名归属与更深词源）：1611 年的定名一般认为是切西周围猞猁学社圈子的功劳，但究竟哪位成员最先说出此词仍有争议；skopein 在希腊语之前的来源亦无定论，凡为其给出的印欧形式均属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds instruments built from Greek skopein with a different first element; group two holds devices and places that do the same work without being a telescope.
note.cn: 第一组是同样由希腊 skopein 构成、但第一个成分不同的仪器；第二组是做同样的事却不叫望远镜的器具或场所。

entries.definition: Micro- means small plus skopein: the instrument looks at what is too small for the eye, not at what is too far.
entries.definitionCN: micro-「小」加 skopein：它看的是肉眼无法分辨的小东西，而不是远处之物。

entries.definition: Peri- means around plus skopein: a tube that lets a viewer see over or around an obstacle.
entries.definitionCN: peri-「环绕」加 skopein：用来越过或绕过障碍观察的镜筒。

entries.definition: Its first element is spectrum, so it separates light into wavelengths instead of enlarging a distant scene.
entries.definitionCN: 第一个成分是 spectrum，因此它把光按波长分开，而不是放大远处景象。

entries.definition: Endon means within plus skopein: a tube for looking inside a body or a machine.
entries.definitionCN: endon「在内」加 skopein：用来观察人体或机器内部的管状器械。

entries.definition: A pair of short telescopes mounted side by side so that both eyes look at once.
entries.definitionCN: 两支短镜并排安装、可双眼同时观察的器具。

entries.definition: An older name for a small hand-held telescope, usually one that draws out in sections.
entries.definitionCN: 对手持小望远镜的旧称，通常是分节拉出的那种。

entries.definition: A curved piece of glass or plastic that bends light; a telescope contains lenses but is not one.
entries.definitionCN: 弯曲的玻璃或塑料片，用来使光偏折；望远镜含镜片，但镜片本身不是望远镜。

entries.definition: A building or site equipped for watching the sky; it houses telescopes without being one.
entries.definitionCN: 为观测天空而建的房屋或场所；它安放望远镜，本身却不是望远镜。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real compounds and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实的复合词与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: tele- means far and -scope means look, so telescope is a far-looker.
normal.cn: tele- 表示「远」，-scope 表示「看」，telescope 就是「看远处的东西」。

normal.en: The same -scope ending appears in microscope, periscope, endoscope and spectroscope.
normal.cn: 同样的 -scope 结尾出现在 microscope、periscope、endoscope 与 spectroscope 里。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the types: optical telescope, radio telescope, space telescope.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出类型：光学望远镜、射电望远镜、空间望远镜。

normal.en: The verb keeps the tube image: a mast telescopes down, a timetable is telescoped.
normal.cn: 动词义保留镜筒的形象：桅杆逐节缩下，时间表被压缩。

normal.en: The adjective is telescopic, as in a telescopic lens or a telescopic mast.
normal.cn: 形容词是 telescopic，如可伸缩镜头或套叠桅杆。

abstract.en: Picture a long brass tube that folds into three neat rings in your pocket.
abstract.cn: 想象一支长长的黄铜筒，折起来变成口袋里三只整齐的圆环。

abstract.en: Picture a century of history squeezed into one page so that two distant dates touch.
abstract.cn: 想象一个世纪的历史被压进一页纸，两个遥远的年份因此挨在一起。

abstract.en: Picture a dark sea where one bright tube turns a speck into a ship with a name.
abstract.cn: 想象一片黑海，一支明亮的筒把一个小点变成一只有名字的船。

examples.en: The Observatory lends a small telescope to every new member.
examples.cn: 天文台借给每位新成员一支小望远镜。

examples.en: A radio telescope can detect signals that no optical instrument would show.
examples.cn: 射电望远镜能探测到任何光学仪器都不会显示出的信号。

examples.en: The antenna mast telescopes to half its height when the wind rises.
examples.cn: 风起时，天线桅杆会缩到原来高度的一半。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「tele（远）+ scope（看）」——用来看远处的东西 → 望远镜；把一节节缩进另一节 → 套叠

root: 希腊 tele「远方」+ skopein「看、察看」，经新拉丁 telescopium（1611 年定名）；skopein 的希腊语之前来源不确定。英语 telescope。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one instrument: a tube that gathers waves from far away, then the tube that folds, then the folding applied to time, then the aim and finally the act of making distance disappear.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一件器物展开：先是可以收拢远处光线的镜筒，再是会套叠的镜筒，接着把套叠用于时间，然后用于瞄准，最后落在「让距离消失」这一动作上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a long tube on a ridge that pulls a far ship into reading distance.
core.cn: 核心意象：山脊上一支长筒，把远处的船拉到可以读清的距离。

branches.en: GATHERED WAVES: light or radio, the instrument still resolves what the eye alone cannot.
branches.cn: 收集波：无论是光还是无线电波，仪器仍在分辨肉眼无法分辨之物。

branches.en: OUTSIDE THE AIR: orbit removes the medium that blurred the older view.
branches.cn: 置于大气之外：轨道去掉了让旧式观测失真的介质。

branches.en: SLIDING TUBE: sections nest, so the object and its folding action share one name.
branches.cn: 套筒：各节嵌套，于是器物与叠缩动作共用一个名称。

branches.en: COMPRESSED TIME: periods are pushed into one another like tube sections.
branches.cn: 压缩时间：时段像镜筒各节一样被推进彼此之中。

branches.en: NEARNESS: a target or a meaning is brought within reach of the eye or the mind.
branches.cn: 拉近：目标或意义被带到眼睛或心智可以触及的范围。

intro.en: Telescope is made of two Greek morphemes that also build a whole family of viewing instruments, so the word can be read piece by piece.
intro.cn: telescope 由两个希腊语素构成，这两个语素还构成一整个观察仪器词族，因此可以逐块读出这个词。

latinIntro.en: There is no native Latin root here; the Latin forms are New Latin coinages and Galileo's own perspicillum. telescopium is the Latinized name of 1611.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有本族拉丁词根；拉丁形式是新拉丁新造词与伽利略自用的 perspicillum，其中 telescopium 是 1611 年的拉丁化名称。

items.example: The prefix marks distance, as in telephone and telegraph.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标出距离，如电话与电报。

items.example: The suffix names what kind of looking the instrument does.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀说明该器械做的是哪一种「看」。

items.example: A brass telescope on the ridge brought the sailboat close.
items.exampleCN: 山脊上的黄铜望远镜把帆船拉近了。

items.meaning: relating to a telescope; able to extend in sections
items.meaningCN: 望远镜的；可分段伸缩的
items.example: The rod has a telescopic joint.
items.exampleCN: 这根杆有一段可伸缩的接头。

items.example: The moons were first seen telescopically.
items.exampleCN: 这些卫星最早是通过望远镜看到的。

items.example: The telescoping of the mast saved space below deck.
items.exampleCN: 桅杆的套叠为甲板下节省了空间。

items.meaning: the barrel that holds the lenses
items.example: Dust had settled on the telescope tube.
items.exampleCN: 灰尘落在了望远镜镜筒上。

items.meaningCN: 接收无线电波的望远镜
items.example: The radio telescope mapped hydrogen clouds.
items.exampleCN: 射电望远镜绘出了氢云分布。

items.example: The space telescope resolved faint stars.
items.exampleCN: 空间望远镜分辨出了暗弱恒星。

latinEntries.structure: telescopium (New Latin, 1611, from Greek tele + skopein)
perspicillum, perspicilli (n., second declension; Latin looking-glass)
latinEntries.meaning: a lens or instrument for looking; the name Galileo used
latinEntries.meaningCN: 镜片或观察器械；伽利略使用的名称

definition_zh: 分光镜；把光分解成光谱以便观察和测量的仪器
definition_en: an instrument that splits light into its component wavelengths so that a spectrum can be seen and measured
core_image: 暗室里一道光穿过狭缝，被棱镜摊成彩色条带，落在带刻度的标尺上
scene: 暗室里，狭缝后的一束光被棱镜摊成彩色条带，落在带刻度的标尺上。A spectroscope split the beam into coloured bands that could be measured line by line.
sceneCN: 这里 spectroscope 指「把入射光分解成光谱以便观察和测量的仪器」（第 1 个义项：借棱镜或光栅分光并显示谱线的装置）；句意为分光镜把光束分成一条条可以逐线测量的彩色带。可辨识物件：狭缝、棱镜、标尺、暗箱。

pos.zh: 分光镜；光谱仪（以目视观察为主）

derivatives.zh: 光谱学家；光谱分析人员

senses.title: An instrument that spreads light into a spectrum
senses.titleCN: 把光分解成光谱的仪器
senses.definition: an instrument that disperses incoming light into its wavelengths and displays the resulting bands for direct viewing
senses.definitionCN: 把入射光按其波长分开，并直接显示所得条带的仪器
senses.example: A spectroscope split the beam into coloured bands that could be measured line by line.
senses.exampleCN: 分光镜把光束分成一条条可以逐线测量的彩色带。
senses.why: spectrum supplies the thing shown and skopein supplies the act of looking, so the word means a looker at spectra.
senses.whyCN: 「光谱」提供被看的东西，希腊语 skopein 提供看的动作，因此这个词的意思是「观看光谱之器」。

senses.title: A prism instrument
senses.titleCN: 棱镜分光镜
senses.definition: a spectroscope whose dispersing element is a glass prism, bending each wavelength through a different angle
senses.definitionCN: 以玻璃棱镜为分光元件的分光镜，使不同波长偏折不同角度
senses.example: The prism spectroscope gave a wide, soft band rather than sharp lines.
senses.exampleCN: 棱镜分光镜给出的是宽而柔和的色带，而非锐利谱线。
senses.why: the prism was the first dispersing element, so the compound simply names the version everyone started with.
senses.whyCN: 棱镜是最早的分光元件，这一复合词只是给最初人人使用的那一版命名。

senses.title: A grating instrument
senses.titleCN: 光栅分光镜
senses.definition: a spectroscope that uses a ruled or holographic grating, spreading light by interference rather than by refraction
senses.definitionCN: 用刻线或全息光栅的分光镜，靠干涉而非折射把光展开
senses.example: A grating spectroscope separates lines that a prism would blur together.
senses.exampleCN: 光栅分光镜能把棱镜会糊成一片的谱线分开。
senses.why: once gratings replaced prisms the old word stayed, because the slot filled by the dispersing element changed but the viewing task did not.
senses.whyCN: 光栅取代棱镜之后旧词仍保留，因为分光元件换了位置，观看的任务却没有换。

senses.title: An instrument attached to a telescope
senses.titleCN: 天文分光镜：接在望远镜后分析星光
senses.definition: a spectroscope mounted at the eyepiece of a telescope so that the light of a star or planet can be analysed
senses.definitionCN: 装在望远镜目镜端、用于分析恒星或行星之光的分光镜
senses.example: The astronomical spectroscope showed lines that no laboratory lamp produced.
senses.exampleCN: 天文分光镜显示出实验室任何灯都产生不了的谱线。
senses.why: the same instrument merely acquires a new source, so astronomy calls it by its function rather than by a new name.
senses.whyCN: 同一件仪器只是换了一个光源，因此天文学按功能称它，而不另造新名。

senses.title: A hand-held direct-vision instrument
senses.titleCN: 直视分光镜：可手持、无需折转光路
senses.definition: a compact spectroscope with an Amici prism that sends the spectrum straight through to the eye
senses.definitionCN: 装阿米西棱镜、使光谱沿直线进入眼睛的小型分光镜
senses.example: The direct-vision spectroscope fits in a coat pocket.
senses.exampleCN: 直视分光镜可以放进外套口袋。
senses.why: direct-vision names the optical trick that lets the viewer look along the same line as the incoming light.
senses.whyCN: 「直视式」指一种光学巧思：观察方向与入射光方向同在一条直线上。

senses.title: An instrument for absorption lines
senses.titleCN: 吸收分光镜：观察物质造成的暗线
senses.definition: a spectroscope used to view the dark absorption lines that a cool gas cuts out of a continuous spectrum
senses.definitionCN: 用于观察冷气体在连续谱上切出的暗线的分光镜
senses.example: With an absorption spectroscope the student identified sodium in the flame.
senses.exampleCN: 学生用吸收分光镜认出了火焰中的钠。
senses.why: absorption work needs the same dispersion, so the compound adds only the kind of line being studied.
senses.whyCN: 吸收研究需要的还是同一种分光，因此这一复合词只补充了所研究的谱线类型。

senses.title: A gemmological instrument
senses.titleCN: 宝石分光镜：鉴定宝石用的手持分光镜
senses.definition: a small spectroscope used by gemmologists to read the absorption bands that identify a stone
senses.definitionCN: 宝石学家用来读取鉴定宝石所需的吸收带的小型分光镜
senses.example: The gemmological spectroscope revealed bands typical of a heat-treated stone.
senses.exampleCN: 宝石分光镜显示出经热处理宝石特有的吸收带。
senses.why: a trade adopts the instrument and shortens its name to the use, so the tool becomes the test.
senses.whyCN: 某个行业采用这件仪器后，用用途来简称它，于是工具本身成了那道检验。

senses.title: Abstract: a test that separates a whole into parts
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：把整体拆成可辨成分的检验
senses.definition: any procedure that resolves a complicated whole into distinguishable components that can be read separately
senses.definitionCN: 任何把复杂整体拆成可分别读取的若干成分的做法
senses.example: The interview acted as a spectroscope for the company culture.
senses.exampleCN: 这场访谈起到了分光镜的作用，把公司文化拆成可辨的几条。
senses.why: the abstract sense keeps only the gesture of dispersion: a mixed thing is laid out so that each part shows.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义只保留「分光」这个动作：把混杂之物摊开，让每一部分显形。

intro.en: Spectroscope joins Latin spectrum, an appearance or image, with Greek skopein, to look. The word belongs to the spectrum-analysis work of Bunsen and Kirchhoff around 1860.
intro.cn: spectroscope 把拉丁 spectrum「外观、影像」与希腊 skopein「看」拼在一起。这个词属于本生与基尔霍夫 1860 年前后的光谱分析工作。

items.en: Spectrum in Latin meant appearance, image or apparition, from specere, to look at. English spectre comes from the same word.
items.cn: spectrum 在拉丁语中意为「外观、影像、幻影」，出自 specere「看」。英语 spectre 同出这个词。

items.en: Skopein meant to look at or examine; its noun skopos meant watcher or target, and English scope descends from it.
items.cn: skopein 意为「看、察看」；其名词 skopos 指「观看者、目标」，英语 scope 由此而来。

items.en: In 1859 and 1860 Bunsen and Kirchhoff showed that each element has a fixed set of lines, and the instrument that displayed them became central to chemistry.
items.cn: 1859 至 1860 年，本生与基尔霍夫证明每种元素都有固定的一组谱线，用来显示这些谱线的仪器随之成为化学的核心工具。

items.en: Spectroscope entered English in the early 1860s; the exact first printed use is not fixed, and spectrograph and spectrometer were coined later for recording and measuring versions.
items.cn: spectroscope 于 1860 年代初进入英语；确切的最早印刷用例并无定论，spectrograph 与 spectrometer 是后来为记录版和测量版另造的。

items.en: The first instruments dispersed light with a prism; gratings later gave sharper separation, but the older name covered both.
items.cn: 最早的仪器用棱镜分光；后来光栅给出更锐利的分开效果，旧名却同时涵盖两者。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and deeper origin): no single first citation is agreed for spectroscope, and the pre-Latin origin of spectrum is unsettled, so any Indo-European form proposed for specere is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与更深词源）：spectroscope 没有公认的唯一最早书证；spectrum 在拉丁语之前的来源亦无定论，凡为 specere 提出的印欧形式均属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds instruments whose names differ only in the last element and whose jobs differ sharply; group two holds the optical parts and methods that a spectroscope depends on.
note.cn: 第一组是名称只在最后一个成分上不同、功能却差别很大的仪器；第二组是分光镜所依赖的光学部件与方法。

entries.definition: Grapho means write, so a spectrograph records a spectrum on film or a detector instead of sending it to the eye.
entries.definitionCN: graphein 意为「写」，因此 spectrograph 把光谱记录在底片或探测器上，而不是送到眼前。

entries.definition: Metron means measure, so a spectrometer quantifies wavelengths and intensities rather than merely displaying them.
entries.definitionCN: metron 意为「测量」，因此 spectrometer 定量给出波长与强度，而不只是显示。

entries.definition: Helios means sun: an instrument that photographs the sun in one selected wavelength.
entries.definitionCN: helios 意为「太阳」：一种在选定波长上拍摄太阳的仪器。

entries.definition: It measures how much light a sample transmits or reflects at each wavelength, a job beyond simple viewing.
entries.definitionCN: 它测量样品在各波长上透过或反射了多少光，这已超出单纯观看。

entries.definition: A triangular block of glass that bends each wavelength by a different amount; it is a part, not the whole instrument.
entries.definitionCN: 三角形玻璃块，使各波长偏折不同角度；它只是部件，不是整台仪器。

entries.definition: A surface ruled with thousands of fine parallel lines, separating wavelengths by interference.
entries.definitionCN: 刻有数千条细平行线的表面，靠干涉把波长分开。

entries.definition: A device that selects a single narrow band from a spectrum and passes it on.
entries.definitionCN: 从光谱中选出单一窄带并让其通过的装置。

entries.definition: The narrow opening that turns a broad beam into a thin line of light before dispersion.
entries.definitionCN: 把宽光束变成一条细光再进入分光部分的窄缝。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the two real morphemes, the real instruments that share the family, and the real optical parts.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：两个真实语素、共享同一词族的真实仪器，以及真实的光学部件。

normal.en: spectro- means spectrum and -scope means look, so a spectroscope is a spectrum-looker.
normal.cn: spectro- 表示「光谱」，-scope 表示「看」，spectroscope 就是「看光谱的器具」。

normal.en: The family splits by suffix: -scope looks, -graph records, -meter measures.
normal.cn: 同族词按后缀分工：-scope 看，-graph 记录，-meter 测量。

normal.en: Its parts are a slit, a prism or grating, and a scale.
normal.cn: 它的部件是狭缝、棱镜或光栅，再加一根标尺。

normal.en: Bunsen and Kirchhoff made the instrument famous by reading lines in a flame.
normal.cn: 本生与基尔霍夫靠读取火焰中的谱线让这件仪器出了名。

normal.en: The adjective is spectroscopic and the field is spectroscopy.
normal.cn: 形容词是 spectroscopic，所属学科是 spectroscopy。

abstract.en: Picture a narrow door that lets a crowd through one at a time, each person a different colour.
abstract.cn: 想象一道窄门让人群一个一个通过，每个人是一种颜色。

abstract.en: Picture a barcode of light that names the substance that printed it.
abstract.cn: 想象一条光的条形码，能说出印出它的物质。

abstract.en: Picture a mixed choir standing in a line, each voice now audible on its own.
abstract.cn: 想象一个混声合唱团站成一排，每条嗓子现在都能单独听见。

examples.en: Kirchhoff and Bunsen used a spectroscope to identify caesium in mineral water.
examples.cn: 基尔霍夫与本生用分光镜在矿泉水中认出了铯。

examples.en: The spectroscope showed dark lines where the cooler gas absorbed light.
examples.cn: 分光镜在较冷气体吸收光的地方显示出暗线。

examples.en: Students built a simple spectroscope from a cardboard tube and a piece of grating.
examples.cn: 学生们用纸筒和一小片光栅做了一台简易分光镜。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「spectro（光谱）+ scope（看）」——把光摊成谱线再看的器具 → 分光镜

root: 拉丁 spectrum「外观、影像」（出自 specere「看」）+ 希腊 skopein「看」；spectrum 与 skopein 在拉丁语、希腊语之前的来源均不确定。英语 spectroscope。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses start from one act, splitting light so that it can be seen, and then follow the dispersing element, the source, the size, the kind of line, the trade and finally the figurative test.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从同一个动作出发：把光分开以便观看，随后依次落到分光元件、光源、体积、谱线种类、行业用途，最后落在比喻性的检验上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a slit, a prism and a scale turning one beam into a row of measurable colours.
core.cn: 核心意象：狭缝、棱镜与标尺把一束光变成一排可以测量的颜色。

branches.en: THE BASIC ACT: dispersion is followed at once by viewing, which is why the name ends in -scope.
branches.cn: 基本动作：分光之后立刻观看，因此名称以 -scope 收尾。

branches.en: DISPERSING ELEMENT: prism and grating do the same job by different physics.
branches.cn: 分光元件：棱镜与光栅以不同物理原理完成同一件事。

branches.en: NEW SOURCE: starlight enters the same tube and the old name simply travels with it.
branches.cn: 新光源：星光进入同一根管子，旧名随之迁移。

branches.en: SIZE AND TRADE: pocket versions and gemmology show the instrument shrinking to its use.
branches.cn: 体积与行业：口袋版与宝石鉴定说明仪器缩小成了它的用途。

branches.en: READING LINES: absorption lines and figurative tests both depend on separated parts being legible.
branches.cn: 读取谱线：吸收暗线与比喻性的检验，都依赖分开的部分可被读清。

intro.en: Spectroscope is a compound of a Latin noun and a Greek verb, and both halves return in a large family of scientific instruments.
intro.cn: spectroscope 由一个拉丁名词与一个希腊动词复合而成，两半都出现在一整个科学仪器词族里。

latinIntro.en: Latin contributes spectrum and specere; Greek contributes skopein and the suffix -skopion. There is no single native Latin verb behind the whole word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁部分提供 spectrum 与 specere，希腊部分提供 skopein 与后缀 -skopion；整词背后并没有一个本族拉丁动词。

items.example: The prefix marks the thing being displayed.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标出被显示的对象。

items.example: The suffix says the device is for looking, not for recording.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀说明该装置用于观看，而非记录。

items.example: A spectroscope split the beam into bands.
items.exampleCN: 分光镜把光束分成条带。

items.example: Spectroscopy identified the element.
items.exampleCN: 光谱分析认出了这种元素。

items.example: Spectroscopic data confirmed the result.
items.exampleCN: 光谱数据证实了这一结果。

items.example: The sample was examined spectroscopically.
items.exampleCN: 样品被以光谱方法检验。

items.meaning: a person who works with spectra
items.example: The spectroscopist calibrated the grating.
items.exampleCN: 光谱学家校准了光栅。

items.meaning: an instrument that records a spectrum
items.example: The spectrograph recorded the lines on film.
items.exampleCN: 摄谱仪把谱线记录在底片上。

items.meaning: an instrument that measures a spectrum
items.example: The spectrometer logged each intensity.
items.exampleCN: 光谱仪记下了每一条强度。

latinEntries.structure: spectare, spectavi, spectatum (verb, first conjugation, frequentative)

definition_zh: 光谱学；光谱分析（用光谱测定物质成分与结构的方法）
definition_en: the branch of science that studies how matter emits, absorbs or scatters radiation at different wavelengths
core_image: 实验台上一排排谱线像条形码，每张卡片记下一种物质对应的谱线位置
scene: 天文台里，观测者把星光拆成一条条谱线，再按谱线的位置推断星体的成分。Astronomers used spectroscopy to read the chemistry of a distant star from its lines.
sceneCN: 这里 spectroscopy 指「通过研究光谱来测定物质成分与结构的方法」（第 1 个义项：研究物质发射、吸收或散射各波长辐射的学科）；句意为天文学家借光谱分析从谱线读出遥远恒星的化学组成。可辨识物件：光谱图、谱线标尺、望远镜终端、记录本。

pos.zh: 光谱学；光谱分析（不可数）

forms.label: 罕用复数（指多种光谱技术）

senses.title: The study of spectra
senses.titleCN: 研究光谱的学科
senses.definition: the branch of physics and chemistry that studies how matter interacts with radiation at different wavelengths
senses.definitionCN: 物理学与化学中研究物质如何与各波长辐射相互作用的分支
senses.example: Astronomers used spectroscopy to read the chemistry of a distant star from its lines.
senses.exampleCN: 天文学家借光谱分析从谱线读出遥远恒星的化学组成。
senses.why: the name is spectrum plus the Greek suffix -skopia, meaning the act of viewing, so it names a whole discipline of looking at spectra.
senses.whyCN: 名称是 spectrum 加希腊后缀 -skopia「观看之事」，因此它命名的是一门观看光谱的完整学科。

senses.title: Reading starlight
senses.titleCN: 天文光谱学：由星光谱线推断天体
senses.definition: the use of spectra to determine the composition, temperature and motion of celestial bodies
senses.definitionCN: 用光谱测定天体的成分、温度与运动
senses.example: Stellar spectroscopy showed that the sun contains iron and calcium.
senses.exampleCN: 恒星光谱分析表明太阳含有铁与钙。
senses.why: astronomy cannot visit its objects, so the spectrum becomes the only message received from them.
senses.whyCN: 天文学无法亲临研究对象，光谱就成了唯一收到的讯息。

senses.title: Absorption spectroscopy
senses.titleCN: 吸收光谱法：看物质吃掉了哪些波长
senses.definition: the technique of passing a continuous spectrum through a sample and reading the wavelengths it absorbs
senses.definitionCN: 让连续谱穿过样品，读取被其吸收的波长
senses.example: Absorption spectroscopy identified the dye from the bands it removed.
senses.exampleCN: 吸收光谱法从被它吸收掉的条带认出了这种染料。
senses.why: a substance absorbs only the wavelengths its electrons or bonds can take, so the gaps become a signature.
senses.whyCN: 物质只吸收其电子或化学键能接受的波长，于是那些缺口就成了签名。

senses.title: Emission spectroscopy
senses.titleCN: 发射光谱法：看受激物质放出哪些波长
senses.definition: the technique of heating or exciting a sample and recording the wavelengths it emits
senses.definitionCN: 加热或激发样品，记录它所放出的波长
senses.example: Emission spectroscopy revealed caesium where no one had expected it.
senses.exampleCN: 发射光谱法在无人预料之处发现了铯。
senses.why: an excited atom returns to a lower state by sending out fixed quanta, and those quanta are the emitted lines.
senses.whyCN: 受激原子回到较低状态时放出固定的一份份能量，这些能量就是发射谱线。

senses.title: Raman spectroscopy
senses.titleCN: 拉曼光谱法：测散射光的微小频移
senses.definition: a technique that reads the small shifts in wavelength when laser light is scattered by molecular vibrations
senses.definitionCN: 读取激光被分子振动散射后波长微小偏移的方法
senses.example: Raman spectroscopy distinguished two powders that looked identical.
senses.exampleCN: 拉曼光谱法把两种看起来相同的粉末区分开来。
senses.why: the effect is named after Raman, and the technique is called spectroscopy because the information still arrives as shifted lines.
senses.whyCN: 该效应以拉曼命名，方法仍称光谱学，因为信息依旧以偏移后的谱线传来。

senses.title: Infrared spectroscopy
senses.titleCN: 红外光谱法：读分子振动
senses.definition: the use of infrared absorption to identify the vibrational modes of chemical bonds
senses.definitionCN: 用红外吸收来识别化学键振动模式的方法
senses.example: Infrared spectroscopy showed a sharp band where the carbonyl group should be.
senses.exampleCN: 红外光谱法在羰基应有的位置显示出一条锐带。
senses.why: infrared photons carry exactly the energies that make bonds stretch and bend, so this band of the spectrum reads structure.
senses.whyCN: 红外光子携带的能量正好能让化学键伸缩弯曲，因此这一段光谱读的是结构。

senses.title: Nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy
senses.titleCN: 核磁共振波谱法：读原子核的共振
senses.definition: a technique that maps the chemical environment of atomic nuclei from their resonance in a magnetic field
senses.definitionCN: 借原子核在磁场中的共振来描绘其化学环境的方法
senses.example: NMR spectroscopy settled the shape of the molecule in a single afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 核磁共振波谱法在一个下午就确定了分子的形状。
senses.why: the resonance is driven by radio waves rather than light, yet the readout is still a spectrum of peaks, so the name travels.
senses.whyCN: 共振由射频波而非光驱动，读出的仍是峰组成的谱，因此这个名称照样适用。

senses.title: Abstract: resolving any whole into readable parts
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：把任何整体拆成可读成分的分析
senses.definition: any systematic reading that separates a complex whole into components that can be identified one by one
senses.definitionCN: 任何把复杂整体分成可逐一识别的成分的系统性解读
senses.example: The survey worked as spectroscopy on the tastes of a whole city.
senses.exampleCN: 这项调查像光谱分析一样，把一整座城的口味拆成可读的几条。
senses.why: the abstract sense keeps the shape of the method: a mixture is spread out until each ingredient can be named.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义保留了方法的形状：把混合物摊开，直到每种成分都能被叫出名字。

intro.en: Spectroscopy is spectrum plus the Greek suffix -skopia, the act of viewing. It grew out of the spectrum analysis of the 1860s and became a discipline of its own.
intro.cn: spectroscopy 是 spectrum 加希腊后缀 -skopia「观看之事」。它从 1860 年代的光谱分析中生长出来，随后成为一门独立学科。

items.en: Spectrum meant appearance or image in Latin, from specere to look; English took the word through optics after Newton.
items.cn: spectrum 在拉丁语中指「外观、影像」，出自 specere「看」；英语在牛顿之后经光学把它引入。

items.en: The suffix -skopia names the act of viewing, from skopein to look; it is the abstract partner of the instrument suffix -scope.
items.cn: 后缀 -skopia 指「观看之事」，出自 skopein「看」；它是仪器后缀 -scope 的抽象对应形式。

items.en: Bunsen and Kirchhoff established that lines identify elements, and the technique was first called spectrum analysis rather than spectroscopy.
items.cn: 本生与基尔霍夫确立了谱线可识别元素，当时这项技术先被称为光谱分析，而非光谱学。

items.en: As infrared, Raman and nuclear magnetic resonance methods multiplied, spectroscopy became the general name for all of them.
items.cn: 随着红外、拉曼与核磁共振方法增多，spectroscopy 成了统称。

items.en: Spectrometry stresses measurement and spectroscopy stresses the reading of spectra, though working scientists often use the two interchangeably.
items.cn: spectrometry 强调测量，spectroscopy 强调读取光谱，不过实际工作者常把二者混用。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and deeper origin): the change from spectrum analysis to spectroscopy has no single documented first use, and the pre-Latin origin of specere is unsettled, so any Indo-European root offered is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与更深词源）：从「光谱分析」到「光谱学」的称谓变化没有唯一的文献首用记录；specere 在拉丁语之前的来源亦无定论，凡提出的印欧词根均属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds the near-identical names that split the work of viewing, recording and measuring; group two holds neighbouring analytical techniques.
note.cn: 第一组是名称几乎相同、却把观看、记录与测量分工开来的词；第二组是相邻的分析方法。

entries.definition: The physical device for viewing a spectrum; spectroscopy is the method and the field, not the object on the bench.
entries.definitionCN: 用于观看光谱的实体装置；spectroscopy 是方法与学科，不是台面上的那件东西。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning relating to spectral observation, as in spectroscopic data; it cannot name the discipline.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，意为「与光谱观察有关的」，如光谱数据；它不能指这门学科本身。

entries.definition: The measurement of spectra, built on metron measure; it overlaps spectroscopy but leans on quantities.
entries.definitionCN: 对光谱的测量，出自 metron「测量」；与光谱学重叠，但偏重量化。

entries.definition: The practice of recording spectra on film or detectors, built on graphein write.
entries.definitionCN: 把光谱记录在底片或探测器上的做法，出自 graphein「写」。

entries.definition: The older phrase for the same work, still used when the emphasis is on identifying a sample rather than on the field.
entries.definitionCN: 同一工作的旧称，在强调鉴定样品而非学科本身时仍在使用。

entries.definition: The measurement of light intensity without resolving wavelength; it gives totals, not lines.
entries.definitionCN: 不区分波长地测量光强；给出总量，不给谱线。

entries.definition: The measurement of radiant energy across the whole electromagnetic range, including invisible bands.
entries.definitionCN: 跨越整个电磁波段（含不可见波段）测量辐射能量。

entries.definition: A laboratory method that separates a mixture into components by how fast each moves; different tool, similar goal.
entries.definitionCN: 按各成分移动快慢把混合物分开的实验室方法；工具不同，目标相近。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real techniques and real instrument names that differ by suffix.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实语素、真实技术，以及只靠后缀区分的真实仪器名称。

normal.en: spectro- plus -scopy: the suffix -scopy names the activity, while -scope names the instrument.
normal.cn: spectro- 加 -scopy：后缀 -scopy 指活动，-scope 指仪器。

normal.en: The main branches are named by the band or effect: infrared, Raman, NMR.
normal.cn: 主要分支按波段或效应命名：红外、拉曼、核磁共振。

normal.en: Absorption reads gaps; emission reads bright lines.
normal.cn: 吸收法读缺口，发射法读亮线。

normal.en: Astronomical spectroscopy is the only way to weigh a star without visiting it.
normal.cn: 天文光谱学是不亲临恒星而测量它的唯一途径。

normal.en: The adjective is spectroscopic and the worker is a spectroscopist.
normal.cn: 形容词是 spectroscopic，从业者叫 spectroscopist。

abstract.en: Picture a choir where every voice is given its own line on a page.
abstract.cn: 想象一个合唱团，每条嗓子在纸面上都分到自己的那一行。

abstract.en: Picture a fingerprint made of light rather than skin.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚用光而不是皮肤印出的指纹。

abstract.en: Picture a locked room that will only answer in wavelengths.
abstract.cn: 想象一间上锁的屋子，只肯用波长来回答。

examples.en: Infrared spectroscopy is routine in every organic chemistry laboratory.
examples.cn: 红外光谱法是每个有机化学实验室的常规手段。

examples.en: The new telescope was built chiefly for spectroscopy of faint galaxies.
examples.cn: 这台新望远镜主要建造用于暗弱星系的光谱分析。

examples.en: Her doctorate is in molecular spectroscopy rather than optics.
examples.cn: 她的博士学位研究方向是分子光谱学，而不是光学。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「spectro（光谱）+ scopy（观看之术）」——专门观看光谱的学问 → 光谱学

root: 拉丁 spectrum「外观、影像」（出自 specere「看」）+ 希腊 -skopia「观看之事」（出自 skopein「看」）；两处更早来源均不确定。英语 spectroscopy。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the discipline itself to its astronomical use, then through absorption, emission, Raman, infrared and resonance methods, and end with the method as a metaphor.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从学科本身走向天文应用，再依次经过吸收、发射、拉曼、红外与共振各类方法，最后以方法的比喻义收尾。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: light laid out in lines that can be read like a printed code.
core.cn: 核心意象：光被摊成一行行谱线，可以像印刷代码一样读取。

branches.en: DISCIPLINE: the suffix -scopy turns one act of looking into a field of study.
branches.cn: 学科：后缀 -scopy 把一次观看的动作变成一门研究领域。

branches.en: DISTANT OBJECTS: starlight is the only sample astronomy can obtain.
branches.cn: 遥远对象：星光是天文学唯一能取得的样品。

branches.en: TWO DIRECTIONS: absorption reads what is missing, emission reads what is sent out.
branches.cn: 两个方向：吸收读缺少的部分，发射读放出的部分。

branches.en: SCATTERED AND INFRARED: shifted lines and bond vibrations widen the range of readable matter.
branches.cn: 散射与红外：偏移的谱线与化学键振动扩大了可读物质的范围。

branches.en: RESONANCE AND METAPHOR: even nuclei yield peaks, and any mixture can be spread out to be read.
branches.cn: 共振与比喻：连原子核也能给出峰，而任何混合物都可摊开来读。

intro.en: Spectroscopy is spectrum plus an abstract Greek suffix, and the same suffix contrasts neatly with the instrument suffix -scope.
intro.cn: spectroscopy 是 spectrum 加一个抽象希腊后缀，这个后缀与仪器后缀 -scope 形成整齐对照。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies spectrum and specere; Greek supplies skopein and -skopia. The abstract noun is later than the instrument noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁提供 spectrum 与 specere，希腊提供 skopein 与 -skopia；抽象名词晚于仪器名词出现。

items.example: The prefix ties every technique to spectra.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把每种技术都系在光谱上。

items.meaning: the act or method of viewing
items.example: The suffix names a method rather than a device.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀命名的是方法，而非装置。

items.example: Spectroscopy identified the element.
items.exampleCN: 光谱学认出了这种元素。

items.example: Spectroscopic evidence supported the claim.
items.exampleCN: 光谱学证据支持了这一说法。

items.example: The gas was detected spectroscopically.
items.exampleCN: 这种气体被以光谱方法探测到。

items.example: The spectroscopist tuned the laser.
items.exampleCN: 光谱学家调好了激光。

items.example: The spectroscope showed the bands directly.
items.exampleCN: 分光镜直接显示出条带。

items.example: Spectrometry gave precise intensities.
items.exampleCN: 光谱测量给出了精确的强度。

items.example: Spectrography preserved the faint lines.
items.exampleCN: 摄谱记录保住了那些暗弱谱线。

latinEntries.meaning: the older name of the method

definition_zh: 光谱；波谱；范围，幅度；（意见、症状等的）整个序列，谱系
definition_en: the band of colours or wavelengths produced when light is dispersed, or a full range of related things
core_image: 一束白光穿过棱镜，在墙上摊成由红到紫的连续彩带，两端渐渐变暗
scene: 一束白光穿过棱镜，在墙上摊成由红到紫的连续彩带，两端渐渐变暗。A prism spread the spectrum across the wall in ordered bands.
sceneCN: 这里 spectrum 指「白光经色散后形成的彩色光带」（第 1 个义项：由不同波长按序排列成的可见色带）；句意为棱镜把光谱摊在墙上，形成有次序的条带。可辨识物件：棱镜、白光束、墙面彩带、暗边。

pos.zh: 光谱；波谱；范围；序列，谱系

senses.title: The colour band from a prism
senses.titleCN: 棱镜色散出的彩色光带
senses.definition: the band of colours seen when white light is dispersed, arranged from red through violet
senses.definitionCN: 白光被色散后出现的彩色带，从红到紫依次排列
senses.example: A prism spread the spectrum across the wall in ordered bands.
senses.exampleCN: 棱镜把光谱摊在墙上，形成有次序的条带。
senses.why: Latin spectrum meant an appearance or image, and Newton applied it to the coloured image thrown by a prism.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 spectrum 意为「外观、影像」，牛顿把这个词用于棱镜投出的彩色影像。

senses.title: The full range of wavelengths
senses.titleCN: 全部波长的范围，含不可见波段
senses.definition: the complete range of radiation, from radio waves through visible light to gamma rays
senses.definitionCN: 从无线电波经可见光到伽马射线的完整辐射范围
senses.example: The electromagnetic spectrum extends far beyond what the eye can see.
senses.exampleCN: 电磁波谱远远超出肉眼可见的范围。
senses.why: once invisible bands were discovered, the colour band widened into a continuum of wavelengths.
senses.whyCN: 不可见波段被发现后，原本的彩色带扩展成了连续的波长范围。

senses.title: A range of values
senses.titleCN: 数值或程度的范围、幅度
senses.definition: a continuous range between two extremes, as of sizes, doses or prices
senses.definitionCN: 在两个极端之间连续分布的范围，如尺寸、剂量或价格
senses.example: The clinic treats a wide spectrum of injuries.
senses.exampleCN: 这家诊所处理范围很广的各种损伤。
senses.why: the image of ordered bands becomes a scale on which a whole set of cases can be placed.
senses.whyCN: 有次序的条带这一形象，变成了一把可以安放一整组情况的标尺。

senses.title: A range of opinions
senses.titleCN: 意见的整个分布或谱系
senses.definition: the full spread of views held by a group, from one extreme to the other
senses.definitionCN: 一个群体所持看法的完整分布，从一端到另一端
senses.example: The committee heard a spectrum of opinion before voting.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会在表决前听取了各种不同意见。
senses.why: politics borrowed the word because opinions, like colours, arrange themselves in a gradation rather than in two blocks.
senses.whyCN: 政治借用这个词，因为意见像颜色一样呈渐变排列，而不是只分两块。

senses.title: A continuum of traits
senses.titleCN: 连续分布的特征谱系
senses.definition: a continuous range of a condition or trait, as in autism spectrum or a spectrum of severity
senses.definitionCN: 某种状况或特征的连续分布，如自闭症谱系或严重程度谱系
senses.example: The diagnosis sits on a spectrum rather than at a fixed point.
senses.exampleCN: 这一诊断位于一个连续谱系上，而不在某个固定点上。
senses.why: medicine took the word to replace sharp categories with a graded range, keeping the sense of ordered bands.
senses.whyCN: 医学用这个词取代非此即彼的分类，保留「有次序条带」的含义，表示渐变范围。

senses.title: A line spectrum
senses.titleCN: 线状谱：由一条条分立的亮线或暗线构成
senses.definition: a spectrum made of discrete bright or dark lines at specific wavelengths rather than a continuous band
senses.definitionCN: 由特定波长上一条条分立亮线或暗线构成的谱
senses.example: The line spectrum of hydrogen became the key to atomic theory.
senses.exampleCN: 氢的线状谱成了原子理论的关键。
senses.why: when a hot gas emits only certain wavelengths, the continuous band breaks into lines and the word still names the result.
senses.whyCN: 热气体只放出特定波长时，连续带断成一条条线，而这个词仍旧称呼这一结果。

senses.title: The frequency content of a signal
senses.titleCN: 信号的频谱：各频率成分的分布
senses.definition: the distribution of a signal across frequencies, shown as peaks on a frequency axis
senses.definitionCN: 信号在各频率上的分布，以频率轴上的峰显示
senses.example: The engineer looked for the hum in the spectrum of the recording.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师在录音的频谱里寻找那阵嗡鸣。
senses.why: Fourier analysis turned a signal into ordered components, exactly the arrangement the older word already described.
senses.whyCN: 傅里叶分析把信号拆成有次序的成分，正是旧词原本描述的那种排列。

senses.title: Abstract: the whole extent of something
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：某事物的全部幅度与全部层次
senses.definition: the entire extent of a thing, from its lowest to its highest level, considered as one ordered whole
senses.definitionCN: 某物从最低到最高层次的全部幅度，被当作一个有次序的整体
senses.example: The exhibition covers the spectrum of the artist career, from student sketches to late murals.
senses.exampleCN: 展览涵盖这位艺术家创作生涯的全部层次，从学生素描到晚期刊画。
senses.why: the abstract sense drops the light and keeps only the span, so any complete gradation can be called a spectrum.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义去掉光，只留跨度，因此任何完整的渐变都可以称为 spectrum。

intro.en: Spectrum is Latin for appearance or image, from specere to look. Newton made it an optical term in 1671, and it later widened into every ordered range.
intro.cn: spectrum 在拉丁语中指「外观、影像」，出自 specere「看」。牛顿 1671 年使它成为光学词，后来它扩展到一切有次序的范围。

items.en: Specere meant to look at or observe; it also stands behind specimen, spectacle, speculate and perspective.
items.cn: specere 意为「看、观察」；specimen、spectacle、speculate 与 perspective 也出自它。

items.en: The noun spectrum named an appearance or image, especially a ghostly one; English spectre descends from the same form.
items.cn: 名词 spectrum 指「外观、影像」，尤指幽灵般的影像；英语 spectre 同出这一形式。

items.en: In his New Theory about Light and Colours Newton used spectrum for the coloured band thrown by a prism, and the optical sense fixed the word in science.
items.cn: 牛顿在《关于光与色的新理论》中用 spectrum 指棱镜投出的彩色带，这一光学义使该词在科学中固定下来。

items.en: Spectral lines and the discovery of invisible radiation extended spectrum from a colour band to the whole range of wavelengths.
items.cn: 谱线的研究与不可见辐射的发现，把 spectrum 从彩色带扩展到全部波长范围。

items.en: In the twentieth century the word spread to opinions, disease traits, political positions and any graded set.
items.cn: 20 世纪，这个词扩展到意见、疾病特征、政治立场以及任何渐变集合。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the pre-Latin shape of specere has no agreed derivation, so its link to the Indo-European root commonly cited for seeing is a reconstruction rather than a proven step.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：specere 在拉丁语之前的形式没有公认的派生路径，因此它与常被引用的「看」这一印欧词根的联系属重构，而非已证实的环节。

note.en: Group one holds words built on the same Latin root specere but now far apart in meaning; group two holds the range words that overlap the modern uses of spectrum.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁 specere、如今意义却相去甚远的词；第二组是与 spectrum 现代用法重叠的范围类词。

entries.definition: The same Latin word in its older sense of a ghostly apparition; the British spelling keeps the Latin -re.
entries.definitionCN: 同一个拉丁词，保留其「幽灵影像」的旧义；英式拼写保留拉丁的 -re 形式。

entries.definition: From specere through a noun meaning something shown; it is a sample, not a range.
entries.definitionCN: 经一个表示「展示之物」的名词出自 specere；它指样品，不指范围。

entries.definition: From specula, a watchtower: to look out and reason about what cannot be seen directly.
entries.definitionCN: 出自 specula「瞭望塔」：向外眺望，并对无法直接看见之事作推断。

entries.definition: From spectare, to watch: something striking enough to draw a crowd of eyes.
entries.definitionCN: 出自 spectare「观看」：夺目到足以引来一片目光的事物。

entries.definition: The everyday word for the distance between limits; spectrum adds the idea of ordered gradation.
entries.definitionCN: 表示上下限之间跨度的日常词；spectrum 多了「有次序的渐变」这一层。

entries.definition: The full series of notes or colours; it stresses completeness where spectrum stresses spread.
entries.definitionCN: 音符或颜色的完整系列；强调完整，而 spectrum 强调铺开的跨度。

entries.definition: A continuous sequence with no breaks; a spectrum may be continuous or broken into lines.
entries.definitionCN: 没有间断的连续序列；而 spectrum 既可以是连续的，也可以断成谱线。

entries.definition: An impressive or ordered display of things; it lacks the physical band image of spectrum.
entries.definitionCN: 事物的有序陈列；它没有 spectrum 那种物理光带的形象。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin root, the real Newtonian sense and the real modern extensions.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁词根、真实的牛顿义，以及真实的现代扩展。

normal.en: Spectrum and spectre share one Latin source: both name an appearance.
normal.cn: spectrum 与 spectre 共享一个拉丁来源：两者都指「显现之物」。

normal.en: Newton gave the word its colour-band sense in 1671.
normal.cn: 牛顿在 1671 年赋予它彩色带的意义。

normal.en: The plural is spectra, following the Latin neuter pattern.
normal.cn: 复数按拉丁中性词模式作 spectra。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the range uses: broad spectrum, spectrum of opinion.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出范围义：广谱、意见的分布范围。

normal.en: The adjective spectral can mean both of a spectrum and ghostly.
normal.cn: 形容词 spectral 既可指「光谱的」，也可指「幽灵般的」。

abstract.en: Picture a street of houses shading from one colour at each end to another in the middle.
abstract.cn: 想象一条街的房子，从两端的一种颜色渐渐过渡到中间的另一种颜色。

abstract.en: Picture a choir arranged by pitch so that every voice finds a place.
abstract.cn: 想象一个按音高排列的合唱团，每条嗓子都能找到位置。

abstract.en: Picture a single note struck, then split into all the notes it contains.
abstract.cn: 想象敲响一个音，再把它拆成其中包含的所有音。

examples.en: The visible spectrum runs from about four hundred to seven hundred nanometres.
examples.cn: 可见光谱大约从四百纳米延伸到七百纳米。

examples.en: Their tastes cover a spectrum from plain folk songs to electronic noise.
examples.cn: 他们的口味覆盖从朴素民歌到电子噪音的整个范围。

examples.en: A spectrum analyser showed a strong peak at fifty hertz.
examples.cn: 频谱分析仪显示出五十赫兹处有一个强峰。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「spectr（看）+ um」——眼睛看到的一条条颜色 → 光谱；引申为一条条排开的整个范围

root: 拉丁 spectrum「外观、影像」，出自 specere「看、观察」；specere 在拉丁语之前的来源不确定。英语 spectrum，复数 spectra。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses begin with the colour band, widen to all wavelengths, then slide into ranges of values, opinions and traits, then to line and signal spectra, and end with any complete gradation.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项以彩色带开始，扩展到全部波长，再滑入数值、意见与特征的范围，接着到线状谱与信号频谱，最后落在任何完整的渐变上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a white beam broken into bands that stay in order from one end to the other.
core.cn: 核心意象：一束白光断成若干条带，从一端到另一端始终保持次序。

branches.en: THE OPTICAL CORE: Newton's prism image is still the literal centre of the word.
branches.cn: 光学核心：牛顿的棱镜影像仍是这个词最字面的中心。

branches.en: BAND AND LINES: invisible bands and discrete lines are two shapes the same spectrum can take.
branches.cn: 带与线：不可见波段与分立谱线，是同一个光谱可以呈现的两种形状。

branches.en: GRADED SCALE: values and traits are placed along a span instead of in two boxes.
branches.cn: 渐变标尺：数值与特征被放在一段跨度上，而不是装进两个格子。

branches.en: POLITICAL SPREAD: opinions arrange themselves like colours, from one edge to the other.
branches.cn: 意见分布：意见像颜色一样，从一端排到另一端。

branches.en: SIGNAL AND WHOLE: a signal decomposed by frequency, and any complete extent, keep only the sense of ordered parts.
branches.cn: 信号与整体：按频率拆开的信号、以及任何完整幅度，都只保留「有次序的各个部分」这一层。

intro.en: Spectrum is a single Latin noun, but the root specere also builds a large English family whose members drifted far apart.
intro.cn: spectrum 是一个拉丁名词，但其词根 specere 还构成一个庞大的英语词族，成员意义已漂得很远。

latinIntro.en: The Latin noun is spectrum, spectri, with specere as its verb. Spectre, specimen and speculate are relatives, not compounds of spectrum.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁名词是 spectrum、spectri，其动词为 specere。spectre、specimen 与 speculate 是它的亲属词，而不是 spectrum 的复合词。

items.example: The spectrum lay across the wall in bands.
items.exampleCN: 光谱以条带形式横在墙上。

items.example: The two spectra overlapped near the red end.
items.exampleCN: 两条光谱在红端附近重叠。

items.example: Spectral lines revealed the gas.
items.exampleCN: 谱线揭示出那种气体。

items.example: The two sources differ spectrally.
items.exampleCN: 这两个光源在光谱上不同。

items.example: The spectroscope showed the band directly.
items.exampleCN: 分光镜直接显示出光带。

items.example: Spectroscopy became a discipline.
items.exampleCN: 光谱学成为一门学科。

items.example: The spectrometer logged the peaks.
items.exampleCN: 光谱仪记下了各个峰。

items.example: The drug is broad-spectrum.
items.exampleCN: 这种药是广谱的。

definition_zh: 波长；按波长区分的色或波段；看待事物的角度（喻）
definition_en: the distance between one point on a wave and the same point on the next wave, or the band of light that distance identifies
core_image: 池面上一列等距的波纹向前推进，两根标杆量出相邻两个波峰之间的距离
scene: 池面上一列等距的波纹向前推进，测量者量出相邻两个波峰之间的距离。Each colour of the beam has its own wavelength, and the grating sorts them by that length.
sceneCN: 这里 wavelength 指「相邻两个波峰或波谷之间的距离」（第 1 个义项：波形重复一次所跨越的长度）；句意为光束中每种颜色各有自己的波长，光栅按这个长度把它们分开。可辨识物件：水波、两根标杆、光栅、分色光斑。

pos.zh: 波长；按波长划分的波段；喻指看法、思路

senses.title: Distance between two crests
senses.titleCN: 相邻两个波峰之间的距离
senses.definition: the distance from one crest of a wave to the next crest, or between any two corresponding points in the same phase
senses.definitionCN: 从一个波峰到下一个波峰、或同一相位任意两点之间的距离
senses.example: Each colour of the beam has its own wavelength, and the grating sorts them by that length.
senses.exampleCN: 光束中每种颜色各有自己的波长，光栅按这个长度把它们分开。
senses.why: the word is simply wave plus length: it names the physical length over which the wave repeats itself.
senses.whyCN: 这个词就是「波」加「长度」：它命名的正是波重复一次所跨越的那段长度。

senses.title: The colour a wavelength identifies
senses.titleCN: 由波长确定的那一种颜色或波段
senses.definition: the particular band of visible light that a given wavelength value stands for, such as red or blue
senses.definitionCN: 某个波长数值所代表的可见光波段，如红或蓝
senses.example: A wavelength near four hundred nanometres looks violet to the eye.
senses.exampleCN: 接近四百纳米的波长在眼中呈紫色。
senses.why: once each colour had a number, people began to use the number for the colour, so wavelength came to name the band itself.
senses.whyCN: 每种颜色有了数值之后，人们开始用数值代指颜色，于是 wavelength 也指那一段光本身。

senses.title: Wavelength of a sound wave
senses.titleCN: 声波的波长
senses.definition: the distance between successive compressions or rarefactions in a sound wave, set by speed and pitch
senses.definitionCN: 声波中相邻密部或疏部之间的距离，由声速与音高决定
senses.example: A low note has a longer wavelength than a high note.
senses.exampleCN: 低音的波长比高音更长。
senses.why: the same definition works for any periodic disturbance, so sound inherited the word without any change.
senses.whyCN: 同一定义适用于任何周期性扰动，因此声学原封不动地继承了这个词。

senses.title: A radio band
senses.titleCN: 无线电波段：通信所用的波长范围
senses.definition: a band of radio waves identified by its wavelength, used to separate broadcast and communication channels
senses.definitionCN: 按波长划分的无线电波段，用来区分广播与通信频道
senses.example: The station moved to a longer wavelength to reach the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 这家电台改用更长的波长，以便传到山谷里。
senses.why: early radio engineering tuned by wavelength rather than frequency, and the habit outlived the physics.
senses.whyCN: 早期无线电工程按波长而非频率调谐，这一习惯比其物理依据活得更久。

senses.title: Wavelength inside a medium
senses.titleCN: 介质中的波长：进入玻璃或水后变短
senses.definition: the reduced distance between crests when a wave enters a medium of higher refractive index, while its frequency stays fixed
senses.definitionCN: 波进入折射率更高的介质后波峰间距变短，而频率保持不变
senses.example: Inside the glass the wavelength shrinks, so the glass can hold more crests per metre.
senses.exampleCN: 进入玻璃后波长变短，因此每米能容纳更多波峰。
senses.why: the length is a property of the wave in a place, not an unchangeable label, so physics had to qualify it.
senses.whyCN: 长度是波在某个地点的属性，而非固定标签，因此物理学必须对它加以限定。

senses.title: Wavelength of a matter wave
senses.titleCN: 物质波波长：电子等粒子对应的波
senses.definition: the wavelength associated with a particle such as an electron, set by its momentum
senses.definitionCN: 电子等粒子所对应的波长，由其动量决定
senses.example: The electron wavelength is short enough to resolve a crystal lattice.
senses.exampleCN: 电子的波长足够短，可以分辨晶格。
senses.why: quantum theory extended the word from waves of light to waves of probability attached to particles.
senses.whyCN: 量子理论把这个词从光波扩展到附着于粒子的概率波。

senses.title: Being on the same wavelength
senses.titleCN: 喻指想法一致、心意相通
senses.definition: sharing the same way of thinking so that two people understand each other easily
senses.definitionCN: 持有相同的思路，因而彼此容易理解
senses.example: The two engineers were on the same wavelength from the first meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 两位工程师从第一次会面起就想法一致。
senses.why: two waves reinforce only when their crests match, and that physical agreement became a figure for mental agreement.
senses.whyCN: 两列波只有波峰对齐才会叠加增强，这种物理上的契合被用来比喻心思相合。

senses.title: Abstract: the scale on which things differ
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：衡量事物差异的尺度
senses.definition: a scale or dimension along which otherwise similar things can be compared
senses.definitionCN: 在某个维度上比较原本相似之物的尺度
senses.example: The two policies differ only in wavelength, not in kind.
senses.exampleCN: 这两项政策只在尺度上不同，性质上并无差别。
senses.why: the abstract sense keeps only the measuring function: wavelength is whatever scale makes the difference visible.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义只保留测量功能：波长成了那个能让差异显形的尺度。

intro.en: Wavelength is an English compound of wave and length, coined when wave optics needed a name for the distance between crests. The exact first use is not settled.
intro.cn: wavelength 是 wave 与 length 的英语复合词，在波动光学需要为相邻波峰之间的距离命名时出现，确切首见年代并无定论。

items.en: Wave named the moving ridge on water long before physics used it; its deeper origin is uncertain.
items.cn: wave 在物理学使用它之前很久就指水面移动的波脊；其更早来源不确定。

items.en: Length comes from Old English lengthu, a native noun built on lang, long.
items.cn: length 出自古英语 lengthu，是本族名词，由 lang「长」构成。

items.en: Wave and length were joined once interference experiments made the spacing between crests measurable; early texts often wrote it as two words.
items.cn: 当干涉实验使波峰间距可以测量时，wave 与 length 被合在一起；早期文本常分写作两个词。

items.en: The compound then covered water waves, sound and light alike, because each repeats over a fixed distance.
items.cn: 此后这一复合词同时涵盖水波、声波与光，因为三者都在固定距离上重复。

items.en: In the twentieth century on the same wavelength turned the physical match into a figure for mutual understanding.
items.cn: 20 世纪，「波长相同」这一说法把物理上的对齐转为彼此理解的比喻。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and deeper origin): the first printed use is not agreed, nor whether it was written wave length or wavelength; the deeper origin of wave is likewise unsettled.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与更深词源）：最早印刷用例没有定论，也无法确认当时写作 wave length 还是 wavelength；wave 的更深来源同样没有定论。

note.en: Group one holds compounds that begin with wave but name different quantities; group two holds the quantities that wavelength is measured against.
note.cn: 第一组是以 wave 开头、却指不同量的复合词；第二组是与波长相互换算或对照的量。

entries.definition: The number of waves per unit length, the inverse of wavelength; a spectroscopist favourite.
entries.definitionCN: 单位长度内的波数，是波长的倒数；光谱学家常用。

entries.definition: The surface over which all points share the same phase; it marks a position, not a distance.
entries.definitionCN: 所有点相位相同的那个面；它标出位置，而不是距离。

entries.definition: A brief localized oscillation used in signal analysis; its length is not the same as its duration.
entries.definitionCN: 信号分析中短暂而局部的一段振荡；其长度与持续时间并非同一件事。

entries.definition: A tube or channel that confines and directs waves; it carries them rather than measuring them.
entries.definitionCN: 约束并引导波的管子或通道；它传输波，而不测量波。

entries.definition: The number of cycles per second; for any fixed speed, frequency and wavelength are inversely related.
entries.definitionCN: 每秒的周期数；在速度固定时，频率与波长成反比。

entries.definition: The maximum displacement of a wave, which sets its intensity rather than its spacing.
entries.definitionCN: 波的最大位移，决定强度而不是间距。

entries.definition: The time one full cycle takes; it is the time-domain partner of wavelength.
entries.definitionCN: 完成一个完整周期所需的时间；是波长在时间上的对应量。

entries.definition: A group of wavelengths treated together; wavelength is a single value, a band is a range.
entries.definitionCN: 被当作一组处理的一段波长；波长是单个值，band 是一段范围。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the two real English halves, the real inverse relation with frequency, and the real fixed phrase.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：两个真实的英语成分、与频率之间真实的倒数关系，以及真实的固定短语。

normal.en: Wave plus length: the length one wave occupies before it repeats.
normal.cn: 「波」加「长度」：一列波重复之前所占据的长度。

normal.en: Wavelength and frequency move in opposite directions when speed is fixed.
normal.cn: 速度固定时，波长与频率朝相反方向变化。

normal.en: The plural is wavelengths, and old texts wrote wave length as two words.
normal.cn: 复数形式加 -s，旧文本曾把「波」与「长度」分作两词。

normal.en: The everyday figure is on the same wavelength, meaning thinking alike.
normal.cn: 日常比喻是「波长相同」，意为想法一致。

normal.en: Radio engineers once tuned by wavelength and still speak of long and short wave.
normal.cn: 无线电工程师曾按波长调谐，如今仍说长波与短波。

abstract.en: Picture a ruler laid along a row of identical hilltops.
abstract.cn: 想象一把尺子沿一排相同的山顶铺开。

abstract.en: Picture two radio dials that must point to the same mark before a call connects.
abstract.cn: 想象两只收音刻度盘必须指到同一格，通话才接得通。

abstract.en: Picture two friends walking in step without having to say so.
abstract.cn: 想象两位朋友不用开口就同步迈步。

examples.en: The laser emits at a wavelength of six hundred and thirty nanometres.
examples.cn: 这台激光器在六百三十纳米的波长上发射。

examples.en: Longer wavelengths travel farther around obstacles but carry less detail.
examples.cn: 更长的波长能绕过障碍传得更远，但携带的细节更少。

examples.en: The two managers were finally on the same wavelength about the budget.
examples.cn: 两位经理在预算问题上终于想法一致了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「wave（波）+ length（长度）」——一列波的长度 → 波长；两个人「长度相同」→ 想法一致

root: 英语本族复合词：wave（古英语，指波浪，更早来源不确定）+ length（古英语 lengthu，出自 lang「长」）。无拉丁同族，故本词条不列拉丁借词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses begin with the measured distance, then move to the colour it names, to sound waves, radio bands, waves inside glass and matter waves, and finally to two figurative scales.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项以可测量的距离开始，随后移到它所代表的颜色、声波、无线电波段、玻璃中的波与物质波，最后落在两种比喻性的尺度上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ruler laid between two crests of the same repeating wave.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把尺子铺在同一列重复波的相邻两个波峰之间。

branches.en: PHYSICAL LENGTH: the literal repetition distance is the root of every other sense.
branches.cn: 物理长度：字面的重复距离，是其余一切义项的根。

branches.en: COLOUR AS NUMBER: a value becomes the name of a visible band.
branches.cn: 以数代色：一个数值变成了某段可见光的名字。

branches.en: OTHER WAVES: sound and radio inherit the same spacing, though engineers tuned by it rather than measured it.
branches.cn: 别的波：声与无线电继承同一种间距，只是工程师按它调谐而非测量它。

branches.en: CONTEXT AND QUANTUM: a medium shortens the length, and matter itself acquires one.
branches.cn: 介质与量子：介质使长度变短，物质本身也获得了波长。

branches.en: ALIGNMENT AND SCALE: matching crests becomes matching minds, and any dimension of difference becomes a scale.
branches.cn: 对齐与尺度：波峰相合变成心思相合，任何差异维度都成了一个尺度。

intro.en: Wavelength is not a Latin derivative but a native English compound, so it is best read as two free morphemes rather than as prefix plus root.
intro.cn: wavelength 不是拉丁派生词，而是英语本族复合词，因此更适合按两个自由语素来读，而不是按前缀加词根来读。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root behind this word: wave and length are both native English nouns, so no Latin borrowing stands behind it; the Greek or Latin quotations sometimes offered for them are cognates, not ancestors.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词背后没有拉丁词根：wave 与 length 都是英语本族名词，没有拉丁借词为其源头；有时为它们给出的希腊或拉丁形式只是同源词，并非祖先。

items.structure: wave (native English noun, older origin uncertain)
items.meaning: a raised ridge that moves across water; any periodic disturbance
items.meaningCN: 在水面移动的波脊；任何周期性扰动
items.example: The wave passed under the boat.
items.exampleCN: 那道波从船下过去。

items.structure: length (native English noun, from Old English lengthu)
items.meaning: the measure of something from end to end
items.meaningCN: 从一端到另一端的长度
items.example: He measured the length of the table.
items.exampleCN: 他量了桌子的长度。

items.meaning: the length over which a wave repeats
items.example: Each colour has its own wavelength.
items.exampleCN: 每种颜色各有自己的波长。

items.example: The instrument records many wavelengths at once.
items.exampleCN: 这台仪器一次记录许多波长。

items.meaning: the number of waves per unit length
items.example: The peak sits at a wavenumber of sixteen hundred.
items.exampleCN: 该峰位于波数一千六百处。

items.example: The wavefront arrived flat and unbroken.
items.exampleCN: 波前平整而不破碎地到达。

items.example: The signal ran through a copper waveguide.
items.exampleCN: 信号沿铜制波导管传输。

items.example: A multiwavelength survey found the faint galaxy.
items.exampleCN: 一次多波段巡天发现了那个暗弱星系。

items.example: The coating is wavelength-dependent.
items.exampleCN: 这层镀膜是随波长变化的。

definition_zh: 频率；频次；频繁；重复率；（无线电）频道频率
definition_en: the rate at which something repeats within a given time, or the number of cycles of a wave per second
core_image: 音叉与琴弦并排，计时器记录每秒振动的次数，指针稳稳停在同一个刻度
scene: 实验台上音叉与琴弦并排，计时器记录每秒振动的次数，指针停在同一个刻度。The tuning fork fixes the frequency that the string must match.
sceneCN: 这里 frequency 指「单位时间内重复的次数」（第 1 个义项：某事件在给定时间内发生的次数）；句意为音叉确定了琴弦必须匹配的频率。可辨识物件：音叉、琴弦、计时器、刻度盘。

pos.zh: 频率；频次；频繁；（无线电）频率

senses.title: Rate of repetition
senses.titleCN: 单位时间内重复的次数
senses.definition: the number of times an event or a process repeats within a given period
senses.definitionCN: 某事件或过程在给定时间内重复的次数
senses.example: The tuning fork fixes the frequency that the string must match.
senses.exampleCN: 音叉确定了琴弦必须匹配的频率。
senses.why: Latin frequentia named a crowding or abundance, and that idea of many occurrences became a countable rate.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 frequentia 指「拥挤、众多」，这种「出现得多」的意思后来变成可计数的比率。

senses.title: Cycles per second
senses.titleCN: 一秒钟内完成的周期数
senses.definition: the number of complete cycles of a periodic wave that pass a point each second, measured in hertz
senses.definitionCN: 每秒通过某点的完整波周期数，以赫兹计
senses.example: The mains supply runs at a frequency of fifty hertz.
senses.exampleCN: 市电以五十赫兹的频率运行。
senses.why: physics narrowed the general rate to a count of wave cycles, and gave it a unit named after Hertz.
senses.whyCN: 物理学把一般的「次数」收窄为波周期的计数，并以赫兹作单位。

senses.title: The fact of happening often
senses.titleCN: 频繁、经常发生
senses.definition: the quality of occurring often or at short intervals
senses.definitionCN: 经常发生或间隔很短的特性
senses.example: The frequency of storms along this coast has doubled in a decade.
senses.exampleCN: 这处海岸风暴的频繁程度十年间翻了一倍。
senses.why: this is the oldest layer of the word: abundance of occurrence, before any counting began.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词最古老的一层：发生得多，早于任何计数。

senses.title: A radio channel
senses.titleCN: 无线电频道所用的频率
senses.definition: a particular band of radio waves assigned to a station or a service
senses.definitionCN: 分配给某个电台或某项业务的特定无线电波段
senses.example: Rescue teams shared a single frequency during the flood.
senses.exampleCN: 洪灾期间各救援队共用同一个无线电频率。
senses.why: broadcasting needed a way to separate channels, and the separation was made by frequency.
senses.whyCN: 广播需要把频道分开，而分开的依据就是频率。

senses.title: Natural frequency
senses.titleCN: 系统的固有频率
senses.definition: the rate at which a system oscillates freely once disturbed, without any outside driving
senses.definitionCN: 系统受扰后在没有外驱动力时自由振动的频率
senses.example: The bridge collapsed because the wind matched its natural frequency.
senses.exampleCN: 桥之所以塌，是因为风的节奏与它的固有频率相合。
senses.why: a system prefers one rate above all others, so frequency becomes a property of the object itself.
senses.whyCN: 系统最偏爱某一个速率，于是频率成了物体自身的属性。

senses.title: A count in statistics
senses.titleCN: 统计中的频数
senses.definition: the number of cases falling into a particular category in a data set
senses.definitionCN: 数据集中落入某一类别的案例数量
senses.example: The frequency table shows how many scores fell in each band.
senses.exampleCN: 频数表显示出每个分数段各有多少人。
senses.why: statistics counts occurrences rather than time, but the underlying notion of how often remains.
senses.whyCN: 统计数的是出现次数而非时间，但「多久出现一次」这一底层观念不变。

senses.title: Word frequency in a corpus
senses.titleCN: 语料库中的词频
senses.definition: the number of times a word appears in a body of text, often per million words
senses.definitionCN: 某词在一批文本中出现的次数，常以每百万词计
senses.example: The frequency of this verb fell sharply after the eighteenth century.
senses.exampleCN: 这个动词的出现频率在十八世纪之后急剧下降。
senses.why: linguistics borrowed the statistical count and made it a measure of how central a word is.
senses.whyCN: 语言学借用了统计上的计数，用它衡量一个词有多核心。

senses.title: Abstract: how often something recurs in experience
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：某事物在经验中出现的疏密
senses.definition: the comparative commonness of an experience or a situation in a person life or a society
senses.definitionCN: 某种经历或情境在个人生活或社会中相对常见的程度
senses.example: The frequency of such losses is easy to underestimate.
senses.exampleCN: 这类损失发生的频繁程度很容易被低估。
senses.why: the technical count becomes a way of speaking about how much of life is made of a given event.
senses.whyCN: 技术性的计数变成了谈论「生活中有多少由某类事件构成」的方式。

intro.en: Frequency comes from Latin frequentia, a crowd or abundance, built on frequens, crowded or repeated. The physical sense dates from the nineteenth century.
intro.cn: frequency 来自拉丁 frequentia「拥挤、众多」，其形容词为 frequens「拥挤的、反复的」。物理义始于十九世纪。

items.en: Frequens meant crowded, numerous or repeated. Its deeper origin is not established, and the Indo-European links sometimes proposed for it are hypotheses.
items.cn: frequens 意为「拥挤的、众多的、反复的」。其更深来源没有定论，有时为它提出的印欧联系只是假说。

items.en: Frequentia named a crowd or an abundance, and later the repeated occurrence of an event.
items.cn: frequentia 指「人群、众多」，后来指事件的反复发生。

items.en: English took the word through French, first in the sense of common occurrence rather than of a measured rate.
items.cn: 英语经法语引入该词，最初指「常见、频繁」，而非可测量的比率。

items.en: With the study of waves and alternating current, frequency became the count of cycles per second; the hertz was adopted as its unit in 1935.
items.cn: 随着波与交流电的研究，frequency 成为每秒周期数的计数；1935 年采用赫兹作为单位。

items.en: Both fields took the same count for their own tables, one counting cases and the other counting words.
items.cn: 统计学与语言学都用同一套计数做各自的表格，一个数案例，一个数词。

items.en: Source uncertain (root and first date): the pre-Latin origin of frequens has no agreed account, so any Indo-European root offered for it is a reconstruction; the first English date is also approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（词根与首见年代）：frequens 在拉丁语之前的来源没有公认说法，凡为其提出的印欧词根均属重构形式；英语首见年代亦只是约数。

note.en: Group one holds the adjective and adverb from the same stem, which are constantly mistaken for the noun; group two holds the counting words that overlap its statistical sense.
note.cn: 第一组是同词干而来的形容词与副词，常被误当作名词；第二组是与统计义重叠的计数类词。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning happening often, or a verb meaning to visit a place often; it is not the noun for a rate.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词指「经常发生的」，动词指「常去某处」；它不是表示比率的名词。

entries.definition: The adverb meaning often; it answers how often, while frequency answers how many times per unit.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，意为「经常」；它回答多常发生，而 frequency 回答每单位时间内多少次。

entries.definition: Rare or not happening often; the noun infrequency is its matching abstract form.
entries.definitionCN: 罕见的、不常发生的；其对应名词是 infrequency。

entries.definition: The act of visiting a place often, from the verb frequent; it has nothing to do with wave rates.
entries.definitionCN: 指经常造访某地，来自动词 frequent；与波的频率无关。

entries.definition: A measure per unit of time; it is broader than frequency and needs no repetition.
entries.definitionCN: 按单位时间计的量；比 frequency 更宽，也不要求重复。

entries.definition: The number of new cases of a condition in a population over a period, a specific statistical rate.
entries.definitionCN: 某时期内人群中某状况的新发病例数，是一种特定的统计率。

entries.definition: The proportion of a population that has a condition at a given time, not how often new ones appear.
entries.definitionCN: 某一时刻人群中患某状况的比例，而不是新病例出现的频率。

entries.definition: The time one cycle takes; it is the reciprocal of frequency for a periodic wave.
entries.definitionCN: 完成一个周期所需的时间；对周期波而言是频率的倒数。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin stem, the real adjective family, and the real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁词干、真实的形容词词族，以及真实的固定搭配。

normal.en: The noun ends in -cy and the adjective ends in -t: frequency, frequent.
normal.cn: 名词以 -cy 收尾，形容词以 -t 收尾：frequency、frequent。

normal.en: Hertz is the unit: one hertz is one cycle per second.
normal.cn: 单位是赫兹：一赫兹就是每秒一个周期。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the technical uses: radio frequency, frequency band, natural frequency.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出技术义：射频、频带、固有频率。

normal.en: The opposite noun is infrequency, and the opposite adjective is infrequent.
normal.cn: 反义名词是 infrequency，反义形容词是 infrequent。

normal.en: Statistics uses a frequency table to show counts per category.
normal.cn: 统计学用频数表显示各类别的计数。

abstract.en: Picture a door that opens a fixed number of times every minute, no matter who knocks.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门每分钟固定开若干次，不管是谁来敲。

abstract.en: Picture a heartbeat monitor where the height of the trace stays the same but the spacing tells the story.
abstract.cn: 想象一台心跳监测仪，波峰高度不变，间距却在讲述一切。

abstract.en: Picture a word that keeps returning to a page until it becomes the page.
abstract.cn: 想象一个词不断回到书页，直到它自己成了那一页。

examples.en: The radio station broadcasts on a frequency of ninety-eight megahertz.
examples.cn: 这家电台以九十八兆赫的频率广播。

examples.en: The frequency of rainfall in the region has fallen since the reservoir was built.
examples.cn: 自水库建成以来，该地区降雨的频次下降了。

examples.en: A frequency count showed the word was used twice in every hundred.
examples.cn: 频数统计显示这个词每一百个词中出现两次。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「frequent（频繁的）+ cy」——一段时间里出现得有多频繁 → 频率、频次

root: 拉丁 frequens「拥挤的、反复的」（属格 frequentis）+ 名词后缀 -ia → frequentia「众多、频繁」；frequens 的更深来源不确定。英语 frequency。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses start from a plain count of repetitions, then narrow to cycles per second, widen back to the everyday sense of often, and pass through radio, resonance, statistics and corpus counts before ending as a figure for how life recurs.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从朴素的「重复次数」开始，收窄为每秒周期数，又回到日常的「经常」，再经过无线电、共振、统计与语料计数，最后成为经验重复疏密的比喻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a counter ticking once per cycle while the pointer holds steady.
core.cn: 核心意象：计数器每完成一个周期跳一下，指针稳稳不动。

branches.en: THE PLAIN COUNT: repetitions divided by time is the trunk from which the other senses branch.
branches.cn: 朴素计数：重复次数除以时间，是其余义项分枝的树干。

branches.en: WAVE AND RESONANCE: cycles per second, and the rate an object prefers of its own accord.
branches.cn: 波与共振：每秒周期数，以及物体自身偏爱的那个速率。

branches.en: OFTENNESS: the oldest and the most abstract layers both speak of recurrence without a stopwatch.
branches.cn: 经常性：最古老与最抽象的两层，都在没有秒表的情况下谈重复。

branches.en: CHANNEL SEPARATION: broadcasting turns a physical number into an address.
branches.cn: 频道分隔：广播把一个物理数字变成了一个地址。

branches.en: COUNTING TABLES: statistics and linguistics keep only the tally, one for cases and one for words.
branches.cn: 计数表：统计与语言学只留下计数，一个数案例，一个数词。

intro.en: Frequency is an abstract noun from a Latin adjective, and the same stem gives the adjective, the adverb and the negative forms.
intro.cn: frequency 是由拉丁形容词派生的抽象名词，同一词干还给出形容词、副词与否定形式。

latinIntro.en: Latin frequens, genitive frequentis, gives frequentia; English added -cy to the Latin stem, and -ly and in- to the English adjective.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 frequens（属格 frequentis）给出 frequentia；英语在拉丁词干上加 -cy，又在英语形容词上加 -ly 与 in-。

items.example: Frequent storms shaped the coast.
items.exampleCN: 频繁的风暴塑造了这处海岸。

items.example: The frequency rose to fifty hertz.
items.exampleCN: 频率升到了五十赫兹。

items.example: The sensor fails frequently.
items.exampleCN: 这个传感器经常失灵。

items.example: Such floods are infrequent here.
items.exampleCN: 这样的洪水在这里并不常见。

items.example: The infrequency of the event makes it hard to study.
items.exampleCN: 这一事件极少发生，因此难以研究。

items.example: The device listens across a wide frequency band.
items.exampleCN: 该装置监听一段很宽的频带。

items.meaning: the frequency range used for radio
items.meaningCN: 无线电所用的频率范围
items.example: The tag answers on a radio frequency.
items.exampleCN: 标签在一个无线电频率上应答。

items.example: The wind matched the natural frequency of the bridge.
items.exampleCN: 风与桥的固有频率相合。

items.meaning: the unit of frequency, one cycle per second
items.meaningCN: 频率单位，每秒一个周期
items.example: The tone is four hundred hertz.
items.exampleCN: 这个音是四百赫兹。

definition_zh: 电磁的；由电与磁共同产生的；涉及电磁场的
definition_en: relating to the combined effects of electricity and magnetism, or produced by an electromagnetic field
core_image: 线圈通电的一瞬，旁边的铁屑立刻排成放射状花纹，方向随电流反转而翻转
scene: 线圈通电的瞬间，旁边的铁屑立刻排成放射状花纹，方向随电流反转而翻转。A coil carrying current creates an electromagnetic field that lifts the iron filings.
sceneCN: 这里 electromagnetic 指「同时涉及电与磁两种作用的」（第 1 个义项：由电流与磁场共同产生或相关的）；句意为通电线圈产生电磁场，把铁屑吸起。可辨识物件：线圈、铁屑、电源、放射状花纹。

pos.zh: 电磁的；由电与磁共同产生的

senses.title: Involving electricity and magnetism together
senses.titleCN: 同时涉及电与磁两种作用
senses.definition: relating to the combined action of electric currents and magnetic fields, which are two sides of one phenomenon
senses.definitionCN: 涉及电流与磁场共同作用的，二者是同一现象的两面
senses.example: A coil carrying current creates an electromagnetic field that lifts the iron filings.
senses.exampleCN: 通电线圈产生电磁场，把铁屑吸起。
senses.why: the word joins electro-, from Greek amber, to magnetic, from Magnesia, because the two effects turned out to be one.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把出自希腊「琥珀」的词根 electro- 与出自小亚细亚地名「马格尼西亚」的词根 magnet- 拼在一起，因为两种效应后来被证明是一回事。

senses.title: A wave of coupled fields
senses.titleCN: 电场与磁场互相激发而成的波
senses.definition: describing a wave in which a changing electric field and a changing magnetic field sustain each other through space
senses.definitionCN: 描述变化的电场与变化的磁场在空间中彼此维持而形成的波
senses.example: Light is an electromagnetic wave, which is why it needs no medium.
senses.exampleCN: 光是电磁波，这正是它不需要介质的原因。
senses.why: Maxwell showed that a changing field generates the other, so radiation became electromagnetic by definition.
senses.whyCN: 麦克斯韦证明变化的场会激发另一种场，于是辐射在定义上成了「电磁的」。

senses.title: A field in space
senses.titleCN: 空间中存在的电磁场
senses.definition: the region around a charge or a current in which electric and magnetic forces can be detected
senses.definitionCN: 电荷或电流周围可以测到电与磁作用力的区域
senses.example: The antenna measures the electromagnetic field of the passing pulse.
senses.exampleCN: 天线测量经过脉冲的电磁场。
senses.why: field language replaced action at a distance, and the adjective named the single field that carries both effects.
senses.whyCN: 场的说法取代了超距作用，这个形容词命名的正是同时承载两种效应的那个场。

senses.title: One of the fundamental forces
senses.titleCN: 四种基本相互作用之一
senses.definition: the force carried by photons that acts between charged particles
senses.definitionCN: 由光子传递、作用于带电粒子之间的力
senses.example: The electromagnetic force holds the electrons around the nucleus.
senses.exampleCN: 电磁力把电子束缚在原子核周围。
senses.why: once light was understood as a field, the force behind chemistry and light could be named with the same adjective.
senses.whyCN: 一旦光被理解为场，支撑化学与光的那股力就可以用同一个形容词命名。

senses.title: Induction
senses.titleCN: 电磁感应：变化的磁通量产生电流
senses.definition: describing the production of an electric current by a changing magnetic flux, as in a generator or a transformer
senses.definitionCN: 描述变化的磁通量产生电流，如发电机或变压器中的情形
senses.example: The bicycle dynamo works by electromagnetic induction.
senses.exampleCN: 自行车发电机靠电磁感应工作。
senses.why: Faraday found that a moving magnet pushes charges, so the pair of effects gained a name for the conversion itself.
senses.whyCN: 法拉第发现移动的磁体能推动电荷，于是这对效应有了一个专指这种转换的名称。

senses.title: Of the whole spectrum
senses.titleCN: 整个电磁波谱的
senses.definition: covering all wavelengths of radiation, from radio waves to gamma rays, seen as one continuous family
senses.definitionCN: 涵盖从无线电波到伽马射线的全部辐射波长，被视作一个连续家族
senses.example: The chart lays out the electromagnetic spectrum from long radio waves to short gamma rays.
senses.exampleCN: 这张图把电磁波谱从长波无线电排到短波伽马射线。
senses.why: the adjective turns a collection of apparently different radiations into a single ordered range.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词把一批看似不同的辐射收束成一个有次序的单一范围。

senses.title: Of a sudden burst of energy
senses.titleCN: 电磁脉冲式的突然能量爆发
senses.definition: describing a brief intense pulse of electromagnetic energy that can damage electronics
senses.definitionCN: 描述短暂而强烈的电磁能量脉冲，足以损坏电子设备
senses.example: The test simulated an electromagnetic pulse over the city.
senses.exampleCN: 该试验模拟了一次覆盖全城的电磁脉冲。
senses.why: a pulse is only a short packet of the same field, so no new word was needed for it.
senses.whyCN: 脉冲不过是同一个场的一小段，因此不需要为它另造新词。

senses.title: Of shielding
senses.titleCN: 电磁屏蔽的：隔绝电磁场的
senses.definition: describing a barrier or enclosure that keeps electromagnetic fields from entering or leaving
senses.definitionCN: 描述阻止电磁场进入或逸出的屏障或外壳
senses.example: The room has electromagnetic shielding on every wall.
senses.exampleCN: 这个房间四面墙都有电磁屏蔽。
senses.why: shielding names what the field cannot pass through, and the adjective simply marks the kind of field involved.
senses.whyCN: 屏蔽指场无法穿过的障碍，这个形容词只标出所涉的场属于哪一类。

intro.en: Electromagnetic joins electro-, from Greek elektron amber, with magnetic, from Greek Magnesia, the region whose stone attracted iron. The compound dates from the 1820s.
intro.cn: electromagnetic 把出自希腊 elektron「琥珀」的 electro- 与出自小亚细亚地名「马格尼西亚」的 magnet- 拼在一起，那里产的石头能吸铁。复合词出现于 1820 年代。

items.en: Elektron named amber; rubbing it produced the attraction that later became electricity. Latin took the same word as electrum.
items.cn: elektron 指琥珀；摩擦琥珀产生的吸引现象后来成了「电」。拉丁语以 electrum 借入此词。

items.en: Magnes lithos meant the stone of Magnesia, a region of Asia Minor; Latin magnes named the lodestone.
items.cn: magnes lithos 指「马格尼西亚之石」，马格尼西亚是小亚细亚的一个地区；拉丁 magnes 指天然磁石。

items.en: Latin kept electrum for amber and magnes for the magnet, and both supplied the roots of the later European terms.
items.cn: 拉丁语保留 electrum 指琥珀、magnes 指磁石，二者共同提供了后来欧洲各语言术语的词根。

items.en: Oersted showed that a current deflects a compass needle, and the link between electricity and magnetism became experimental fact.
items.cn: 厄斯泰德证明电流能使指南针偏转，电与磁的联系由此成为实验事实。

items.en: The adjective electromagnetic appeared in English shortly after, built by adding -ic to the noun electromagnet.
items.cn: 形容词 electromagnetic 随即在英语中出现，是在名词 electromagnet 后加 -ic 构成。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and deeper origin): the exact first English use of the adjective is not agreed, and the deeper origin of Greek elektron is unsettled, so any proposed Indo-European source is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与更深词源）：该形容词的确切英语首用无定论；希腊 elektron 的更深来源亦无定论，凡提出的印欧来源均属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds the neighbouring technical adjectives whose difference is easy to miss; group two holds the plainer words that name the two component effects separately.
note.cn: 第一组是差别容易被忽略的相邻技术形容词；第二组是把两种成分作用分开说的朴素词。

entries.definition: Concerns electric charge and current alone; it says nothing about the magnetic half of the phenomenon.
entries.definitionCN: 只涉及电荷与电流；不涉及该现象中磁的那一半。

entries.definition: Describes circuits that control electrons, as in electronic music or electronic mail; it is not a field term.
entries.definitionCN: 描述控制电子的电路，如电子音乐或电子邮件；它不是场论术语。

entries.definition: Concerns magnets and magnetic fields alone; the electric half is absent.
entries.definitionCN: 只涉及磁体与磁场；缺少电的那一半。

entries.definition: Concerns charges that are not moving, so no magnetic field arises.
entries.definitionCN: 涉及静止的电荷，因此不产生磁场。

entries.definition: A coil with an iron core that becomes magnetic when current flows; the adjective describes its field, the noun names the thing.
entries.definitionCN: 通电后带磁性的铁芯线圈；形容词描述它的场，名词指这件东西。

entries.definition: The whole phenomenon of attraction and repulsion between magnetic poles.
entries.definitionCN: 磁极之间吸引与排斥的整个现象。

entries.definition: The phenomenon of charge and current, named from the same amber root.
entries.definitionCN: 电荷与电流的现象，同样出自「琥珀」这个词根。
