entries.definition: Joins electricity with mechanical parts, as in a relay; it does not name a field.
entries.definitionCN: 把电与机械部件结合，如继电器；它不指场。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the two real Greek place-and-substance roots and the real historical experiment.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：两个真实的希腊语「物与地」词根，以及真实的史料记载实验。

normal.en: Electro- comes from amber and magnetic- comes from Magnesia; two souvenir words became one science.
normal.cn: electro- 出自琥珀，magnet- 出自马格尼西亚；两个「地名物名」成了一个学科。

normal.en: The noun is electromagnetism, the object is an electromagnet, and the adverb is electromagnetically.
normal.cn: 名词是 electromagnetism，物件是 electromagnet，副词是 electromagnetically。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the physics: field, wave, spectrum, force, induction.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出物理内容：场、波、谱、力、感应。

normal.en: Oersted 1820 is the experiment: a current moved a compass needle.
normal.cn: 1820 年厄斯泰德的实验：电流让指南针动了。

normal.en: The word always keeps both halves: electric and magnetic are not alternatives.
normal.cn: 这个词始终保留两半：电与磁并非二者择一。

abstract.en: Picture two invisible hands that only move when the other moves first.
abstract.cn: 想象两只看不见的手，只有另一只先动，这只才动。

abstract.en: Picture a field that fills a room without anything visible in it.
abstract.cn: 想象一个充满房间却看不见任何东西的场。

abstract.en: Picture a switch that turns a piece of iron into a magnet and back again.
abstract.cn: 想象一个开关，能把一块铁变成磁体，又能变回去。

examples.en: Visible light occupies only a small part of the electromagnetic spectrum.
examples.cn: 可见光只占电磁波谱的一小部分。

examples.en: The relay is held closed by an electromagnetic coil.
examples.cn: 继电器由一个电磁线圈保持闭合。

examples.en: Electromagnetic induction is the principle behind every generator.
examples.cn: 电磁感应是每一台发电机的原理。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「electro（电）+ magnetic（磁）」——电与磁合在一起 → 电磁的

root: 希腊 elektron「琥珀」（拉丁 electrum）+ 希腊 Magnes「马格尼西亚之石」（拉丁 magnes）+ 形容词后缀 -ic；两词的更深来源均不确定。英语 electromagnetic。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run from the bare pairing of two effects to the wave, the field, the force, induction, the whole spectrum, a pulse and a shield.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从两种效应的并列开始，依次走向波、场、力、感应、整个波谱、脉冲与屏蔽。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a current in a coil that instantly arranges iron filings into a pattern.
core.cn: 核心意象：线圈中的电流一通过，铁屑立刻排成花纹。

branches.en: THE PAIRING: electricity and magnetism are named together because they never act alone.
branches.cn: 成对出现：电与磁被并称，因为它们从不单独起作用。

branches.en: FIELD AND WAVE: a changing field makes the other, and the pair travels as a wave.
branches.cn: 场与波：变化的场激发另一种场，二者以波的形式传播。

branches.en: FORCE: the same interaction that binds electrons is one of the four fundamental forces.
branches.cn: 力：束缚电子的那种相互作用，正是四种基本力之一。

branches.en: CONVERSION: a moving magnet pushes charges, which is induction.
branches.cn: 转换：移动的磁体推动电荷，这就是感应。

branches.en: RANGE, BURST AND BARRIER: the whole spectrum, a short pulse and a shield are three ways of bounding the same field.
branches.cn: 范围、爆发与屏障：整个波谱、一段短脉冲与一层屏蔽，是给同一个场划界的三种方式。

intro.en: Electromagnetic is a compound adjective, and its two roots each bring their own small family of English words.
intro.cn: electromagnetic 是复合形容词，两个词根各自带来一小族英语词。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies electrum for amber and magnes for the lodestone; Greek supplies elektron and Magnes. The scientific compounds are modern.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁以 electrum 指琥珀、magnes 指磁石；希腊语提供 elektron 与 Magnes。科学复合词是近代形成的。

items.example: The prefix ties the word to electric charge.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把词系在电荷上。

items.example: The magnetic half supplies attraction.
items.exampleCN: 磁的那一半提供吸引。

items.example: A coil creates an electromagnetic field.
items.exampleCN: 线圈产生电磁场。

items.meaning: the unified phenomenon and its science
items.meaningCN: 统一的电磁现象及其学科
items.example: Electromagnetism governs chemistry.
items.exampleCN: 电磁作用支配着化学。

items.example: The crane lifted the scrap with an electromagnet.
items.exampleCN: 吊车用电磁铁吸起废钢。

items.example: The shutter is released electromagnetically.
items.exampleCN: 快门以电磁方式释放。

items.meaningCN: 同时承载两种效应的场
items.example: The probe mapped the electromagnetic field.
items.exampleCN: 探头绘出了电磁场。

items.example: The electromagnetic force binds the atom.
items.exampleCN: 电磁力把原子结合在一起。

items.example: Radio sits at one end of the electromagnetic spectrum.
items.exampleCN: 无线电位于电磁波谱的一端。

latinEntries.meaning: amber; also a natural alloy of gold and silver
latinEntries.meaningCN: 琥珀；亦指金银天然合金

latinEntries.meaning: of amber; producing attraction when rubbed
latinEntries.meaningCN: 琥珀的；摩擦后产生吸引的

definition_zh: 电磁辐射；以电磁波形式在空间传播的能量
definition_en: energy that travels through space as oscillating electric and magnetic fields, from radio waves to gamma rays
core_image: 炉火热意隔空传到手背，看不见的能量不靠空气流动也能穿过空处
scene: 炉火把热送到房间各处，这种看不见的能量不靠空气流动也能穿过空处。A warm stove sends electromagnetic radiation across the room in the form of heat.
sceneCN: 这里 electromagnetic radiation 指「以电磁波形式传播的能量」（第 1 个义项：由交变电场与磁场共同承载并可在空间中行进的能量）；句意为温暖的火炉以热的形式向房间发出电磁辐射。可辨识物件：炉火、空荡的房间、手背、热气。

pos.zh: 电磁辐射（不可数，技术用语）

forms.label: 罕用复数（指多束或多种辐射）

senses.title: Energy carried by coupled fields
senses.titleCN: 由交变电场与磁场共同承载的能量
senses.definition: energy travelling through space as electric and magnetic fields that oscillate at right angles to each other
senses.definitionCN: 以互相垂直振动的电场与磁场在空间中行进的能量
senses.example: A warm stove sends electromagnetic radiation across the room in the form of heat.
senses.exampleCN: 温暖的火炉以热的形式向房间发出电磁辐射。
senses.why: the phrase names the carrier, not the source: the energy rides on two fields that keep regenerating each other.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语命名的是载体而非来源：能量骑在两个彼此不断再生的场上。

senses.title: The whole family of waves
senses.titleCN: 从无线电波到伽马射线的整个家族
senses.definition: the complete set of radiations ordered by wavelength, including radio, microwave, infrared, visible, ultraviolet, X-ray and gamma
senses.definitionCN: 按波长排列的全部辐射，包括无线电、微波、红外、可见光、紫外、X 射线与伽马射线
senses.example: The poster plots electromagnetic radiation from long radio waves to short gamma rays.
senses.exampleCN: 这张海报把电磁辐射从长波无线电排到短波伽马射线。
senses.why: one phrase covers radiations that behave very differently, because the underlying mechanism is identical.
senses.whyCN: 一个短语涵盖了行为差别很大的各种辐射，因为其底层机制完全相同。

senses.title: Heat from a warm body
senses.titleCN: 物体因温度而发出的热辐射
senses.definition: the radiation emitted by any object above absolute zero, whose spectrum and intensity depend on its temperature
senses.definitionCN: 任何高于绝对零度的物体所发出的辐射，其谱与强度取决于温度
senses.example: The kettle loses heat mainly through electromagnetic radiation from its surface.
senses.exampleCN: 水壶主要通过表面发出的电磁辐射散失热量。
senses.why: thermal radiation is just the infrared part of the family, so everyday heat is already electromagnetic.
senses.whyCN: 热辐射只是这个家族中的红外部分，因此日常的「热」本身就已经是电磁的。

senses.title: Radiation reaching Earth from the sun
senses.titleCN: 由太阳到达地球的辐射
senses.definition: the solar energy that passes through space and the atmosphere to warm the surface and drive weather
senses.definitionCN: 穿过太空与大气到达地表、加热地面并驱动天气的太阳能
senses.example: Most electromagnetic radiation reaching the ground arrives as visible light and infrared.
senses.exampleCN: 到达地面的电磁辐射大部分以可见光与红外形式出现。
senses.why: the atmosphere filters the family unevenly, so what arrives is a selection rather than the whole set.
senses.whyCN: 大气对家族中各成员过滤不均，因此到达的只是一部分，而非全部。

senses.title: Radiation as a hazard
senses.titleCN: 作为危害的辐射剂量
senses.definition: the amount of radiation absorbed by a body, especially the high-energy part that can damage tissue
senses.definitionCN: 物体所吸收的辐射量，尤指能损伤组织的高能部分
senses.example: The badge records the electromagnetic radiation dose each worker receives.
senses.exampleCN: 这枚徽章记录每位工作者受到的电磁辐射剂量。
senses.why: the same phrase shifts from carrier to risk once energy is high enough to break chemical bonds.
senses.whyCN: 当能量高到足以打断化学键时，同一短语就从「载体」转向「风险」。

senses.title: Radiation pressure
senses.titleCN: 辐射压：光对表面施加的微小推力
senses.definition: the small pressure that radiation exerts on a surface when its photons carry momentum
senses.definitionCN: 光子携带动量时，辐射对表面施加的微小压力
senses.example: Electromagnetic radiation pressure pushes the sail of a solar probe.
senses.exampleCN: 电磁辐射压推动太阳探测器的帆。
senses.why: momentum in the field turns radiation from a mere messenger into something that can push.
senses.whyCN: 场中的动量把辐射从单纯的传递者变成了能推东西的东西。

senses.title: Emission from an antenna
senses.titleCN: 天线发出的无线电辐射
senses.definition: the radio-frequency radiation launched into space when an antenna is driven by an alternating current
senses.definitionCN: 天线被交变电流驱动时向空间发出的射频辐射
senses.example: The tower launches electromagnetic radiation at a narrow band.
senses.exampleCN: 这座塔在窄频带上发出电磁辐射。
senses.why: radio is simply the longest member of the same family, generated by moving charges in a conductor.
senses.whyCN: 无线电只是同一家族中最长的成员，由导体中运动的电荷产生。

senses.title: Abstract: invisible influence spreading outward
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：无形影响向外扩散
senses.definition: any influence that spreads outward from a source without a visible carrier and reaches things at a distance
senses.definitionCN: 任何从源头向外扩散、没有可见载体却能抵达远处之物的影响
senses.example: Rumour behaves like electromagnetic radiation, travelling without a wire.
senses.exampleCN: 谣言就像电磁辐射，不用导线也能传播。
senses.why: the abstract sense keeps only the geometry: a centre, a spreading field and effects felt at a distance.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义只保留几何关系：一个中心、一片扩散的场，以及远处感受到的效果。

intro.en: The phrase is modern: electromagnetic is an 1820s compound, and radiation comes from Latin radiare, to emit rays, from radius, a ray or spoke.
intro.cn: 这个短语是近代的：electromagnetic 是 1820 年代的复合词，radiation 来自拉丁 radiare「发出光线」，其词根 radius 意为「光线、辐条」。

items.en: Radius meant a ray of light or the spoke of a wheel, and radiare meant to emit rays or to shine.
items.cn: radius 指光线或车轮的辐条，radiare 指发出光线或闪耀。

items.en: Radiatio named a shining or a beam, and English radiation entered through French with that optical sense.
items.cn: radiatio 指「发光、光束」，英语 radiation 经法语引入，带着这一光学含义。

items.en: Maxwell showed that light is an oscillation of electric and magnetic fields, so radiation could be called electromagnetic.
items.cn: 麦克斯韦证明光是电场与磁场的振荡，因此辐射可以称为「电磁的」。

items.en: Hertz produced and detected radio waves, proving that the electromagnetic family extends beyond visible light.
items.cn: 赫兹产生并探测到无线电波，证明电磁家族延伸到可见光之外。

items.en: The phrase became standard in physics, medicine and engineering as the neutral name for the whole family.
items.cn: 20 世纪，这一短语成为物理学、医学与工程中称呼整个家族的中性名称。

items.en: Source uncertain (coinage date and deeper origin): the first use of the exact phrase is not fixed, and the deeper origin of Latin radius is unsettled, so any Indo-European root proposed for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（成词年代与更深词源）：这一确切短语的首用无定论；拉丁 radius 的更深来源亦无定论，凡为其提出的印欧词根均属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds phrases that name neighbouring parts of the same physics; group two holds common names for particular members of the family.
note.cn: 第一组是命名同一物理相邻概念的短语；第二组是家族中某些成员的通称。

entries.definition: The wave is the shape the radiation takes; radiation is the energy that the wave carries.
entries.definitionCN: 波是辐射所取的形式，辐射是波所携带的能量。

entries.definition: The field is the condition of space around charges; radiation is that condition propagating away.
entries.definitionCN: 场是电荷周围空间的状态，辐射则是这种状态向外传播。

entries.definition: The spectrum is the ordered range of wavelengths, not the energy that travels.
entries.definitionCN: 波谱是按波长排好的范围，不是行进中的能量。

entries.definition: A brief intense burst of the same radiation, usually named for its effect on electronics.
entries.definitionCN: 同一辐射短暂而强烈的爆发，通常以其对电子设备的影响得名。

entries.definition: The infrared emission of warm objects, a subset of electromagnetic radiation.
entries.definitionCN: 温热物体发出的红外辐射，是电磁辐射的一个子集。

entries.definition: The narrow band the eye can see; it is one member of the family, not the whole.
entries.definitionCN: 肉眼能看到的那一窄段；它是家族中的一员，而非全部。

entries.definition: The longest waves used for communication, a low-energy part of the same radiation.
entries.definitionCN: 用于通信的最长波，是同一辐射中的低能部分。

entries.definition: The shortest, most energetic radiation, emitted by nuclear processes.
entries.definitionCN: 最短、能量最高的辐射，由核过程发出。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the two real roots, the real discoverers and the real named members of the family.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：两个真实词根、真实的发现者，以及家族中真实有名字的成员。

normal.en: Radiation comes from radius, a ray, so the word already says rays going out.
normal.cn: radiation 出自 radius「光线」，词本身就在说「光线向外发出」。

normal.en: The family runs radio, microwave, infrared, visible, ultraviolet, X-ray, gamma.
normal.cn: 这个家族依次是无线电、微波、红外、可见光、紫外、X 射线、伽马射线。

normal.en: Maxwell predicted it and Hertz detected it.
normal.cn: 麦克斯韦预言了它，赫兹探测到了它。

normal.en: The phrase is uncountable: one speaks of electromagnetic radiation, not of a radiation.
normal.cn: 这个短语不可数：可以整体使用该术语，却不能加不定冠词。

normal.en: Every warm object radiates; the kettle, the wall and the human body all emit it.
normal.cn: 每个温热物体都在辐射；水壶、墙壁与人体都会发出它。

abstract.en: Picture warmth arriving with nothing visible in between.
abstract.cn: 想象暖意抵达，而中间空无一物可见。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp whose light keeps going after the lamp is switched off, only weaker.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏灯关掉之后光还在走，只是变弱了。

abstract.en: Picture news spreading through a town without anyone carrying a note.
abstract.cn: 想象消息在全城传开，却没有人拿着纸条。

examples.en: The ozone layer absorbs most of the harmful electromagnetic radiation from the sun.
examples.cn: 臭氧层吸收了来自太阳的大部分有害电磁辐射。

examples.en: A black body is a perfect absorber of electromagnetic radiation at every wavelength.
examples.cn: 黑体能在所有波长上完美吸收电磁辐射。

examples.en: The satellite measures electromagnetic radiation reflected from the ocean surface.
examples.cn: 这颗卫星测量海面反射的电磁辐射。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「electromagnetic（电磁的）+ radiation（辐射）」——电磁场向外送出的能量 → 电磁辐射

root: electromagnetic（希腊 elektron「琥珀」+ Magnes「马格尼西亚之石」）+ radiation（拉丁 radiare「发出光线」，出自 radius「光线、辐条」）；两词的更深来源均不确定。英语 electromagnetic radiation。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses begin with the carrier fields, take in the whole family, then narrow to heat, sunlight, dose and pressure, then to an antenna, and end as a figure for influence without a wire.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从承载它的场开始，收进整个家族，再依次收窄到热、日光、剂量与辐射压，随后到天线，最后成为「不用导线的影响」这一比喻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an invisible stream leaving a warm surface and reaching a distant hand.
core.cn: 核心意象：一股看不见的流离开温热的表面，抵达远处的手。

branches.en: CARRIER AND RANGE: one mechanism, many wavelengths, from radio to gamma.
branches.cn: 载体与范围：一种机制，许多波长，从雷达到伽马。

branches.en: WARMTH AND DAYLIGHT: the two forms people meet without a laboratory.
branches.cn: 温暖与日光：人们不必进实验室就会遇见的两种形式。

branches.en: RISK AND PUSH: high energy damages tissue, and momentum presses on a surface.
branches.cn: 风险与推力：高能量损伤组织，动量则压在表面上。

branches.en: ENGINEERED SOURCE: an antenna turns a current into radiation on purpose.
branches.cn: 人造源：天线有意把电流变成辐射。

branches.en: METAPHOR: any influence that spreads from a centre without a visible carrier.
branches.cn: 比喻：任何从中心扩散、没有可见载体的影响。

intro.en: The phrase is two words, each analysable: a compound adjective and a Latin-derived noun.
intro.cn: 这个短语由两个词组成，各自可分析：一个复合形容词与一个拉丁派生的名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin contributes radius, radiare and radiatio; Greek contributes elektron and Magnes through the first word. Radiation is the noun half.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁部分提供 radius、radiare 与 radiatio；希腊部分经第一个词提供 elektron 与 Magnes。radiation 是名词那一半。

items.meaning: to send out rays or energy
items.example: The heater radiates warmth in all directions.
items.exampleCN: 取暖器向四面八方散发热量。

items.meaning: the sending out of rays; the rays themselves
items.meaningCN: 光线的发出；所发出的射线本身
items.example: The wall blocks most of the radiation.
items.exampleCN: 这堵墙挡住了大部分辐射。

items.meaning: relating to or caused by radiation
items.example: Radiative cooling chills the desert at night.
items.exampleCN: 辐射冷却使沙漠夜间变冷。

items.example: The radiator warmed the whole room.
items.exampleCN: 散热器把整个房间暖了起来。

items.example: The coil makes an electromagnetic field.
items.exampleCN: 线圈产生电磁场。

items.meaning: sending out light or heat; bright
items.example: The radiant panel heated the ceiling.
items.exampleCN: 辐射板把天花板加热了。

items.example: The seeds were irradiated to kill pests.
items.exampleCN: 种子经辐射处理以杀死害虫。

items.meaningCN: 由不稳定原子核发出辐射的
items.example: The sample is weakly radioactive.
items.exampleCN: 这个样品放射性很弱。

items.structure: X + ray (compound noun, translation of German)
items.meaning: a high-energy form of electromagnetic radiation
items.example: The X-ray passed through the soft tissue.
items.exampleCN: X 射线穿过了软组织。

latinEntries.meaning: a ray of light; a spoke

definition_zh: 红外线的；红外区的；红外辐射（不可数）
definition_en: relating to the band of radiation just beyond the red end of the visible spectrum, felt as heat
core_image: 夜里的热成像仪把人形轮廓染成橙红色，肉眼看不见的暖意显了形
scene: 停电的暗室里，热成像仪把人体轮廓染成橙红色，肉眼看不见的暖意显了形。A thermal camera reads the infrared that a warm body emits in a dark room.
sceneCN: 这里 infrared 指「波长比红光更长、肉眼看不见的那段辐射」（第 1 个义项：位于可见光谱红端之外的长波辐射）；句意为暗室中热成像仪读取温暖人体发出的红外线。可辨识物件：热成像屏、人形轮廓、暗室、橙红色块。

pos.zh: 红外的；红外区的
红外线；红外辐射（不可数）

forms.label: 名词（红外线；红外辐射，不可数）

senses.title: The band beyond red
senses.titleCN: 红光之外的那段不可见辐射
senses.definition: the region of the electromagnetic spectrum with wavelengths longer than visible red but shorter than microwaves
senses.definitionCN: 电磁波谱中波长比可见红光更长、比微波更短的那一段
senses.example: A thermal camera reads the infrared that a warm body emits in a dark room.
senses.exampleCN: 暗室中，热成像仪读取温暖人体发出的红外线。
senses.why: infra- means below, so the name places this band below red on the ordered scale of colours.
senses.whyCN: infra- 意为「在下方」，因此这个名字把这一段放在颜色次序中红的下面。

senses.title: Infrared radiation as heat
senses.titleCN: 作为热量的红外辐射
senses.definition: the invisible radiation that warm objects emit and that is felt as radiant heat
senses.definitionCN: 温热物体发出、可被感受为辐射热的不可见辐射
senses.example: The fire warms the room mostly through infrared radiation.
senses.exampleCN: 炉火主要靠红外辐射把房间烘暖。
senses.why: every object at ordinary temperature peaks in this band, so this is the radiation people actually feel as warmth.
senses.whyCN: 普通温度下的物体大多在这一波段辐射最强，因此人们实际感到的暖意正是这种辐射。

senses.title: Thermal imaging
senses.titleCN: 热成像：把红外转成可见图像
senses.definition: the use of infrared detectors to build a picture of temperature differences, as in night vision or fault finding
senses.definitionCN: 用红外探测器把温差转成图像，如夜视或故障排查
senses.example: Infrared imaging showed where the wall was losing heat.
senses.exampleCN: 红外成像显示出墙体在哪里散失热量。
senses.why: a detector can translate an invisible band into a visible picture, so the word comes to name the technique.
senses.whyCN: 探测器能把不可见波段转成可见图像，于是这个词也指这项技术。

senses.title: Remote control signals
senses.titleCN: 红外遥控所用的信号
senses.definition: the pulsed infrared light that a hand-held control sends to a receiver a few metres away
senses.definitionCN: 手持遥控器向几米外接收器发送的脉冲红外光
senses.example: Infrared remote control works only when nothing blocks the beam.
senses.exampleCN: 红外遥控只有光束不被挡住时才有效。
senses.why: the band is invisible and cheap to generate, which makes it ideal for short line-of-sight commands.
senses.whyCN: 这一段不可见且易于产生，因此很适合作短距离、需直视的指令传输。

senses.title: Infrared astronomy
senses.titleCN: 红外天文学：观测冷天体与尘埃
senses.definition: the observation of celestial objects through their infrared emission, which penetrates dust that hides visible light
senses.definitionCN: 借天体红外辐射进行观测，可穿透遮挡可见光的尘埃
senses.example: Infrared astronomy revealed stars still forming inside dark clouds.
senses.exampleCN: 红外天文学揭示出仍在暗云中形成的恒星。
senses.why: cool objects and dust-shrouded regions glow mainly in this band, so astronomy needs it to see what visible light cannot.
senses.whyCN: 冷天体与被尘埃包裹的区域主要在这一波段发光，因此天文学需要它来看到可见光看不到的东西。

senses.title: Infrared spectroscopy
senses.titleCN: 红外光谱法：读分子振动
senses.definition: the use of infrared absorption bands to identify chemical bonds and molecular structure
senses.definitionCN: 利用红外吸收带识别化学键与分子结构
senses.example: Infrared spectroscopy identifies the functional groups in a sample.
senses.exampleCN: 红外光谱法能识别样品中的官能团。
senses.why: infrared photons have just the energies that stretch and bend bonds, so this band reads structure.
senses.whyCN: 红外光子的能量正好能让化学键伸缩与弯曲，因此这一段读的是结构。

senses.title: Near and far subdivisions
senses.titleCN: 近红外与远红外的分区
senses.definition: the division of the band into near infrared, closest to visible light, and far infrared, closest to microwaves
senses.definitionCN: 把该波段分为靠近可见光的近红外与靠近微波的远红外
senses.example: Near infrared penetrates fog better than visible light does.
senses.exampleCN: 近红外穿透雾的能力强于可见光。
senses.why: a broad band needed subdivisions, and they are named by distance from the visible edge.
senses.whyCN: 一段宽波段需要再分，分区便按离可见光边缘的远近命名。

senses.title: Infrared heating
senses.titleCN: 红外加热：直接辐射受热体
senses.definition: heating by directing infrared radiation at an object so that its surface warms without heating the air first
senses.definitionCN: 把红外辐射直接投向物体，使表面升温而不必先加热空气
senses.example: An infrared heater warms the terrace without warming the air around it.
senses.exampleCN: 红外取暖器把露台烘暖，却不加热周围空气。
senses.why: radiant heat can be aimed like light, so the adjective names a whole method of warming.
senses.whyCN: 辐射热可以像光一样瞄准，因此这个形容词命名了一整套加热方式。

intro.en: Infrared is a Latin-English hybrid: infra, below, plus the English colour word red. It was coined in the 1870s, after invisible radiation beyond red was measured.
intro.cn: infrared 是拉丁与英语的混合词：拉丁 infra「在下方」加英语颜色词 red。它于 1870 年代、在红光之外不可见辐射被测量之后出现。

items.en: Infra meant below or beneath, and English uses it as the prefix infra-, as in infrastructure and infrasonic.
items.cn: infra 意为「在下方、在下」，英语以 infra- 作前缀，如 infrastructure 与 infrasonic。

items.en: Red is a native English colour word from Old English read; it is cognate with Latin ruber but not borrowed from it.
items.cn: red 是古英语 read 而来的本族颜色词；它与拉丁 ruber 同源，但并非借自拉丁。

items.en: Herschel placed a thermometer beyond the red end of a prism spectrum and found it warmed, proving radiation beyond visible red.
items.cn: 赫歇尔把温度计放在棱镜光谱红端之外，发现那里变热，从而证明红光之外还有辐射。

items.en: The English term infrared was formed in the 1870s, once the measurement needed a name; earlier writers used ultra-red.
items.cn: 英语 infrared 于 1870 年代成形，因为测量结果需要一个名字；更早的作者用过 ultra-red。

items.en: Thermal imaging, remote controls and infrared spectroscopy all date from the twentieth century and widened the word.
items.cn: 热成像、遥控与红外光谱法都出现在 20 世纪，扩展了这个词的使用范围。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date only): the exact first use of infrared is not agreed and ultra-red competed with it; infra itself is an established Latin preposition, so no root uncertainty attaches to that half.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代）：infrared 的确切首用无定论，且曾与 ultra-red 并存；infra 本身是有据的拉丁介词，因此这一半不存在词根存疑。

note.en: Group one holds words that mark where a band sits relative to a boundary; group two holds the neighbouring bands and the common names for their effects.
note.cn: 第一组是标出某波段相对边界位置的词；第二组是相邻波段及其效应的通称。

entries.definition: Ultra- means beyond, so ultraviolet sits past the violet end, with shorter waves and higher energy.
entries.definitionCN: ultra- 意为「超出」，因此紫外线在紫端之外，波长更短、能量更高。

entries.definition: Infra- plus sound: waves too low in pitch for the ear, a different scale entirely.
entries.definitionCN: infra- 加「声」：音高低于人耳可闻的波，完全属于另一套尺度。

entries.definition: Ultra- plus sound: waves too high in pitch for the ear, used in sonar and cleaning baths.
entries.definitionCN: ultra- 加「声」：音高高于人耳可闻的波，用于声呐与清洗槽。

entries.definition: An older rival of infrared, built with ultra- instead of infra; it lost and is now rare.
entries.definitionCN: infrared 的旧日竞争写法，用 ultra- 而非 infra-；后来落败，现已罕用。

entries.definition: The radiation any warm body emits; most of it falls in the infrared band.
entries.definitionCN: 任何温热物体发出的辐射，大部分落在红外波段。

entries.definition: The energy transferred by temperature difference; infrared is one of the ways it travels.
entries.definitionCN: 由温差传递的能量；红外是它传递的方式之一。

entries.definition: The band just beyond far infrared, with longer waves used for radar and ovens.
entries.definitionCN: 远红外之外的那一段，波长更长，用于雷达与微波炉。

entries.definition: The band the eye can see, lying just beyond near infrared on the other side of red.
entries.definitionCN: 肉眼能看见的那一段，在红端另一侧、紧邻近红外。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin prefix, the real experiment and the real applications.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁前缀、真实的实验与真实的应用。

normal.en: infra- means below, so infrared is the band below red on the colour scale.
normal.cn: infra- 意为「在下方」，因此红外是颜色次序中红之下的那一段。

normal.en: Herschel 1800 found warmth beyond red with a thermometer.
normal.cn: 1800 年赫歇尔用温度计在红光之外测到了热。

normal.en: Every warm object emits it, so the band is the heat you cannot see.
normal.cn: 每个温热物体都发出它，因此这一段就是看不见的热。

normal.en: The subdivisions are near infrared and far infrared.
normal.cn: 分区是近红外与远红外。

normal.en: The adjective and the noun are spelled the same: infrared light, the infrared.
normal.cn: 形容词与名词拼写相同：红外光、红外波段。

abstract.en: Picture a colour just past the last colour, where only warmth remains.
abstract.cn: 想象一种颜色，刚过最后一种颜色，那里只剩下暖意。

abstract.en: Picture a dark room where people glow without any lamp.
abstract.cn: 想象一间黑屋，人不用灯也在发着光。

abstract.en: Picture a beam that carries a command instead of a picture.
abstract.cn: 想象一束光，送的是命令而不是图像。

examples.en: The satellite maps forest fires by their infrared glow.
examples.cn: 这颗卫星根据森林火灾发出的红外辉光绘制火点。

examples.en: Most remote controls send a coded infrared pulse.
examples.cn: 大多数遥控器发送编码的红外脉冲。

examples.en: Infrared heaters warm people directly rather than warming the air.
examples.cn: 红外取暖器直接把人烘暖，而不是加热空气。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「infra（在下方）+ red（红）」——排在红色之下的那一段 → 红外线

root: 拉丁 infra「在下方」+ 英语 red（古英语 read）；red 与拉丁 ruber 同源但非借自拉丁，infra 为有据的拉丁介词。英语 infrared。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses start at the band itself, then move to felt heat, imaging, remote commands, astronomy, spectroscopy, the near-far split and radiant heating.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从波段本身开始，随后走向可感的热、成像、遥控、天文、光谱、近远分区与辐射加热。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a body in a dark room showing as an orange shape on a screen.
core.cn: 核心意象：黑屋中的人体在屏幕上显出一团橙红的形状。

branches.en: POSITION: the prefix fixes the band just below red, and every later sense inherits that address.
branches.cn: 位置：前缀把这一段定在红之下，后来每个义项都继承这个地址。

branches.en: WARMTH: the band is both what a body emits and what a heater aims.
branches.cn: 暖意：这一段既是物体发出的，也是取暖器所瞄准的。

branches.en: SIGNALS: an invisible band becomes a picture or a command.
branches.cn: 信号：不可见的一段变成了图像或命令。

branches.en: KNOWLEDGE: dust-hidden stars and vibrating bonds are both read in this band.
branches.cn: 认知：藏在尘埃中的恒星与振动的化学键，都在这一段被读取。

branches.en: SUBDIVISION: near and far keep the band ordered by distance from visible light.
branches.cn: 再分：近与远按离可见光的距离把这一段继续排序。

intro.en: Infrared is a Latin prefix on a native English colour word, a small but very productive pattern in scientific naming.
intro.cn: infrared 是拉丁前缀加英语本族颜色词，这在科学命名中是一种小而多产的构词方式。

latinIntro.en: Infra is a genuine Latin preposition; red is native English. No Latin noun stands behind the whole word, so the Latin entries cover only the prefix side.
latinIntro.cn: infra 是有据的拉丁介词，red 是英语本族词。整词背后没有拉丁名词，因此拉丁条目只覆盖前缀这一侧。

items.example: The prefix places the band below red.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把该波段放在红之下。

items.structure: red (native English adjective, Old English read)
items.example: The last visible band is red.
items.exampleCN: 最后一个可见波段是红色。

items.example: The camera reads infrared.
items.exampleCN: 相机读取红外线。

items.meaning: the part closest to visible red
items.meaningCN: 最靠近可见红光的那部分
items.example: Near-infrared light passes through fog.
items.exampleCN: 近红外光能穿过雾。

items.example: Far-infrared panels heat a room slowly.
items.exampleCN: 远红外板缓慢地把房间加热。

items.example: The infrared camera found the leak.
items.exampleCN: 红外相机找到了漏点。

items.example: The infrared sensor opened the door.
items.exampleCN: 红外传感器把门打开了。

items.example: Infrared spectroscopy found the bond.
items.exampleCN: 红外光谱法找到了那个化学键。

items.meaningCN: 在红外波段进行的天文观测
items.example: Infrared astronomy sees into dust clouds.
items.exampleCN: 红外天文学能看进尘埃云内部。

latinEntries.structure: inferus, infera, inferum (adj., first and second declension)

definition_zh: 紫外线的；紫外区的；紫外线辐射（不可数）
definition_en: relating to the band of radiation just beyond the violet end of the visible spectrum, with shorter waves and higher energy
core_image: 石英灯发出看不见的短波光，培养皿里的菌落几分钟后全部失活
scene: 实验台上石英灯发出看不见的短波光，几分钟后培养皿里的菌落全部失活。A quartz lamp emits ultraviolet strong enough to kill bacteria on the bench.
sceneCN: 这里 ultraviolet 指「波长比紫光更短、肉眼看不见的那段辐射」（第 1 个义项：位于可见光谱紫端之外的高能短波辐射）；句意为石英灯发出的紫外线强到能杀死台面上的细菌。可辨识物件：石英灯、培养皿、菌落、护目镜。

pos.zh: 紫外的；紫外区的
紫外线；紫外辐射（不可数）

forms.label: 名词（紫外线；紫外辐射，不可数）

senses.title: The band beyond violet
senses.titleCN: 紫光之外的那段不可见辐射
senses.definition: the region of the electromagnetic spectrum with wavelengths shorter than visible violet but longer than X-rays
senses.definitionCN: 电磁波谱中波长比可见紫光更短、比 X 射线更长的区域
senses.example: A quartz lamp emits ultraviolet strong enough to kill bacteria on the bench.
senses.exampleCN: 石英灯发出的紫外线强到能杀死台面上的细菌。
senses.why: ultra- means beyond, so the name places this band past violet on the ordered scale of colours.
senses.whyCN: ultra- 意为「超出」，因此这个名字把这一段放在颜色次序中紫之外。

senses.title: Sunlight ultraviolet
senses.titleCN: 阳光中的紫外部分
senses.definition: the short-wave component of sunlight that reaches the ground after the atmosphere filters much of it
senses.definitionCN: 阳光中被大气滤去大半后仍到达地面的短波成分
senses.example: Sunlight ultraviolet darkens the pigment in skin.
senses.exampleCN: 阳光中的紫外线使皮肤中的色素变深。
senses.why: the sun is the everyday source, so the band is usually met as a component of daylight rather than as a lamp.
senses.whyCN: 太阳是最日常的来源，因此这一段通常作为日光的一部分被遇见，而不是作为灯。

senses.title: Sterilising ultraviolet
senses.titleCN: 用于杀菌消毒的紫外线
senses.definition: the use of short-wave ultraviolet to damage the genetic material of microbes and stop them reproducing
senses.definitionCN: 用短波紫外破坏微生物遗传物质、使其无法繁殖
senses.example: Ultraviolet treatment cleared the water of bacteria within minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 紫外线处理几分钟内就清除了水中的细菌。
senses.why: the same short waves that damage skin also damage microbial DNA, so the band becomes a tool.
senses.whyCN: 伤害皮肤的短波同样会损伤微生物的遗传物质，于是这一段成了工具。

senses.title: Ultraviolet astronomy
senses.titleCN: 紫外天文学：观测高温天体
senses.definition: the observation of hot stars and gas through their ultraviolet emission, which the atmosphere blocks from the ground
senses.definitionCN: 借高温恒星与气体的紫外辐射进行观测，而大气在地面挡住了这些辐射
senses.example: Ultraviolet astronomy must be done from orbit.
senses.exampleCN: 紫外天文学必须从轨道上进行。
senses.why: only very hot objects emit strongly in this band, and the atmosphere absorbs it, so the technique needs space.
senses.whyCN: 只有非常高温的物体在这一段强烈辐射，而大气又吸收它，因此这项技术需要太空。

senses.title: The ultraviolet index
senses.titleCN: 紫外线指数：衡量到达地面的强度
senses.definition: a scale reporting the intensity of burning ultraviolet at the surface on a given day
senses.definitionCN: 报告某日地表灼伤性紫外线强度的指数
senses.example: The ultraviolet index reached eleven at noon.
senses.exampleCN: 正午时紫外线指数达到十一。
senses.why: a public warning needs a number, and the number is reported under the band name.
senses.whyCN: 公共警示需要一个数字，而这个数字就以该波段的名字发布。

senses.title: Ultraviolet absorbance
senses.titleCN: 紫外吸光度：光谱分析中的读数
senses.definition: the amount of ultraviolet a sample absorbs, used to infer concentration or electronic structure
senses.definitionCN: 样品所吸收的紫外量，用来推断浓度或电子结构
senses.example: The ultraviolet absorbance told them how much protein the solution held.
senses.exampleCN: 紫外吸光度让他们知道溶液中有多少蛋白质。
senses.why: many molecules absorb specific ultraviolet wavelengths, so a single reading can measure what is present.
senses.whyCN: 许多分子会吸收特定的紫外波长，因此一次读数就能测出存在的东西。

senses.title: Ultraviolet curing
senses.titleCN: 紫外固化：用紫外光使涂层硬化
senses.definition: the curing of inks, resins or adhesives by ultraviolet light that triggers a chemical reaction
senses.definitionCN: 用紫外光触发化学反应，使油墨、树脂或胶黏剂硬化
senses.example: Ultraviolet curing sets the printing ink in under a second.
senses.exampleCN: 紫外固化在不到一秒内就让印刷油墨定形。
senses.why: the high energy of the band starts reactions that heat alone would take far longer to start.
senses.whyCN: 这一段的高能量能启动单靠加热要慢得多的反应。

senses.title: Abstract: an invisible part of a range
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：一个范围中看不见却起作用的部分
senses.definition: the portion of any range that lies past its obvious limit and still has effects, though it cannot be seen directly
senses.definitionCN: 任何范围中超出明显边界、虽不能直接看见却仍起作用的那部分
senses.example: The costs were the ultraviolet of the budget, invisible but damaging.
senses.exampleCN: 这些成本是预算中看不见的紫外部分，无形却有伤害。
senses.why: the abstract sense keeps only the position beyond the visible edge, where effect outruns sight.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义只保留「在可见边缘之外」这个位置：效果超出视觉所能及。

intro.en: Ultraviolet is a Latin-English hybrid: ultra, beyond, plus the English colour word violet. It dates from the 1840s, after chemical effects beyond violet were found.
intro.cn: ultraviolet 是拉丁与英语的混合词：拉丁 ultra「超出」加英语颜色词 violet。它出现于 1840 年代，在紫光之外的化学效应被发现之后。

items.en: Ultra meant beyond or on the far side, and English uses it as the prefix ultra-, as in ultrasonic and ultramarine.
items.cn: ultra 意为「超出、在远侧」，英语以 ultra- 作前缀，如 ultrasonic 与 ultramarine。

items.en: Violet goes back through Old French to Latin viola, the violet flower; the colour name is older than the physics.
items.cn: violet 经古法语上溯到拉丁 viola「堇菜」；颜色名比物理学用法更早。

items.en: Ritter found that silver salts darkened fastest beyond the violet end of a prism spectrum, showing a chemical effect where nothing was visible.
items.cn: 里特尔发现银盐在棱镜光谱紫端之外变黑最快，说明在看不见之处仍有化学作用。

items.en: The English adjective ultraviolet was formed in the 1840s, once the invisible band needed a name of its own.
items.cn: 英语形容词 ultraviolet 于 1840 年代成形，因为这段不可见波段需要一个自己的名字。

items.en: Sterilisation, the ozone layer, the ultraviolet index and curing all became familiar in the twentieth century.
items.cn: 杀菌、臭氧层、紫外线指数与固化都在 20 世纪变得常见。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date only): the exact first use of ultraviolet is not agreed; ultra and viola are well attested Latin words, so no root uncertainty attaches to either half.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代）：ultraviolet 的确切首用无定论；ultra 与 viola 都是有据的拉丁词，因此两半都不存在词根存疑。

note.en: Group one holds the boundary words that look alike because they share ultra-; group two holds the neighbouring bands and the effects people confuse with them.
note.cn: 第一组是因共享 ultra- 而形近的边界词；第二组是相邻波段以及人们容易混淆的效应。

entries.definition: Infra- means below, so infrared lies past the red end with longer waves and lower energy.
entries.definitionCN: infra- 意为「在下」，因此红外在红端之外，波长更长、能量更低。

entries.definition: Ultra- plus marine: a deep blue pigment once shipped from beyond the sea, with nothing to do with radiation.
entries.definitionCN: ultra- 加「海」：一种曾从海外运来的深蓝颜料，与辐射无关。

entries.definition: Ultra- plus sound: vibrations above hearing, used in scanning and cleaning.
entries.definitionCN: ultra- 加「声」：高于听觉的振动，用于扫描与清洗。

entries.definition: An instrument that reveals particles too small for an ordinary microscope by scattering light sideways.
entries.definitionCN: 靠侧向散射光显示普通显微镜看不见的微粒的仪器。

entries.definition: The last visible colour before the band begins; it is the boundary ultraviolet is named against.
entries.definitionCN: 该波段开始前最后一个可见颜色；紫外线正是以它为界命名。

entries.definition: Radiation energetic enough to strip electrons from atoms; short ultraviolet belongs to this class.
entries.definitionCN: 能量足以把电子从原子中剥离的辐射；短波紫外属于这一类。

entries.definition: The band beyond ultraviolet, with even shorter waves and enough energy to pass through tissue.
entries.definitionCN: 紫外之外的那一段，波长更短，能量足以穿过组织。

entries.definition: The whole solar spectrum at the surface, of which ultraviolet is the part that burns.
entries.definitionCN: 地表的整个太阳光谱，其中造成灼伤的那部分就是紫外。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin prefix, the real experiment and the real public uses.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁前缀、真实的实验与真实的公共用途。

normal.en: ultra- means beyond, so ultraviolet is the band beyond violet.
normal.cn: ultra- 意为「超出」，因此紫外是紫之外的那一段。

normal.en: Violet comes from Latin viola, the flower, so the colour name came first.
normal.cn: 紫色一词出自拉丁 viola「堇菜」，所以颜色名先于物理术语。

normal.en: The abbreviation UV is standard in labels and forecasts.
normal.cn: 两个字母的缩写在标签与预报中是标准写法。

normal.en: It both burns and sterilises, because short waves damage genetic material.
normal.cn: 它既灼伤也能杀菌，因为短波会损伤遗传物质。

normal.en: Near ultraviolet and far ultraviolet are the two subdivisions.
normal.cn: 近紫外与远紫外是两个分区。

abstract.en: Picture a room lit by a lamp everyone insists is off.
abstract.cn: 想象一间屋子，人人都说灯关了，屋里却仍亮着。

abstract.en: Picture a colour that only the skin can read.
abstract.cn: 想象一种只有皮肤读得懂的颜色。

abstract.en: Picture a cost that never appears on any invoice but still arrives.
abstract.cn: 想象一笔从不出现在任何账单上、却仍然到来的成本。

examples.en: The ozone layer absorbs most ultraviolet before it reaches the ground.
examples.cn: 臭氧层在紫外线到达地面之前吸收了其中大部分。

examples.en: Ultraviolet lamps sterilise the air inside the hospital ward.
examples.cn: 紫外灯对病房内的空气进行杀菌。

examples.en: The forecast put the ultraviolet index at eight, high enough to burn in minutes.
examples.cn: 预报的紫外线指数为八，足以在几分钟内晒伤。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ultra（超出）+ violet（紫）」——排在紫色之外的那一段 → 紫外线

root: 拉丁 ultra「超出」+ 英语 violet（经古法语上溯拉丁 viola「堇菜」）；两半均为有据来源，无重构词根。英语 ultraviolet。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses begin at the band, then move to sunlight, sterilising, astronomy, the public index, absorbance, curing and finally the unseen part of any range.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从波段本身开始，随后走向阳光、杀菌、天文、公共指数、吸光度、固化，最后落在任何范围中看不见的那一部分。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lamp that shows nothing yet empties a dish of living colonies.
core.cn: 核心意象：一盏看不见光的灯，却让一皿活菌落全部失活。

branches.en: POSITION: the prefix fixes the address past violet, and everything else follows from that place.
branches.cn: 位置：前缀把地址定在紫之外，其余义项都从这个位置而来。

branches.en: DAYLIGHT AND WARNING: the sun supplies it, and a number warns how much arrives.
branches.cn: 日光与警示：太阳提供它，一个数字警告来了多少。

branches.en: CONTROL: the same energy kills microbes and hardens resins.
branches.cn: 控制：同一份能量既能杀死微生物，也能使树脂硬化。

branches.en: MEASUREMENT: hot stars and absorbing molecules are both read through this band.
branches.cn: 测量：高温恒星与吸收分子都通过这一段被读取。

branches.en: METAPHOR: whatever lies past the visible edge but still acts.
branches.cn: 比喻：位于可见边缘之外却仍然起作用的一切。

intro.en: Ultraviolet is a Latin prefix on a colour word of Latin descent, so both halves have a traceable history.
intro.cn: ultraviolet 是拉丁前缀加一个源自拉丁的颜色词，两半都有可追溯的历史。

latinIntro.en: Latin ultra means beyond; Latin viola gives violet through French. The modern compound itself is nineteenth-century English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 ultra 意为「超出」；拉丁 viola 经法语给出 violet。这个近代复合词本身是十九世纪英语的产物。

items.example: The prefix places the band beyond violet.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把该波段放在紫之外。

items.structure: violet (English colour word, from Old French violette, from Latin viola)
items.example: Violet is the boundary of the visible band.
items.exampleCN: 紫色是可见波段的边界。

items.example: The lamp emits ultraviolet.
items.exampleCN: 这盏灯发出紫外线。

items.meaning: the part closest to visible violet
items.meaningCN: 最靠近可见紫光的那部分
items.example: Near-ultraviolet light is used in some detectors.
items.exampleCN: 近紫外光用于某些探测器。

items.example: Far-ultraviolet light is absorbed high in the atmosphere.
items.exampleCN: 远紫外光在大气高层被吸收。

items.meaning: a lamp made to emit ultraviolet
items.example: The ultraviolet lamp sterilised the bench.
items.exampleCN: 紫外灯对台面做了杀菌。

items.meaning: a public scale of ultraviolet intensity
items.meaningCN: 紫外线强度的公共指数
items.example: The ultraviolet index warned of strong sun.
items.exampleCN: 紫外线指数提示阳光很强。

items.example: Ultraviolet spectroscopy measured the protein.
items.exampleCN: 紫外光谱法测出了蛋白质。

items.meaning: how much ultraviolet a sample takes in
items.example: The ultraviolet absorbance rose with concentration.
items.exampleCN: 紫外吸光度随浓度升高。

definition_zh: 可见的；看得见的；明显的；可公开查阅的；有形的（贸易）
definition_en: able to be seen, or easy to notice and recognize
core_image: 黑屋里一盏灯亮起，桌角从模糊到清晰，轮廓终于被眼睛分辨出来
scene: 全黑的屋子里只有很窄的一段波段能被眼睛接收，其余部分完全感觉不到。Only a narrow band of the whole spectrum is visible to the human eye.
sceneCN: 这里 visible 指「能被眼睛看见的」（第 1 个义项：落在人眼可感知范围内的）；句意为整个波谱中只有很窄的一段对人眼可见。可辨识物件：黑屋、灯、眼睛、被照亮的桌角。

pos.zh: 可见的；看得见的；明显的；可公开查阅的；有形的

senses.title: Able to be seen
senses.titleCN: 能被眼睛看见的
senses.definition: capable of being perceived by the eye under the conditions present
senses.definitionCN: 在现有条件下能够被眼睛感知的
senses.example: Only a narrow band of the whole spectrum is visible to the human eye.
senses.exampleCN: 整个波谱中只有很窄的一段对人眼可见。
senses.why: Latin visibilis came from videre, to see, so the word simply says able to be seen.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 visibilis 出自 videre「看见」，因此这个词说的就是「能被看见」。

senses.title: The visible band of light
senses.titleCN: 可见光：人眼能感知的那段波长
senses.definition: describing the range of wavelengths, roughly four hundred to seven hundred nanometres, that the eye responds to
senses.definitionCN: 描述人眼能响应的大约四百至七百纳米的那段波长
senses.example: Visible light occupies only a small slice of the electromagnetic spectrum.
senses.exampleCN: 可见光只占电磁波谱的一小片。
senses.why: physics uses the adjective as a fixed label for one band, turning a general ability into a named range.
senses.whyCN: 物理学把这个形容词固定用作某一波段的标签，把一般能力变成了有名有姓的范围。

senses.title: Easy to notice
senses.titleCN: 明显的、容易察觉的
senses.definition: clear enough to be noticed without effort, as a change, a sign or an effect
senses.definitionCN: 清楚到不必费力就能察觉，如变化、迹象或效果
senses.example: There were visible signs of wear along the edge of the blade.
senses.exampleCN: 刀刃边缘有明显的磨损迹象。
senses.why: what can be seen needs no argument, so visible drifted from eyesight to evidence.
senses.whyCN: 看得见的东西不需要论证，于是 visible 从「眼见」滑向「证据明显」。

senses.title: Open to public view
senses.titleCN: 可公开查阅的、对公众开放的
senses.definition: available for public inspection rather than hidden or restricted
senses.definitionCN: 可供公众查阅，而非隐藏或受限的
senses.example: The register is visible to anyone who asks at the counter.
senses.exampleCN: 这份登记册对任何到柜台询问的人公开。
senses.why: institutions borrowed the word because a record that can be looked at is a record that can be trusted.
senses.whyCN: 机构借用这个词，因为能被查看的记录才是可信的记录。

senses.title: Visible trade
senses.titleCN: 有形贸易：货物而非服务的进出口
senses.definition: describing trade in physical goods, which can be counted at a border, as opposed to invisible trade in services
senses.definitionCN: 描述实物货物的进出口，可在边境清点，与服务类的无形贸易相对
senses.example: Visible trade in machinery outweighs the export of insurance services.
senses.exampleCN: 机械类的有形贸易额超过保险服务出口。
senses.why: economics set visible goods against invisible services, keeping the plain sense of something that can be handled.
senses.whyCN: 经济学把「有形货物」与「无形服务」对置，保留「能拿在手里」的朴素含义。

senses.title: The visible horizon
senses.titleCN: 可见地平线：视线能达到的最远边界
senses.definition: the line or limit beyond which an object can no longer be seen because of distance, terrain or haze
senses.definitionCN: 因距离、地形或薄雾而不能再看见物体的那条界线
senses.example: The ship disappeared below the visible horizon before dusk.
senses.exampleCN: 天黑前，那艘船消失在了可见地平线之下。
senses.why: the adjective marks a boundary of sight rather than a property of the object.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词标出的是视线的边界，而不是物体的属性。

senses.title: Visible means of support
senses.titleCN: 有形的生计来源（法律用语）
senses.definition: a legal phrase for an identifiable source of income, used in statutes on vagrancy and support
senses.definitionCN: 法律上指可查明收入来源的固定说法，用于流浪与扶养相关法规
senses.example: The old statute asked whether the person had visible means of support.
senses.exampleCN: 那条旧法规要问此人是否有可查明的生计来源。
senses.why: law needed a phrase for income that could actually be shown, and visible supplied exactly that.
senses.whyCN: 法律需要一个短语指「确实拿得出证据的收入」，visible 正好提供这层意思。

senses.title: Conspicuous, seeking attention
senses.titleCN: 显眼的、引人注意的
senses.definition: striking enough to draw attention, sometimes in a way that is considered too showy
senses.definitionCN: 醒目到足以引来注意，有时带有过于招摇的意味
senses.example: The campaign made the candidate highly visible in every district.
senses.exampleCN: 这场竞选让候选人在每个选区都十分显眼。
senses.why: the abstract sense adds intent: not merely seeable, but placed where many eyes will land.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义添上了意图：不只是能被看见，而是被放在许多目光会落下的地方。

intro.en: Visible comes from Latin visibilis, able to be seen, from videre, to see, through French. Its root is one of the oldest in the language.
intro.cn: visible 经法语来自拉丁 visibilis「能被看见的」，其动词为 videre「看见」。这个词根是语言中最古老的词根之一。

items.en: Videre meant to see. Its perfect participle visus supplies vision, visual and video, and the root is generally traced to an Indo-European word for seeing.
items.cn: videre 意为「看见」。其完成分词 visus 给出 vision、visual 与 video，这个词根一般认为是印欧语中表示「看见」的词。

items.en: The adjective visibilis meant able to be seen, built with the suffix -ibilis, which marks capacity.
items.cn: 形容词 visibilis 意为「能被看见的」，由表示能力的后缀 -ibilis 构成。

items.en: Old French visible brought the word into English in the fourteenth century, first in the plain optical sense.
items.cn: 古法语 visible 在十四世纪把这个词带入英语，最初只有朴素的光学义。

items.en: By the sixteenth century visible also meant clear to the mind, since what is plainly seen needs no proof.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，visible 也指「对心智而言清楚」，因为明明白白看见的东西不需要证明。

items.en: Physics fixed visible light as a band name, and economics set visible trade against invisible trade in services.
items.cn: 物理学把「可见光」固定为波段名，经济学则以「有形贸易」与服务类的「无形贸易」相对。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper root only): the link of videre to the Indo-European seeing root is generally accepted rather than demonstrated step by step, so the reconstructed forms offered for it should be read as reconstructions.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅更深词根）：videre 与印欧「看见」词根的联系属一般认为，而非逐环证明，因此为其给出的重构形式应视为重构。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same seeing root whose meanings have separated; group two holds the near synonyms that stress evidence rather than eyesight.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「看见」词根、意义已经分开的词；第二组是强调证据而非视力的近义词。

entries.definition: Relating to seeing or to the sense of sight, as in visual aids; it does not mean that something can be seen.
entries.definitionCN: 与观看或视觉有关，如视觉辅助；它并不表示某物能被看见。

entries.definition: The ability to see, or a far-reaching plan; it names the power, not the property of an object.
entries.definitionCN: 视力，或远大构想；它命名的是能力，不是物体的属性。

entries.definition: In a way that can be seen, as in visibly tired; it modifies the verb rather than the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 以看得见的方式，如明显疲惫；它修饰动词，而非名词。

entries.definition: An official or formal visit, from visitare, to go to see; the seeing here is going somewhere to look.
entries.definitionCN: 正式或官方的造访，出自 visitare「去看」；这里的「看」是前往某处查看。

entries.definition: Clear to the understanding, though it can also mean merely seeming rather than real.
entries.definitionCN: 对理解而言清楚，但也可指「表面上如此而非真实」。

entries.definition: Plain from the evidence; it stresses inference from signs rather than direct sight.
entries.definitionCN: 由证据看来显而易见；强调从迹象推断，而非直接看见。

entries.definition: Easy to become aware of, often through a change in appearance or behaviour.
entries.definitionCN: 容易被察觉，常因外观或行为有变化。

entries.definition: Able to be watched or measured in a systematic way, a word of science rather than of eyesight.
entries.definitionCN: 能被系统地观察或测量，是科学用语，而非日常视力用语。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin verb, the real suffix and the real technical labels.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁动词、真实的后缀与真实的技术标签。

normal.en: videre means see, and -ible means can be, so visible means can be seen.
normal.cn: videre 意为「看见」，-ible 意为「能够」，因此 visible 就是「能被看见」。

normal.en: The same root gives video, vision, visual and visor.
normal.cn: 同一词根给出 video、vision、visual 与 visor。

normal.en: The noun is visibility, and the negative pair is invisible and invisibility.
normal.cn: 名词是 visibility，否定的一对是 invisible 与 invisibility。

normal.en: Visible light is a fixed band name, not a description of a particular lamp.
normal.cn: 「可见光」是固定的波段名，不是对某盏灯的描述。

normal.en: Visible trade means goods, invisible trade means services.
normal.cn: 「有形贸易」指货物，「无形贸易」指服务。

abstract.en: Picture a line drawn on the ground past which the eye simply gives up.
abstract.cn: 想象地上画着一条线，越过它眼睛就再也看不见了。

abstract.en: Picture a stain on a shirt that no one can pretend not to notice.
abstract.cn: 想象衬衫上的一块污渍，没人能假装没看见。

abstract.en: Picture a person standing under the only working lamp in a dark hall.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人站在黑走廊里唯一还亮着的灯下。

examples.en: The comet is just visible through a small telescope tonight.
examples.cn: 今晚用一架小望远镜勉强能看到这颗彗星。

examples.en: The repair was visible as a faint line across the painting.
examples.cn: 那道修补在画面上显成一条淡淡的线。

examples.en: Visible trade data excludes earnings from tourism and shipping services.
examples.cn: 有形贸易数据不包括旅游与航运服务的收入。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「vis（看）+ ible（能够）」——能够被看到的 → 可见的；看得清楚 → 明显的

root: 拉丁 videre「看见」+ 后缀 -ibilis「能够被……」→ visibilis「能被看见的」，经古法语进入英语；videre 与印欧「看见」词根的联系属一般认为。英语 visible。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses start with the eye, then name a band of light, then move to evidence, public access, counted goods, the edge of sight, a legal phrase and finally the wish to be noticed.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从眼睛开始，随后命名一段光，再依次走向证据、公开查阅、可清点的货物、视线边界、法律短语，最后落在「希望被注意」上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a shape in a dark room becoming clear as a lamp is lit.
core.cn: 核心意象：黑屋里的一个形状，随着灯亮起而变清晰。

branches.en: THE EYE: the literal capacity to be perceived is the trunk of the word.
branches.cn: 眼睛：字面上「能被感知」的能力，是这个词的树干。

branches.en: BOUNDARIES OF SIGHT: a fixed band and a horizon both mark where seeing stops.
branches.cn: 视线的边界：固定的波段与地平线，都标出「看」停止的地方。

branches.en: EVIDENCE AND ACCESS: what can be looked at becomes what can be trusted.
branches.cn: 证据与公开：能被查看的东西，成了能被信任的东西。

branches.en: INSTITUTIONS: trade law counts visible goods, and support law asks for visible income.
branches.cn: 制度：贸易法清点有形货物，扶养法要求有形收入。

branches.en: ATTENTION: being seeable turns into being deliberately placed in sight.
branches.cn: 注意力：能被看见，变成了被有意放在目光之下。

intro.en: Visible is a Latin adjective with a transparent suffix, and its root runs through a large family of seeing words.
intro.cn: visible 是一个后缀透明的拉丁形容词，其词根贯穿一大族「看」的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin videre gives visus and visibilis; English adds -ly for the adverb and in- for the negative.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 videre 给出 visus 与 visibilis；英语再加 -ly 构成副词，加 in- 构成否定。

items.example: The root underlies video and vision.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根支撑着 video 与 vision。

items.example: The suffix turns a verb into a capacity.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把动词变成一种能力。

items.example: Only one band is visible.
items.exampleCN: 只有一段是可见的。

items.meaning: in a way that can be seen
items.example: He was visibly tired.
items.exampleCN: 他明显累了。

items.meaning: the state of being seen; clearness of air
items.meaningCN: 可见的状态；空气的能见度
items.example: Fog cut visibility to fifty metres.
items.exampleCN: 雾把能见度降到五十米。

items.example: The gas is invisible.
items.exampleCN: 这种气体看不见。

items.meaning: the state of not being seen
items.example: The cloak promised invisibility.
items.exampleCN: 这件斗篷许诺隐身。

items.meaning: the band the eye can see
items.example: Visible light spans four hundred to seven hundred nanometres.
items.exampleCN: 可见光横跨四百到七百纳米。

items.example: Visible trade rose with the port expansion.
items.exampleCN: 有形贸易随港口扩建而增长。

definition_zh: 光学的；与光有关的；视觉的；眼睛的；光学仪器（复数名词）
definition_en: relating to light, to sight, or to devices that use lenses, mirrors or fibres
core_image: 玻璃丝里跑着一串光脉冲，细丝末端亮起一个小点
scene: 玻璃丝里跑着一个个光脉冲，信号沿细丝传到远处的接收端。The optical fibre carries the signal as pulses of light along a glass thread.
sceneCN: 这里 optical 指「与光或光学有关的」（第 1 个义项：涉及光的产生、传播或控制的）；句意为光纤把信号以光脉冲形式沿玻璃丝传送。可辨识物件：玻璃细丝、光脉冲、接收端、连接头。

pos.zh: 光学的；与光有关的；视觉的
（常用复数）光学仪器；光学部件

derivatives.zh: 在光学上；用光学方法地

senses.title: Relating to light
senses.titleCN: 与光有关的
senses.definition: concerned with light itself, its production, transmission or detection
senses.definitionCN: 涉及光本身，即其产生、传播或探测
senses.example: The optical fibre carries the signal as pulses of light along a glass thread.
senses.exampleCN: 光纤把信号以光脉冲形式沿玻璃丝传送。
senses.why: Greek optikos meant of sight, from optos, seen; the adjective moved from the eye to the light the eye uses.
senses.whyCN: 希腊 optikos 意为「视觉的」，出自 optos「被看见的」；这个形容词从眼睛移到了眼睛所用的光。

senses.title: An optical instrument
senses.titleCN: 使用透镜或反射镜的光学仪器
senses.definition: describing a device that uses lenses, mirrors or prisms to form an image or direct light
senses.definitionCN: 描述用透镜、反射镜或棱镜成像或导光的装置
senses.example: The laboratory keeps its optical instruments in a dust-free cabinet.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室把光学仪器放在无尘柜里。
senses.why: the adjective names the working principle rather than the purpose, so a microscope and a camera share it.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词命名的是工作原理而非用途，因此显微镜与相机共用它。

senses.title: An optical illusion
senses.titleCN: 视错觉：眼睛被图案骗过
senses.definition: a false perception produced when the visual system interprets a pattern in the wrong way
senses.definitionCN: 视觉系统对图案作出错误解释时产生的错误感知
senses.example: The optical illusion made the straight lines appear to bend.
senses.exampleCN: 这个视错觉让直线看起来弯了。
senses.why: the error lies in sight rather than in light, which is why the word keeps its link to the eye.
senses.whyCN: 错误出在视觉而非光线，因此这个词仍与眼睛相连。

senses.title: An optical fibre
senses.titleCN: 光纤：把光约束在细丝中传输
senses.definition: a thin thread of glass that guides light by repeated internal reflection, used to carry signals
senses.definitionCN: 靠反复全反射把光约束其中的细玻璃丝，用于传输信号
senses.example: Optical fibre replaced copper in the new trunk line.
senses.exampleCN: 新干线路上，光纤取代了铜线。
senses.why: the fibre works by optics alone, so the adjective distinguishes it from the electrical cable it replaced.
senses.whyCN: 这种纤维只靠光学工作，因此用该形容词与它取代的电线区分开来。

senses.title: The optical axis
senses.titleCN: 光轴：光学系统的对称中心线
senses.definition: the line through the centre of a lens or mirror system about which the optical elements are arranged
senses.definitionCN: 穿过透镜或反射镜系统中心、各光学元件据以排列的那条线
senses.example: The lens was mounted slightly off the optical axis.
senses.exampleCN: 这片透镜安装得略微偏离光轴。
senses.why: a system needs a reference line, and the adjective marks that the line belongs to light rather than to mechanics.
senses.whyCN: 系统需要一条参考线，这个形容词标出这条线属于光而非机械。

senses.title: Optical character recognition
senses.titleCN: 光学字符识别：让机器读印刷文字
senses.definition: the automatic conversion of a picture of printed text into machine-readable characters
senses.definitionCN: 把印刷文字的图像自动转成机器可读字符
senses.example: Optical character recognition turned the scanned page into searchable text.
senses.exampleCN: 光学字符识别把扫描页变成了可检索的文本。
senses.why: the machine looks at the page with light and lenses, so computing borrowed the adjective for the seeing part.
senses.whyCN: 机器用光与镜头看这一页，因此计算机领域借这个形容词指「看」的那一环。

senses.title: Optical astronomy
senses.titleCN: 光学天文学：用可见光观测
senses.definition: the branch of astronomy that observes visible light rather than radio, infrared or other bands
senses.definitionCN: 观测可见光而非射电、红外等波段的天文学分支
senses.example: Optical astronomy still supplies the sharpest pictures of planets.
senses.exampleCN: 光学天文学仍能提供最清晰的行星图像。
senses.why: as other bands opened up, the old visible-light work needed a label, and optical became it.
senses.whyCN: 当别的波段被打开后，旧的可见光工作需要一个标签，optical 便承担了这个角色。

senses.title: Abstract: visual rather than conceptual
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：视觉层面的，而非概念层面的
senses.definition: concerned with how something looks to the eye rather than with what it means
senses.definitionCN: 关注某物在眼睛看来是什么样，而非它意味着什么
senses.example: The disagreement was optical rather than substantive, a matter of layout.
senses.exampleCN: 这一分歧是视觉层面的而非实质性的，只是版式问题。
senses.why: the abstract sense keeps only the channel: something is judged by appearance, not by content.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义只保留通道：判断依据是外观，而非内容。

intro.en: Optical comes through Latin opticus from Greek optikos, of sight, built on optos, seen, from the verb for seeing. The word entered English in the sixteenth century.
intro.cn: optical 经拉丁 opticus 来自希腊 optikos「视觉的」，其词为 optos「被看见的」，出自「看见」这一动词。这个词在十六世纪进入英语。

items.en: Ops meant the eye or the face, and the related verb meant to see; the family also gives optos, seen.
items.cn: ops 指眼睛或脸，相关动词意为「看见」；这一族还给出 optos「被看见的」。

items.en: Optikos meant of sight or of the science of seeing, and it named the study of light and vision.
items.cn: optikos 意为「视觉的、看之学的」，并用来说明研究光与视觉的学问。

items.en: Latin took the adjective as opticus; English optical follows the Latin stem with the suffix -al.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入作 opticus；英语 optical 沿用拉丁词干并加后缀 -al。

items.en: English optical appears in the sixteenth century, first in treatises on lenses and the eye.
items.cn: 英语 optical 出现于十六世纪，最初见于论透镜与眼睛的著作。

items.en: Optical fibre, optical character recognition and optical astronomy are all twentieth-century compounds built on the adjective.
items.cn: 光纤、光学字符识别与光学天文学都是 20 世纪以该形容词构成的复合词。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper root only): the further origin of Greek ops is unsettled, and the link sometimes drawn to a Indo-European seeing root is a reconstruction rather than a demonstrated step.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅更深词根）：希腊 ops 的更早来源没有定论，有人把它与某个印欧「看见」词根相连，那属重构，而非已证实的环节。

note.en: Group one holds words that look like optical but come from different roots or different word classes; group two holds the adjectives that also describe sight and light.
note.cn: 第一组是与 optical 形近、却来自不同词根或不同词类的词；第二组是同样描述视觉与光的形容词。

entries.definition: The science of light, a plural-looking singular noun; it is the discipline, not a property of an object.
entries.definitionCN: 研究光的学科，形式是复数而作单数用；它是学科，不是物体的属性。

entries.definition: A person who makes or sells lenses and spectacles, built with -ian marking a practitioner.
entries.definitionCN: 制作或售卖镜片与眼镜的人，后缀 -ian 表示从业者。

entries.definition: From optio, a choice, not from ops, the eye; it means not compulsory and has no optical sense at all.
entries.definitionCN: 出自 optio「选择」，而非 ops「眼睛」；意为「非必需的」，完全没有光学含义。

entries.definition: The profession of measuring vision and prescribing lenses, from optos plus metron, measure.
entries.definitionCN: 测量视力并验配镜片的行业，由 optos 加 metron「测量」构成。

entries.definition: Relating to the act of seeing or to visual perception, as in visual memory.
entries.definitionCN: 与看这一行为或视觉感知有关，如视觉记忆。

entries.definition: Relating to the eye as an organ, as in ocular muscles; it is anatomical rather than physical.
entries.definitionCN: 与作为器官的眼睛有关，如眼肌；属解剖用语而非物理用语。

entries.definition: Relating to light as a stimulus to living things, as in the photic zone of the sea.
entries.definitionCN: 与光作为生物刺激有关，如海洋透光层。

entries.definition: A plain descriptive phrase for equipment built around lenses; it lacks the scientific scope of optical.
entries.definitionCN: 对围绕透镜构造的设备的朴素描述，缺少 optical 的科学涵盖面。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Greek root, the real word family and the real twentieth-century compounds.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的希腊词根、真实的词族与真实的 20 世纪复合词。

normal.en: Greek optos means seen, so optical is about what light makes visible.
normal.cn: 希腊 optos 意为「被看见的」，因此 optical 讲的是光使什么可见。

normal.en: Optics is the field, an optician is the person, and optically is the adverb.
normal.cn: optics 是学科，optician 是从业者，optically 是副词。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the uses: optical fibre, optical illusion, optical axis.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：光纤、视错觉、光轴。

normal.en: Optical astronomy means visible-light astronomy, as opposed to radio astronomy.
normal.cn: 「光学天文学」指依靠可见光的观测分支，与射电天文学相对。

normal.en: Optional looks similar but comes from choice, not from the eye.
normal.cn: optional 形近，却出自「选择」而非「眼睛」。

abstract.en: Picture a thread of glass so clear that only the light inside it shows the way.
abstract.cn: 想象一根玻璃丝清透到只有里面的光能指路。

abstract.en: Picture two parallel lines that insist on looking bent.
abstract.cn: 想象两条平行线偏要看起来是弯的。

abstract.en: Picture a page that a machine reads with a lamp instead of a mind.
abstract.cn: 想象机器用一盏灯而不是用头脑去读的一页纸。

examples.en: The telescope is the oldest optical instrument still in daily use.
examples.cn: 望远镜是仍被日常使用的最古老光学仪器。

examples.en: Optical fibres carry most of the world long-distance data traffic.
examples.cn: 光纤承载了世界上大部分长途数据流量。

examples.en: The museum uses optical character recognition to index its labels.
examples.cn: 博物馆用光学字符识别为标签建索引。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「opt（看）+ ical」——与看、与光有关的 → 光学的；用镜片和光工作的 → 光学仪器

root: 希腊 ops「眼睛、脸」→ optos「被看见的」→ optikos「视觉的」，经拉丁 opticus 进入英语并加 -al；ops 的更深来源不确定。英语 optical。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses start with light itself, then pass through instruments, illusions, fibres, axes, machine reading and astronomy, and end as a figure for appearance over substance.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从光本身开始，随后经过仪器、错觉、光纤、光轴、机器识读与天文，最后成为「外观压过实质」的比喻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a glass thread guiding pulses of light to a small bright point.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根玻璃丝把光脉冲引到一个小小的亮点。

branches.en: THE PHYSICAL CORE: light produced, transmitted or detected is the trunk of every other sense.
branches.cn: 物理核心：光的产生、传播或探测，是其余义项的树干。

branches.en: HARDWARE: instruments and axes are arranged around the behaviour of light.
branches.cn: 硬件：仪器与光轴都围绕光的行为了布置。

branches.en: THE EYE FAILS: an illusion is an error of sight, not of light.
branches.cn: 眼睛出错：错觉是视觉的错误，而非光的错误。

branches.en: APPLICATIONS: fibre, character recognition and optical astronomy each take one technical face of light.
branches.cn: 应用：光纤、字符识别与光学天文，各取光的某一个技术侧面。

branches.en: APPEARANCE: what is judged is how it looks, not what it is.
branches.cn: 外观：被判断的是它看起来怎样，而不是它是什么。

intro.en: Optical is a Greek adjective that reached English through Latin, and its stem also builds the names of the field and the practitioner.
intro.cn: optical 是经拉丁进入英语的希腊形容词，其词干还构成学科名与从业者名。

latinIntro.en: Greek optikos became Latin opticus; English added -al. The noun optics keeps the Greek plural ending -ics that marks a field.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 optikos 转为拉丁 opticus，英语再加 -al。名词 optics 保留希腊复数后缀 -ics，用来表示学科。

items.example: The combining form appears in optoelectronics.
items.exampleCN: 这个组合形式出现在光电子学中。

items.example: The suffix makes an adjective of the Greek stem.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把希腊词干变成形容词。

items.example: Optical fibre carries the signal.
items.exampleCN: 光纤传输信号。

items.example: Optics explains the rainbow.
items.exampleCN: 光学解释了彩虹。

items.meaning: a maker or seller of lenses
items.example: The optician fitted new lenses.
items.exampleCN: 眼镜师装上了新镜片。

items.example: The signal is read optically.
items.exampleCN: 信号以光学方式读取。

items.example: Optometry checks how the eye focuses.
items.exampleCN: 验光学检查眼睛如何聚焦。

items.meaning: a glass thread that guides light
items.example: The optical fibre runs under the street.
items.exampleCN: 光纤铺在街道下面。

items.meaning: a trick played on the eye
items.example: The optical illusion bent the straight lines.
items.exampleCN: 这个视错觉把直线弄弯了。

latinEntries.structure: opticus, optica, opticum (adj., first and second declension; from Greek)
optice (f., first declension; from Greek optike)

definition_zh: 光子；光量子（电磁辐射的最小能量单元）
definition_en: the smallest discrete unit of electromagnetic energy, which behaves both as a particle and as a wave
core_image: 极弱的光打在金属板上，偶尔有一个能量单元击出一个电子
scene: 金属板被极弱的光照到，偶尔有一个能量单元击出一个电子。A single photon carries just enough energy to free one electron from the metal.
sceneCN: 这里 photon 指「电磁辐射不可再分的最小能量单元」（第 1 个义项：光与电磁辐射的量子）；句意为单个光子携带的能量刚好足以把金属中的一个电子释放出来。可辨识物件：金属板、微弱光束、逸出的电子、电源。

pos.zh: 光子；光量子

senses.title: A quantum of electromagnetic energy
senses.titleCN: 电磁辐射的最小能量单元
senses.definition: the smallest indivisible amount of energy in an electromagnetic field, carrying one frequency-dependent packet
senses.definitionCN: 电磁场中不可再分的最小能量单位，其能量由频率决定
senses.example: A single photon carries just enough energy to free one electron from the metal.
senses.exampleCN: 单个光子携带的能量刚好足以把金属中的一个电子释放出来。
senses.why: the name joins Greek phos, light, to the -on ending of electron, so it presents light as a particle.
senses.whyCN: 这个名字把希腊 phos「光」与 electron 的 -on 后缀结合，因此把光呈现为粒子。

senses.title: Photon energy
senses.titleCN: 光子能量：与频率成正比的能量份额
senses.definition: the energy of one quantum, proportional to frequency and fixed by Planck constant times frequency
senses.definitionCN: 一个量子的能量，与频率成正比，等于普朗克常数乘频率
senses.example: Photon energy rises as the wavelength falls.
senses.exampleCN: 波长变短时，光子能量升高。
senses.why: because each quantum is one frequency worth of energy, the word became a unit of accounting.
senses.whyCN: 因为每个量子恰好是一份与频率对应的能量，这个词成了能量核算的单位。

senses.title: Photon and the photoelectric effect
senses.titleCN: 光子与光电效应：一个光子打出一个电子
senses.definition: the particle of light whose one-to-one collision with an electron explains why weak blue light can eject electrons while strong red light cannot
senses.definitionCN: 与电子一对一碰撞的光粒子，这解释了为何弱蓝光能打出电子而强红光不能
senses.example: The photoelectric effect is explained by one photon striking one electron.
senses.exampleCN: 光电效应可由一个光子撞击一个电子来解释。
senses.why: classical waves spread energy, but the experiment needed lumps, and the photon was the lump.
senses.whyCN: 经典波把能量摊开，而实验需要一份一份的「块」，光子就是那个块。

senses.title: Photon momentum
senses.titleCN: 光子动量：推动表面的那份动量
senses.definition: the momentum carried by a photon despite its lack of mass, which produces radiation pressure
senses.definitionCN: 光子虽无静止质量却携带的动量，由此产生辐射压
senses.example: Photon momentum nudges the sail of a solar spacecraft.
senses.exampleCN: 光子动量轻轻推动太阳帆飞船的帆。
senses.why: if light is a particle it can push, and the word supplies the object that does the pushing.
senses.whyCN: 如果光是粒子，它就能推东西，而这个词提供了实施推动的那个对象。

senses.title: Photon in quantum information
senses.titleCN: 量子信息中的光子：常作量子比特载体
senses.definition: a single photon used to encode a quantum bit, since its polarisation or path can carry a superposition
senses.definitionCN: 用来编码量子比特的单个光子，其偏振或路径可承载叠加态
senses.example: The experiment entangled one photon with another across the table.
senses.exampleCN: 实验把桌上的一个光子与另一个光子纠缠起来。
senses.why: a photon barely interacts with its surroundings, which makes it a good carrier for fragile quantum states.
senses.whyCN: 光子几乎不与周围相互作用，因此适合承载脆弱的量子态。

senses.title: Photon counting in imaging
senses.titleCN: 成像中的光子计数：逐个记录到达的光子
senses.definition: the detection of individual photons to build images at extremely low light levels
senses.definitionCN: 逐个探测单个光子，以在极弱光下成像
senses.example: Photon counting revealed structures too faint for ordinary cameras.
senses.exampleCN: 光子计数显示出普通相机拍不出的微弱结构。
senses.why: a detector able to register single arrivals turns the theory into a measuring method.
senses.whyCN: 能记录单个到达事件的探测器，把理论变成了测量方法。

senses.title: Virtual photon
senses.titleCN: 虚光子：传递相互作用的临时量子
senses.definition: a short-lived quantum of the electromagnetic field that mediates a force between charged particles
senses.definitionCN: 电磁场中短暂存在、在带电粒子间传递作用力的量子
senses.example: Two electrons repel each other by exchanging a virtual photon.
senses.exampleCN: 两个电子通过交换一个虚光子而相互排斥。
senses.why: the same quantum can be off its energy shell while it mediates a force, so the adjective marks the temporary role.
senses.whyCN: 同一个量子在传递力时可以不在能量壳上，因此用形容词标出这种临时角色。

senses.title: Abstract: the smallest packet of anything
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：任何事物的最小一份
senses.definition: an indivisible unit of some quantity, used figuratively for the least amount that can be transferred
senses.definitionCN: 某种量不可再分的一份，比喻上指可以传递的最小量
senses.example: Each photon of gossip carried one unshakeable rumour.
senses.exampleCN: 每一份流言都只带一个无法动摇的传闻。
senses.why: the abstract sense keeps only discreteness: something arrives in units rather than as a smooth flow.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义只保留「分立」：某物以份为单位到达，而非以平滑的流到达。

intro.en: Photon was coined in 1926 by Gilbert N. Lewis from Greek phos, light, with the -on ending of electron. Latin has only the modern borrowing photon.
intro.cn: photon 由吉尔伯特·路易斯于 1926 年以希腊 phos「光」加 electron 的 -on 后缀造出。拉丁语只有近代借形 photon。

items.en: Phos, genitive photos, meant light, and it also supplied words such as photograph and phosphorus.
items.cn: phos（属格 photos）意为「光」，还给出 photograph 与 phosphorus 等词。

items.en: Einstein proposed that light itself comes in discrete packets, though he did not yet call them photons.
items.cn: 爱因斯坦 1905 年提出光本身以分立的一份份出现，但当时尚未称它们为光子。

items.en: Gilbert Lewis coined photon for the light quantum, and the name displaced the older term light quantum.
items.cn: 吉尔伯特·路易斯为光量子造出 photon 一词，这个名字取代了旧的「光量子」。

items.en: The ending -on was copied from electron and later spread to proton, neutron and phonon, marking particles.
items.cn: 后缀 -on 借自 electron，后来扩展到 proton、neutron 与 phonon，用来标记粒子。

items.en: Photon became standard in quantum optics, and its derivatives photonic and photonics name the applied field.
items.cn: photon 在量子光学中成为标准词，其派生词 photonic 与 photonics 命名应用领域。

items.en: Source uncertain (naming credit only): the coinage is generally credited to Lewis in 1926, but the term was used in correspondence earlier in the same year, so the first printed use is disputed.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅命名归属）：这一新造词一般认为是路易斯 1926 年的功劳，但同年稍早的书信中已出现该词，因此最早印刷用例仍有争议。

note.en: Group one holds particle names that share the -on ending; group two holds the quantum terms that are often used loosely in place of photon.
note.cn: 第一组是共享 -on 结尾的粒子名；第二组是常被宽松地用来代替光子的量子术语。

entries.definition: The light negative particle of the atom; the -on ending in photon was copied from this word.
entries.definitionCN: 原子中带负电的轻粒子；photon 的 -on 后缀正是从这个词借来的。

entries.definition: A positive particle in the nucleus; its name uses -on by analogy, not by etymology.
entries.definitionCN: 原子核中带正电的粒子；其 -on 是类推而来，并非同源。

entries.definition: An uncharged nuclear particle, named from neutral plus the same -on ending.
entries.definitionCN: 不带电的核粒子，由 neutral 加相同的 -on 后缀命名。

entries.definition: A quantum of vibrational energy in a crystal, named by analogy with photon using Greek phone, sound.
entries.definitionCN: 晶体中振动能量的量子，仿 photon 以希腊 phone「声」命名。

entries.definition: Any indivisible unit of a physical quantity; a photon is the quantum of the electromagnetic field.
entries.definitionCN: 任何物理量的不可分单位；光子是电磁场的量子。

entries.definition: The older term for the same entity, still seen in translations of early twentieth-century papers.
entries.definitionCN: 同一实体的旧称，仍见于二十世纪早期论文的译本。

entries.definition: A localized group of waves that can represent a particle; it is a description, not a counted unit.
entries.definitionCN: 可代表粒子的局域波群；它是描述方式，不是计数的单位。

entries.definition: An idealised straight line along which light travels; rays describe paths, photons count energy.
entries.definitionCN: 光传播所沿的理想直线；光线描述路径，光子计能量。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Greek root, the real -on family and the real experiments.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的希腊词根、真实的 -on 词族与真实的实验。

normal.en: Photo- means light, and -on marks a particle, so a photon is a particle of light.
normal.cn: photo- 意为「光」，-on 标记粒子，因此 photon 就是光的粒子。

normal.en: The -on ending came from electron and spread to proton, neutron and phonon.
normal.cn: -on 后缀来自 electron，并扩展到 proton、neutron 与 phonon。

normal.en: Energy equals Planck constant times frequency, so bluer light carries more per photon.
normal.cn: 能量等于普朗克常数乘频率，因此越偏蓝的光，每个光子携带越多。

normal.en: The photoelectric effect is one photon in, one electron out.
normal.cn: 光电效应就是一个光子进、一个电子出。

normal.en: Plural is photons, adjective is photonic, field is photonics.
normal.cn: 复数是 photons，形容词是 photonic，领域是 photonics。

abstract.en: Picture a coin small enough that only one can be handed over at a time.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚小到一次只能递出一枚的硬币。

abstract.en: Picture a dark room where each arriving spark is counted separately.
abstract.cn: 想象一间黑屋，每一颗到达的火星都被单独计数。

abstract.en: Picture a message that can only be sent in single letters.
abstract.cn: 想象一条只能一个字母一个字母发送的消息。

examples.en: A photon of green light carries about two electron volts.
examples.cn: 一个绿光光子大约携带两电子伏特的能量。

examples.en: The detector can register a single photon in complete darkness.
examples.cn: 这个探测器能在完全黑暗中记录到单个光子。

examples.en: In the collision, a virtual photon passed between the two charges.
examples.cn: 在碰撞中，一个虚光子在两个电荷之间传递。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「photo（光）+ on（粒子后缀）」——光的最小一份 → 光子

root: 希腊 phos（属格 photos）「光」+ 仿 electron 而来的 -on 后缀；1926 年由吉尔伯特·路易斯造出。拉丁仅有近代借形 photon，无本族拉丁词根。英语 photon。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses begin with the quantum itself, then follow its energy, its role in the photoelectric effect, its momentum, its use in quantum information and imaging, its virtual form, and finally the idea of an indivisible packet.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从量子本身开始，随后依次经过它的能量、它在光电效应中的角色、它的动量、它在量子信息与成像中的用途、它的虚形式，最后落在「不可再分的一份」这一观念上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one tiny packet of light knocking one electron out of a metal plate.
core.cn: 核心意象：一小份光把金属板上的一个电子敲了出来。

branches.en: THE QUANTUM: a single indivisible packet is the trunk of every other sense.
branches.cn: 量子：单个不可再分的一份，是其余义项的树干。

branches.en: ACCOUNTING: energy per packet is fixed by frequency, which makes the photon a unit of exchange.
branches.cn: 核算：每份能量由频率确定，这使光子成为交换单位。

branches.en: HIT AND PUSH: one collision ejects an electron, and momentum presses on a surface.
branches.cn: 撞击与推动：一次碰撞打出一个电子，动量则压在表面上。

branches.en: INFORMATION AND FORCE: single photons carry qubits, build faint images, and mediate interactions as virtual quanta.
branches.cn: 信息与力：单光子承载量子比特、构建微弱图像，并作为虚量子传递相互作用。

branches.en: METAPHOR: anything that arrives only in smallest separate units.
branches.cn: 比喻：任何只以最小分立单位到达的东西。

intro.en: Photon is a modern coinage with a Greek first element and an analogical particle ending, so its family is short but technical.
intro.cn: photon 是近代新造词，第一成分来自希腊语，结尾是类推而来的粒子后缀，因此词族不长，却很技术化。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root: phos is Greek and -on was copied from electron. The only Latin entry is the modern borrowing photon.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁词根：phos 是希腊语，-on 借自 electron。唯一的拉丁条目是近代借形 photon。

items.example: The prefix marks the word as belonging to light.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标出该词属于「光」。

items.example: The suffix later spread to proton and phonon.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀后来扩展到 proton 与 phonon。

items.example: A single photon freed one electron.
items.exampleCN: 一个光子释放出一个电子。

items.example: The beam delivers millions of photons each second.
items.exampleCN: 这束光每秒送出数百万个光子。

items.example: Photonic circuits use light instead of electrons.
items.exampleCN: 光子电路用光而非电子。

items.meaningCN: 研究光粒子的技术领域
items.example: Photonics drives modern optical communication.
items.exampleCN: 光子学推动现代光通信。

items.example: The photoelectron left the metal surface.
items.exampleCN: 光电子离开了金属表面。

items.example: Photon energy depends on frequency.
items.exampleCN: 光子能量取决于频率。

items.example: Photon counting works at very low light.
items.exampleCN: 光子计数在极弱光下仍能工作。

definition_zh: 光；光线；灯；明亮；浅色的；轻的；点燃；照亮
definition_en: the natural agent that makes things visible, or something that produces it; also pale in colour or not heavy
core_image: 一束细光穿过棱镜，在墙上散成彩色条纹
scene: 一束细光穿过棱镜，在墙上散成彩色条纹。A thin beam of light passes through the prism and spreads into colours.
sceneCN: 这里 light 指「使人能看见物体的那种辐射」（第 1 个义项：眼睛可感知的电磁辐射）；句意为一束细光穿过棱镜，在墙上散成彩色条纹。可辨识物件：细光束、棱镜、墙上条纹、暗室。

pos.zh: 光；光线；灯；亮光
明亮的；浅色的；轻的
点燃；照亮

senses.title: Radiation the eye can see
senses.titleCN: 人眼能感知的辐射
senses.definition: the band of electromagnetic radiation that the human eye can detect, making objects visible
senses.definitionCN: 人眼能探测到的电磁辐射波段，使物体可见
senses.example: A thin beam of light passes through the prism and spreads into colours.
senses.exampleCN: 一束细光穿过棱镜，散成彩色条纹。
senses.why: the word is native English and named brightness long before physics described it as a band of radiation.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是英语本族词，在物理学把它描述为一段辐射之前很久，就指「明亮」。

senses.title: A lamp or other source
senses.titleCN: 灯或其他发光源
senses.definition: a device or object that produces illumination, such as a lamp, a candle or a headlight
senses.definitionCN: 产生照明的装置或物体，如灯、蜡烛或车头灯
senses.example: She switched on the light above the kitchen table.
senses.exampleCN: 她打开了厨房桌子上方的灯。
senses.why: the effect and the thing that makes it are named by one word, as often happens with everyday nouns.
senses.whyCN: 效果与造成效果的物件共用一个词，这在日常名词中很常见。

senses.title: Brightness in a place
senses.titleCN: 某个场所的明亮程度
senses.definition: the amount of illumination present in a place, whether natural or artificial
senses.definitionCN: 某处现有的照明量，无论天然或人造
senses.example: The room filled with morning light.
senses.exampleCN: 房间里充满了晨光。
senses.why: the word can name an unbounded mass of brightness, not only a countable lamp.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以指一片无边界的明亮，而不只是可数的灯。

senses.title: Pale in colour
senses.titleCN: 颜色浅的
senses.definition: describing a colour that is pale rather than deep, as in light blue or light grey
senses.definitionCN: 描述颜色浅而非深，如浅蓝或浅灰
senses.example: The walls were painted a light grey.
senses.exampleCN: 墙被刷成浅灰色。
senses.why: a pale surface reflects more light, so the word for brightness came to describe weak colour.
senses.whyCN: 浅色表面反射更多光，因此表示明亮的词转而描述淡的颜色。

senses.title: Not heavy
senses.titleCN: 重量轻的
senses.definition: having little weight, or easy to lift and carry
senses.definitionCN: 重量小，或容易搬动携带
senses.example: The case was light enough to carry in one hand.
senses.exampleCN: 这只箱子轻到一只手就能提。
senses.why: this is a different word from the brightness sense, though the two spellings merged; it goes back to a Germanic root for easy to lift.
senses.whyCN: 这一义与「明亮」义本是不同的词，只是拼写合并了；它上溯到表示「容易提起」的日耳曼词根。

senses.title: To set something burning
senses.titleCN: 点燃某物
senses.definition: to start a fire or make something begin to burn
senses.definitionCN: 生起火，或使某物开始燃烧
senses.example: He lit a candle and set it on the windowsill.
senses.exampleCN: 他点了一支蜡烛，放在窗台上。
senses.why: the verb comes from the brightness word: to light something is to give it a flame.
senses.whyCN: 动词来自「明亮」这个词：给某物点上火，就是让它发光。

senses.title: To illuminate
senses.titleCN: 照亮
senses.definition: to provide light for a place or an object so that it can be seen
senses.definitionCN: 为某处或某物提供光，使其可见
senses.example: A single lamp lit the whole stairwell.
senses.exampleCN: 一盏灯照亮了整个楼梯间。
senses.why: the transitive verb reverses the noun: what was bright is now made bright by someone.
senses.whyCN: 及物动词把名词反过来：原本明亮的东西，现在被人使它变亮。

senses.title: Understanding or insight
senses.titleCN: 理解、启发或线索
senses.definition: information or understanding that makes a difficult matter clear
senses.definitionCN: 使困难之事变得清楚的信息或理解
senses.example: The letters shed light on why the project was abandoned.
senses.exampleCN: 这些信件为项目为何被放弃提供了线索。
senses.why: seeing has always stood for understanding, so light became the standard figure for insight.
senses.whyCN: 「看见」一向代表「理解」，因此 light 成了表示「洞见」的标准比喻。

intro.en: Light has two unrelated histories that share one spelling: the brightness word and the not-heavy word both come from Old English but from different roots. Latin lux is a cognate, not an ancestor.
intro.cn: light 有两个彼此无关、却共用同一拼写的历史：「明亮」与「不重」都来自古英语，但词根不同。拉丁 lux 是同源词，而非祖先。

items.en: Leoht meant light or brightness, from a Germanic root also seen in German Licht. It is related to Latin lux by common ancestry, not by borrowing.
items.cn: leoht 意为「光、明亮」，来自一个也在德语 Licht 中出现的日耳曼词根；它与拉丁 lux 是同源关系，而非借用。

items.en: A second leoht meant not heavy or easy to lift, from a different Germanic root; the two words fell together in Middle English spelling.
items.cn: 另一个 leoht 意为「不重、容易提起」，来自不同的日耳曼词根；两个词在中古英语的拼写上合流。

items.en: The verb light, to set burning or to illuminate, developed from the brightness noun in Old English.
items.cn: 动词 light「点燃、照亮」在古英语中由表示明亮的名词发展而来。

items.en: From the seventeenth century light was studied as rays and waves, and later as one band of the electromagnetic spectrum.
items.cn: 从十七世纪起，光被作为光线与波研究，后来又作为电磁波谱中的一段。

items.en: Shed light on and see the light extend brightness to understanding, a figure already old in English.
items.cn: 「向某事投光」与「看见光」把明亮延伸到理解，这一比喻在英语中已很古老。

items.en: Source uncertain (roots only): the two Germanic roots behind the spellings have no fully settled pre-history, so the reconstructed forms commonly cited for them are reconstructions.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅词根）：这两个日耳曼词根的更早历史都没有完全定论，因此常被引用的重构形式应视为重构。

note.en: Group one holds words that look like light but belong to different families; group two holds the nouns and verbs that overlap its senses.
note.cn: 第一组是形近却属于不同词族的词；第二组是与其义项重叠的名词与动词。

entries.definition: The sudden electrical flash in a storm; it is a different noun and contains no sense of weight.
entries.definitionCN: 风暴中突然的电闪；它是另一个名词，也不含重量之义。

entries.definition: Either to make brighter or to make less heavy, because it was built from both senses of light.
entries.definitionCN: 既可指「使变亮」，也可指「减轻」，因为它由 light 的两个义项共同派生。

entries.definition: In a light manner, either gently or without seriousness; it modifies an action rather than naming light.
entries.definitionCN: 以轻的方式，或轻柔，或不认真；它修饰动作，而非命名光。
