entries.definition: A tower with a lamp for guiding ships; the compound uses the source sense of light.
entries.definitionCN: 为船只导航的灯塔建筑；这一复合词用的是 light 的「光源」义。

entries.definition: A device that gives light, typically a bulb or a flame in a holder; it is the object, not the radiation.
entries.definitionCN: 发出光的装置，通常是带座的灯泡或火焰；它是物件，不是辐射。

entries.definition: The supply or level of light in a place, used in technical and formal writing.
entries.definitionCN: 某处光照的供给或水平，多用于技术与正式写作。

entries.definition: A steady soft light without flame, as from hot metal or a screen.
entries.definitionCN: 无火焰的稳定柔光，如灼热金属或屏幕发出的。

entries.definition: The intensity of light as perceived or measured; it is the property, while light is the thing.
entries.definitionCN: 被感知或测量到的光强；它是属性，而 light 是事物本身。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real native roots, the real verb family and the real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的本族词根、真实的动词词族，以及真实的固定搭配。

normal.en: Light and the German Licht descend from the same Germanic root.
normal.cn: light 与德语 Licht 出自同一个日耳曼词根。

normal.en: The not-heavy light is a separate word that happened to take the same spelling.
normal.cn: 表示「不重」的 light 是另一个词，只是碰巧拼写相同。

normal.en: The verb forms are lit and lighted, with lighting as the participle noun.
normal.cn: 动词形式是 lit 与 lighted，动名词是 lighting。

normal.en: Shed light on means explain, and see the light means come to understand.
normal.cn: 英语里「向某事投光」意为阐明，「看见光」意为明白过来。

normal.en: The Latin cognate is lux, which gives luminous and lucid, but English light is not borrowed from it.
normal.cn: 拉丁同源词是 lux，它给出 luminous 与 lucid，但英语 light 并非借自它。

abstract.en: Picture a match struck in a room where every object was only a guess.
abstract.cn: 想象在黑屋里划着一根火柴，此前每件东西都只是猜测。

abstract.en: Picture a page that was unreadable until one sentence made all of it clear.
abstract.cn: 想象一页原本读不懂的文字，因一句话而全部清楚。

abstract.en: Picture a feather and a stone held in the same hand, one easy and one not.
abstract.cn: 想象同一只手里拿着一根羽毛与一块石头，一个轻松，一个不轻松。

examples.en: The speed of light in a vacuum is about three hundred million metres per second.
examples.cn: 真空中的光速约为每秒三亿米。

examples.en: Please turn off the lights when you leave the room.
examples.cn: 离开房间时请把灯关掉。

examples.en: The new evidence shed light on a case that had been closed for decades.
examples.cn: 新证据为这桩尘封数十年的案子提供了线索。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「light」两义同形：亮的东西 → 光、灯；提起来不费劲 → 轻的；让火亮起来 → 点燃

root: 英语本族词，两个同形异源：表示「光、明亮」的 light 出自古英语 leoht（日耳曼词根，与拉丁 lux 同源而非借用）；表示「不重」的 light 出自另一个古英语 leoht（不同日耳曼词根）。无拉丁同族，故本词条不列拉丁借词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses begin with the radiation, then the lamp, the brightness of a place, pale colour, lightness of weight, fire, illumination and finally understanding.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从辐射开始，随后是灯、某处的明亮、浅色、重量之轻、点火、照明，最后落在理解。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a narrow beam splitting into colour on a wall.
core.cn: 核心意象：一束窄光在墙上分成彩色。

branches.en: RADIATION AND FILL: the same word names both the agent and the amount of it in a place.
branches.cn: 辐射与充盈：同一个词既指作用的媒介，也指某处该媒介的量。

branches.en: SOURCE AND ACTION: a lamp, the act of igniting, and the act of illuminating all circle the same brightness.
branches.cn: 源与动作：灯、点燃的动作、照亮的动作，都围绕同一份明亮。

branches.en: PALE COLOUR: a surface that reflects much light is called light in colour.
branches.cn: 浅色：反射大量光的表面，被称为颜色浅。

branches.en: A SEPARATE WORD: not heavy shares the spelling but not the root.
branches.cn: 另一个词：表示「不重」的词共用拼写，却不共用词根。

branches.en: INSIGHT: seeing becomes understanding, the oldest figure in the word.
branches.cn: 洞见：看见变成理解，这是这个词最古老的比喻。

intro.en: Light is a native English word, so its family is built by ordinary English suffixes and compounds rather than by Latin affixes.
intro.cn: light 是英语本族词，其词族靠普通英语后缀与复合来构建，而非拉丁词缀。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root behind the English word: lux and lucere are cognates, not ancestors, so no Latin borrowing stands behind it; the Latin forms sometimes quoted are only relatives.
latinIntro.cn: 英语这个词背后没有拉丁词根：lux 与 lucere 是同源词，而非祖先，没有拉丁借词为其源头；有时引用的拉丁形式只是亲属词。

items.structure: light (native English noun and adjective, Old English leoht)
items.example: The light filled the room.
items.exampleCN: 光充满了房间。

items.example: The lights went out at midnight.
items.exampleCN: 午夜时灯全灭了。

items.meaning: the arrangement or use of light
items.example: The stage lighting was too harsh.
items.exampleCN: 舞台灯光太刺眼。

items.meaning: less heavy; a device that makes a flame
items.example: This bag is lighter than the other.
items.exampleCN: 这个包比另一个轻。

items.example: She touched the surface lightly.
items.exampleCN: 她轻轻碰了碰表面。

items.example: The lightness of the fabric surprised him.
items.exampleCN: 这布料的轻让他惊讶。

items.meaning: to brighten, or to reduce weight
items.example: The sky lightened before dawn.
items.exampleCN: 天亮前天空变亮了。

items.meaning: a tower with a guiding lamp
items.example: The lighthouse flashed every ten seconds.
items.exampleCN: 灯塔每十秒闪一次。

items.example: The sun is the main light source.
items.exampleCN: 太阳是主要光源。

definition_en: the total amount of energy a star or other object radiates per second, or the quality of giving off light
core_image: 两枚恒星在夜空里看起来一样亮，其中一枚其实远得多、也亮得多
scene: 两枚恒星在夜空里看起来一样亮，天文学家却要比较它们真正放出多少能量。Astronomers compare the luminosity of stars to learn how much energy each one pours out.
sceneCN: 这里 luminosity 指「恒星自身每秒辐射的总能量」（第 1 个义项：天体固有的发光本领，与它看起来多亮不同）；句意为天文学家比较恒星的光度，以了解它们各自放出多少能量。可辨识物件：两颗星、夜空、光度曲线、望远镜。

pos.zh: 光度；发光度；亮度；光辉

senses.title: Intrinsic brightness of a star
senses.titleCN: 恒星自身固有的发光本领
senses.definition: the total energy a star radiates each second, independent of how bright it looks from Earth
senses.definitionCN: 恒星每秒辐射的总能量，与它从地球看起来多亮无关
senses.example: Astronomers compare the luminosity of stars to learn how much energy each one pours out.
senses.exampleCN: 天文学家比较恒星的光度，以了解它们各自放出多少能量。
senses.why: Latin luminositas meant fullness of light, and astronomy narrowed it to the power a star actually emits.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 luminositas 意为「充满光」，天文学把它收窄为恒星实际发出的功率。

senses.title: Total radiant power
senses.titleCN: 每秒辐射的总功率
senses.definition: the rate at which an object emits radiant energy across all wavelengths, measured in watts
senses.definitionCN: 物体在所有波长上发出辐射能量的速率，以瓦特计
senses.example: The luminosity of the sun is about four times ten to the twenty-six watts.
senses.exampleCN: 太阳的光度约为四乘十的二十六次方瓦特。
senses.why: once brightness was given a unit of power, the word became a measurable quantity rather than a look.
senses.whyCN: 一旦亮度有了功率单位，这个词就成了可测量的量，而不只是一种外观。

senses.title: Perceived brightness
senses.titleCN: 人眼所感知的明亮程度
senses.definition: how bright a surface or a light appears to a human observer
senses.definitionCN: 表面或光源在人眼看来有多亮
senses.example: The perceived luminosity of the screen depends on the room lighting.
senses.exampleCN: 屏幕的感知亮度取决于房间的照明。
senses.why: the older sense of shining survives in everyday use, where the observer rather than the physics sets the measure.
senses.whyCN: 「发光」的旧义在日常用法中保留下来，此时衡量者是人眼而非物理量。

senses.title: Brightness of a colour
senses.titleCN: 颜色的明亮度
senses.definition: the lightness of a colour, that is, how much light it appears to reflect
senses.definitionCN: 颜色的明亮程度，即它看起来反射了多少光
senses.example: The luminosity of that yellow makes the whole wall glow.
senses.exampleCN: 那抹黄的明度让整面墙都亮了起来。
senses.why: colour theory borrowed the word for the light-and-dark axis of a hue.
senses.whyCN: 色彩理论借这个词来指色相中「明与暗」的那条轴。

senses.title: Luminosity function
senses.titleCN: 视见函数：人眼对不同波长的敏感度
senses.definition: a standard curve describing how sensitive the average human eye is to each wavelength
senses.definitionCN: 描述普通人眼对各波长敏感程度的标准曲线
senses.example: The luminosity function peaks near green, where the eye is most sensitive.
senses.exampleCN: 视见函数在绿色附近达到峰值，那里人眼最敏感。
senses.why: the word names the function because the curve converts physical power into perceived light.
senses.whyCN: 这个词用来命名该函数，是因为这条曲线把物理功率换算成感知到的光。

senses.title: Luminosity distance
senses.titleCN: 光度距离：由亮度的衰减推算的距离
senses.definition: a cosmological distance inferred from how much a standard candle dims over space
senses.definitionCN: 由标准烛光在空间中变暗多少推算出的宇宙学距离
senses.example: The supernova gave a luminosity distance far beyond the nearby cluster.
senses.exampleCN: 这颗超新星给出的光度距离远在邻近星系团之外。
senses.why: because apparent brightness falls with distance, a measured luminosity becomes a ruler.
senses.whyCN: 由于视亮度随距离衰减，测得的光度就成了尺子。

senses.title: Luminosity in particle physics
senses.titleCN: 粒子物理中的亮度：对撞束的密集程度
senses.definition: a measure of how many particle collisions a collider delivers per unit area per unit time
senses.definitionCN: 衡量对撞机单位面积、单位时间内产生多少次粒子碰撞的量
senses.example: The upgrade doubled the luminosity of the collider.
senses.exampleCN: 这次升级使对撞机的亮度翻倍。
senses.why: the word keeps its core of brightness: a denser beam is a brighter beam in the technical sense.
senses.whyCN: 这个词保留「明亮」的核心：更密的束在技术意义上就是一束「更亮」的束。

senses.title: Abstract: brilliance of a person or style
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：人或风格的光彩
senses.definition: a quality of exceptional mental or artistic radiance that draws admiration
senses.definitionCN: 非凡的心智或艺术光彩，引人赞赏
senses.example: The luminosity of her prose comes from plain words used exactly.
senses.exampleCN: 她文笔的光彩来自把朴素的词用得恰到好处。
senses.why: the physical glow becomes a figure for intellectual or artistic light, a very old habit of language.
senses.whyCN: 物理的辉光变成了心智或艺术之光的比喻，这是语言很古老的习惯。

intro.en: Luminosity comes from Late Latin luminositas, fullness of light, from luminosus, full of light, from lumen, light. English took it through French in the sixteenth century.
intro.cn: luminosity 来自晚期拉丁 luminositas「充满光」，其形容词 luminosus「充满光的」，词根 lumen「光」。英语于十六世纪经法语引入。

items.en: Lumen meant light, especially the light of a lamp or of the eye; its genitive is luminis, which is why the family shows lumin-.
items.cn: lumen 意为「光」，尤指灯或眼睛的光；其属格为 luminis，因此词族中出现 lumin- 这一形式。

items.en: Luminosus meant full of light or bright, built with the suffix -osus, which marks abundance.
items.cn: luminosus 意为「充满光的、明亮的」，由表示「充满」的后缀 -osus 构成。

items.en: The abstract noun luminositas named the quality of being full of light, and English borrowed it as luminosity.
items.cn: 抽象名词 luminositas 指「充满光的性质」，英语借入作 luminosity。

items.en: English used luminosity first for the quality of shining, then for the measurable output of a source.
items.cn: 英语最初用 luminosity 指「发光的性质」，后来指光源可测量的输出。

items.en: Modern astronomy fixed luminosity as the intrinsic power of a star, distinct from apparent magnitude.
items.cn: 现代天文学把 luminosity 固定为恒星固有的功率，与视星等区分。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper root only): the pre-Latin origin of lumen is unsettled, and the common link drawn to a Indo-European light root is a reconstruction rather than a proven chain.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅更深词根）：lumen 在拉丁语之前的来源没有定论，把它与某个印欧「光」词根相连属重构，而非已证实的链条。

note.en: Group one holds the light-measuring nouns that are constantly interchanged; group two holds the everyday words for brightness and fame.
note.cn: 第一组是常被互换的光度量名词；第二组是表示明亮与光彩的日常词。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning giving off light, as in luminous paint; it describes, while luminosity measures.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，意为「发光的」，如发光涂料；它作描述，而 luminosity 作计量。

entries.definition: The intensity of light leaving a surface per unit area, a photometric quantity with its own unit.
entries.definitionCN: 单位面积表面射出的光强，是有自身单位的光度量。

entries.definition: Light produced without heat, as by a firefly or a phosphor; it names the process, not the power.
entries.definitionCN: 不伴热产生的光，如萤火虫或荧光粉；它指过程，而非功率。

entries.definition: The amount of light falling on a surface, measured in lux; it is incident rather than emitted.
entries.definitionCN: 落在表面上的光量，以勒克斯计；它是入射光，而非射出光。

entries.definition: How bright something looks or is; it can mean either emitted power or perceived glare.
entries.definitionCN: 某物看起来或实际有多亮；既可指发出的功率，也可指感知到的刺眼程度。

entries.definition: A logarithmic scale of apparent brightness; it is not the same as luminosity, which is intrinsic.
entries.definitionCN: 视亮度的对数标度；与表示固有本领的 luminosity 并不等同。

entries.definition: Bright glowing light, often used with warmth or beauty, as in the radiance of a face.
entries.definitionCN: 明亮的光辉，常带温暖或美的意味，如脸上的光彩。

entries.definition: Power per unit area or per unit solid angle; it is a distribution, while luminosity is a total.
entries.definitionCN: 单位面积或单位立体角的功率；它是分布量，而 luminosity 是总量。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin root, the real astronomy distinction and the real photometric family.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁词根、真实的天文学区分，以及真实的光度量词族。

normal.en: lumen means light and -osity means fullness, so luminosity is fullness of light.
normal.cn: lumen 意为「光」，-osity 意为「充满」，因此 luminosity 就是「充满光」。

normal.en: Astronomy separates luminosity from apparent magnitude: one is intrinsic, the other is seen.
normal.cn: 天文学把光度与视星等分开：前者固有，后者是被看见的。

normal.en: The family runs luminous, luminously, luminance, luminescence.
normal.cn: 词族包括 luminous、luminously、luminance、luminescence。

normal.en: Solar luminosity is a standard unit in astronomy.
normal.cn: 太阳光度是天文学中的标准单位。

normal.en: The plural is luminosities, and the adjective keeps the same root.
normal.cn: 复数是 luminosities，形容词沿用同一词根。

abstract.en: Picture two lamps that look equal from across a field, though one is far larger.
abstract.cn: 想象两盏灯从田野对面看来一样亮，其中一盏其实大得多。

abstract.en: Picture a page whose plain sentences somehow light the room.
abstract.cn: 想象一页文字，句子朴素，却不知怎地把屋子照亮了。

abstract.en: Picture a star that keeps pouring out energy long after no one is watching.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗星在无人注视之后仍不断倾泻能量。

examples.en: The star has a luminosity a thousand times that of the sun.
examples.cn: 这颗恒星的光度是太阳的一千倍。

examples.en: Luminosity distance and redshift together give the expansion rate.
examples.cn: 光度距离与红移合起来给出膨胀速率。

examples.en: The collider reached a luminosity high enough to see rare decays.
examples.cn: 对撞机的亮度高到足以观测稀有衰变。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「lumin（光）+ osity（充满）」——满满地发光 → 光度、发光度

root: 拉丁 lumen（属格 luminis）「光」→ luminosus「充满光的」→ 晚期拉丁 luminositas「充满光」；lumen 的更深来源不确定。英语 luminosity。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses begin with a star own power, then the total wattage, then what the eye perceives, the brightness of a colour, a standard sensitivity curve, a cosmological ruler, collider brightness and finally personal brilliance.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从恒星自身的本领开始，接着是总功率、人眼所感、颜色明度、标准敏感曲线、宇宙学尺子、对撞亮度，最后落在个人的光彩。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two stars equal to the eye, one of them pouring out far more energy.
core.cn: 核心意象：两颗星在眼中一样亮，其中一颗却放出多得多的能量。

branches.en: INTRINSIC POWER: the star own output, not the light that happens to reach an eye.
branches.cn: 固有功率：恒星自身的输出，而非恰好到达眼睛的光。

branches.en: WHAT IS SEEN: perceived brightness and colour lightness belong to the observer.
branches.cn: 所见：感知亮度与颜色明度属于观察者一侧。

branches.en: STANDARDS: a sensitivity curve and a distance ruler turn brightness into measurement.
branches.cn: 标准：敏感曲线与距离尺子把亮度变成测量。

branches.en: TECHNICAL ECHO: collider luminosity keeps only the idea of a denser, brighter beam.
branches.cn: 技术回声：对撞亮度只保留「更密即更亮」的观念。

branches.en: METAPHOR: mental or artistic light that draws admiration.
branches.cn: 比喻：引人赞赏的心智或艺术之光。

intro.en: Luminosity is an abstract noun from a Latin adjective, and the same root supplies the whole photometric vocabulary.
intro.cn: luminosity 是由拉丁形容词派生的抽象名词，同一词根提供了一整套光度学词汇。

latinIntro.en: Latin lumen, genitive luminis, gives luminosus and then luminositas; English adds -ity only in form, since the abstract noun already existed in Late Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 lumen（属格 luminis）给出 luminosus，再给出 luminositas；英语在形式上加了 -ity，而这个抽象名词在晚期拉丁中已经存在。

items.example: Lumen is the root of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: lumen 是整个词族的根。

items.example: The suffix turns light into full of light.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把「光」变成「充满光的」。

items.example: The dial is luminous at night.
items.exampleCN: 表盘在夜里发光。

items.example: The suffix makes an abstract noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成抽象名词。

items.meaning: the state of being full of light
items.example: The star luminosity is enormous.
items.exampleCN: 这颗恒星的光度极大。

items.example: The paint dried luminously white.
items.exampleCN: 这漆干后白得发亮。

items.meaning: light per unit area from a surface
items.meaningCN: 表面单位面积射出的光
items.example: The screen luminance was measured in nits.
items.exampleCN: 屏幕亮度以尼特计。

items.example: The firefly luminescence is chemical.
items.exampleCN: 萤火虫的发光是化学的。

items.example: A lamp illuminated the entrance.
items.exampleCN: 一盏灯照亮了入口。

latinEntries.meaning: light; the light of a lamp or eye

latinEntries.structure: luminosus, luminosa, luminosum (adj., first and second declension)
luminositas, luminositatis (f., third declension; Late Latin)
